senses.def: used before a singular countable noun when it is not a specific one or has not been mentioned before
examples: I saw a fox in the backyard this morning.
She works as a nurse at a hospital downtown.

senses.def: used to mean 'each' or 'per' with amounts, prices and frequencies
examples: The gym costs forty dollars a month.
I drink coffee three times a day.

note: Use "an" before a vowel sound: an hour, an idea, but a university, a one-way street.

senses.def: to leave someone or something you are responsible for, with no intention of returning
examples: The puppy had been abandoned on the side of the road.
The crew abandoned the sinking ship.

senses.def: to stop doing or supporting something, especially before it is finished
examples: They abandoned the project after funding ran out.
Never abandon hope.

senses.def: the skill, power or opportunity to do something
examples: She has the ability to stay calm under pressure.
The disease affects a patient's ability to walk.

collocations: to the best of your ability

senses.def: having the skill, chance or power to do something; used in "be able to"
examples: Will you be able to come to the meeting tomorrow?
After the surgery, he was able to walk again.

senses.def: clever or good at doing something
examples: She is one of the most able students in her class.

note: "Can" has no future or perfect forms, so use "be able to": I will be able to, I have been able to.

senses.def: to officially end a law, system or institution
examples: Many countries have abolished the death penalty.
The new government promised to abolish the tax on books.

senses.def: a medical procedure that deliberately ends a pregnancy at an early stage
examples: The state passed a law restricting access to abortion.
Abortion remains one of the most divisive issues in American politics.

note: A natural loss of a pregnancy is a "miscarriage" (düşük), not an abortion. "Abort" also means to stop a plan or process.

senses.def: on the subject of or connected with someone or something
examples: We talked about our plans for the summer.
What's the book about?

senses.def: a little more or less than a number or time
examples: The flight takes about three hours.
There were about fifty people at the party.

senses.def: used in "be about to" to say something will happen very soon
examples: I was just about to call you when you walked in.

senses.def: in or to a higher position than something
examples: There's a small shelf above the sink.
The plane flew high above the clouds.

senses.def: more than a particular number, amount or level
examples: Temperatures rose above 100 degrees last week.
The tour is for children aged ten and above.

senses.def: at or to a higher place, or earlier in a piece of writing
examples: The neighbors in the apartment above are very noisy.
Please contact us at the address given above.

note: "Above all" means "most importantly". "Above" is for position/level; "over" can also mean covering or moving across.

senses.def: in or to a foreign country
examples: She spent a year studying abroad in Spain.
More Americans are traveling abroad than ever before.

note: An adverb, so no preposition: "go abroad", not "go to abroad". But you can say "from abroad".

senses.def: the fact of being away from a place where you are expected, or the period you are away
examples: Her frequent absences from work worried her manager.
He returned to the team after a two-month absence.

senses.def: the fact that something does not exist or is missing
examples: In the absence of evidence, the police had to release him.
The absence of clear rules caused confusion.

senses.def: not present in a place where you are expected to be, for example because of illness
examples: Three students were absent from class today with the flu.
He was absent from the meeting without explanation.

senses.def: not existing in a place or situation where you would expect it
examples: Any sense of humor was completely absent from his speech.

senses.def: total and complete; used to emphasize something
examples: The trip was an absolute disaster from start to finish.
I have absolute confidence in her judgment.

senses.def: having unlimited power, or not depending on or compared with anything else
examples: The king held absolute power over the country.
Measured in absolute terms, wages have risen.

senses.def: completely or totally; used to emphasize what you are saying
examples: The view from the top was absolutely amazing.
I have absolutely no idea where my keys are.

senses.def: used as a strong way of saying yes or agreeing
examples: "Can I bring a friend?" "Absolutely!"
"Absolutely not," she said when he asked to borrow her car.

note: Use with extreme adjectives (absolutely freezing, absolutely delicious), not usually with gradable ones (not "absolutely cold").

senses.def: to take in a liquid, gas, heat or other substance
examples: The towel absorbed most of the spilled milk.
Dark clothes absorb more heat from the sun.

senses.def: to take in and understand information fully
examples: There was too much information to absorb in one lecture.

senses.def: to hold someone's attention completely
examples: He was so absorbed in his game that he didn't hear me.

senses.def: based on general ideas rather than real, physical things or specific situations
examples: Justice and freedom are abstract concepts.
The discussion was too abstract for most of the students.

senses.def: (of art) using shapes and colors rather than showing people or things realistically
examples: The museum has a large collection of abstract paintings.

senses.def: a short summary of a research article or academic paper
examples: Read the abstract first to see if the study is relevant.

note: Opposite: concrete (somut).

senses.def: completely unreasonable or silly, and not making sense
examples: It's absurd to charge ten dollars for a bottle of water.
The idea sounded absurd at first, but it worked.

senses.def: a very large amount of something, more than is needed
examples: The region has an abundance of fresh water.
Wild berries grow in abundance along the trail.

note: Formal. "In abundance" comes after the noun: "Food was available in abundance."

senses.def: the wrong or harmful use of something, such as power or drugs
examples: The scandal involved a clear abuse of power.
He spent years struggling with drug abuse.

senses.def: cruel or violent treatment of a person or animal
examples: The charity supports victims of child abuse.
She reported the abuse to the police.

senses.def: to use something wrongly or too much, in a way that causes harm
examples: The officer was accused of abusing his authority.
Some people abuse prescription painkillers.

senses.def: to treat a person or animal cruelly or violently
examples: The dog had been abused by its previous owner.

note: Pronunciation differs: noun /əˈbjuːs/ (s sound), verb /əˈbjuːz/ (z sound).

senses.def: connected with education, especially study and research at schools and universities
examples: The new academic year starts in late August.
Her academic performance improved after she joined the study group.

senses.def: a person who teaches or does research at a university or college
examples: The report was written by a group of leading academics.

senses.def: not relevant to a real situation; only of theoretical interest
examples: The question is purely academic now that the decision has been made.

senses.def: a school or college that gives training in a special skill or subject
examples: He graduated from the police academy last spring.
She trained at a famous ballet academy in New York.

senses.def: an official organization of respected scholars, scientists or artists
examples: She was elected to the National Academy of Sciences.

senses.def: to happen or make something happen faster or earlier
examples: The government wants to accelerate the switch to clean energy.
Climate change has accelerated the melting of glaciers.

senses.def: (of a vehicle or driver) to go faster
examples: The car accelerated as it merged onto the highway.

note: Opposite: decelerate / slow down. The car pedal is the "accelerator" or informally the "gas pedal".

senses.def: a way of pronouncing a language that shows where someone comes from
examples: She speaks English with a slight French accent.
I could tell from his accent that he grew up in Texas.

senses.def: special emphasis given to a syllable, or a particular focus on something
examples: In "hotel", the accent is on the second syllable.
The menu puts the accent on local ingredients.

senses.def: to take something that is offered or say yes to an offer or invitation
examples: She accepted the job offer without hesitation.
Do you accept credit cards?

senses.def: to agree that something is true or to deal with a difficult situation without trying to change it
examples: He finally accepted that the relationship was over.
You have to accept some risk when you invest.

senses.def: to allow someone to join a group, school or organization
examples: She was accepted to three different colleges.

note: Don't confuse with "except" (hariç). Turkish "kabul etmek" also translates as "admit" when confessing something.

senses.def: agreed or approved of by most people in a society
examples: Smoking indoors is no longer socially acceptable.
Violence is never an acceptable way to solve problems.

senses.def: good enough, but not excellent
examples: The hotel was clean and the price was acceptable.

senses.def: the act of saying yes to an offer, invitation or gift
examples: She gave an emotional acceptance speech at the awards ceremony.
Please confirm your acceptance of the offer by Friday.

senses.def: the fact of being approved of or welcomed, or of agreeing that something difficult is true
examples: The theory gained wide acceptance among scientists.
Grief eventually gave way to acceptance.

senses.def: the right, opportunity or way to use, reach or enter something
examples: Many rural areas still lack access to fast internet.
Students have free access to the library's databases.

senses.def: to open or use a computer file, system or information
examples: You can access your account from any device.
Hackers accessed the personal data of thousands of customers.

note: Noun takes "to": access to clean water. The verb takes no preposition: access the files (not "access to the files").

senses.def: possible to reach, enter or use, including for people with disabilities
examples: The island is only accessible by boat.
All the station's entrances are wheelchair accessible.

senses.def: easy to understand or enjoy
examples: The book makes complex science accessible to ordinary readers.

senses.def: an unexpected event, often involving a vehicle, that causes damage or injury
examples: He broke his leg in a car accident last year.
Most accidents happen close to home.

senses.def: something that happens by chance, without being planned
examples: I found the old photos by accident while cleaning the attic.
It was no accident that she got the job.

senses.def: by chance or by mistake, without intending to
examples: I accidentally deleted the whole folder.
She accidentally locked herself out of the house.

note: Opposite: deliberately / on purpose. "Accidentally on purpose" is a joke meaning secretly on purpose.

senses.def: to provide a place to stay or have enough space for a number of people or things
examples: The hotel can accommodate up to 300 guests.
The new stadium accommodates 60,000 fans.

senses.def: to consider and try to meet someone's needs or wishes
examples: The airline did its best to accommodate passengers with special needs.
We can adjust the schedule to accommodate your request.

note: Common spelling mistake: double c and double m — accommodate.

senses.def: a place to stay, live or work in; in American English usually "accommodations"
examples: The price includes flights and hotel accommodations.
Finding cheap accommodation near campus is difficult.

senses.def: a change or arrangement that helps someone, especially a person with a disability
examples: Students with dyslexia may receive accommodations such as extra time on tests.

note: In American English, the plural "accommodations" is usual for lodging; British English uses the uncountable "accommodation".

senses.def: to go somewhere with someone
examples: Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult.
She accompanied her father to his doctor's appointment.

senses.def: to happen or exist together with something else
examples: The fever was accompanied by a bad headache.
Each photo is accompanied by a short description.

senses.def: to play music while someone sings or plays the main part
examples: She sang while her brother accompanied her on the piano.

note: No preposition after it: "accompany someone", not "accompany with someone".

senses.def: to succeed in doing or finishing something, especially after effort
examples: We accomplished a lot in our first week.
The team accomplished its goal of raising $10,000.

senses.def: an impressive thing that someone achieves after a lot of work
examples: Finishing the marathon was a huge accomplishment for her.
The report lists the company's main accomplishments this year.

senses.def: the act of successfully completing something
examples: The accomplishment of the mission took three years.

senses.tr: (in accordance with) uyarınca, -e uygun olarak, -e göre
senses.def: used in "in accordance with" to mean following a rule, law or someone's wishes
examples: The funds were spent in accordance with the law.
His body was cremated in accordance with his wishes.

note: Formal; almost always used in the phrase "in accordance with".

senses.def: as stated or reported by someone or something
examples: According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow.
According to police, the driver was not injured.

senses.def: following or depending on a plan, rule or system
examples: Everything went according to plan.
Students are grouped according to their ability.

note: Don't say "according to me" for your own opinion; say "in my opinion" or "I think".

senses.tr: buna göre, ona göre, uygun şekilde
senses.def: in a way that suits what has been said or what is happening
examples: The weather can change quickly, so dress accordingly.
We'll find out how many people are coming and plan accordingly.

senses.def: for that reason; as a result
examples: The company lost its biggest client. Accordingly, it had to cut jobs.

senses.def: an arrangement with a bank or online service to keep money or use the service
examples: I opened a savings account at my local bank.
You need to create an account to leave a comment.

senses.def: a spoken or written description of an event
examples: Witnesses gave different accounts of the accident.
By all accounts, the concert was a success.

senses.def: used in "account for" to mean explain something or form a particular amount of a total
examples: How do you account for the missing money?
Women account for 60% of the workforce.

note: "Take something into account" = hesaba katmak. "On account of" = because of (formal).

senses.def: the fact of being responsible for your decisions and actions and having to explain them
examples: Voters are demanding greater accountability from elected officials.
There was no accountability for the mistakes that were made.

senses.def: responsible for your decisions or actions and expected to explain them
examples: Police officers must be held accountable for their actions.
Managers are accountable to the board of directors.

note: Accountable to a person or group; accountable for an action or result.

senses.def: a person whose job is to keep or check financial records
examples: Our accountant helps us file our taxes every April.
She works as an accountant for a large firm.

note: In the US, a qualified accountant is a CPA (certified public accountant).

senses.def: to gradually collect or get more and more of something over time
examples: He accumulated a huge collection of vinyl records.
Over the years, she accumulated a lot of debt.

senses.def: to gradually increase in amount
examples: Dust had accumulated on the old bookshelves.
Snow accumulated quickly overnight.

senses.def: the gradual increase of something, or an amount that has built up over time
examples: The accumulation of fat in the arteries can lead to heart disease.
There was a large accumulation of snow on the roof.

senses.def: the quality of being exact and correct, or the ability to do something without mistakes
examples: Journalists must check the accuracy of their sources.
The new test detects the disease with 95% accuracy.

senses.def: correct and exact in every detail
examples: The weather forecast was surprisingly accurate.
We need an accurate count of how many people are coming.

senses.def: in a way that is correct and exact
examples: It's hard to accurately predict the stock market.
The movie accurately portrays life in the 1950s.

senses.def: a statement saying that someone has done something wrong or illegal
examples: He denied all accusations of cheating.
The senator faces accusations of corruption.

senses.def: to say that someone has done something wrong or illegal
examples: She accused her coworker of stealing her ideas.
He was accused of murder but found not guilty.

note: Pattern: accuse someone OF doing something (not "for"). Compare: blame someone FOR something.

senses.def: the person or people on trial for a crime
examples: The accused was led into the courtroom in handcuffs.
The jury found the accused not guilty.

note: Always used with "the": "the accused" can be singular or plural, with no -s.

senses.def: to succeed in reaching a goal or standard, especially after a lot of effort
examples: She worked hard to achieve her dream of becoming a doctor.
The country achieved independence in 1960.

senses.def: something you have done successfully, especially through effort and skill
examples: Winning the championship was the greatest achievement of his career.
The report celebrates the achievements of local volunteers.

senses.def: the act or process of reaching a goal or standard
examples: The program aims to raise academic achievement in poor neighborhoods.

senses.def: a chemical substance, usually a liquid, with a pH below seven that can burn or damage things
examples: Stomach acid helps break down the food we eat.
Wear gloves when handling the acid in the lab.

senses.def: containing acid or having its qualities; also, sour in taste
examples: Acid rain has damaged forests across the region.
Blueberries grow best in acid soil.

note: "The acid test" means a decisive test that shows whether something is really good or true.

senses.def: to accept or admit that something is true or exists
examples: The company acknowledged that mistakes had been made.
He refused to acknowledge the problem.

senses.def: to tell someone that you have received their letter, message or gift
examples: Please acknowledge receipt of this email.

senses.tr: selamlamak, fark ettiğini göstermek; takdir etmek
senses.def: to show that you have noticed someone, or to publicly recognize their work
examples: She walked past without even acknowledging me.
The author acknowledges the help of her research team.

note: American spelling: acknowledgment (British often: acknowledgement).

senses.def: to gain knowledge, a skill or a quality through your own effort or experience
examples: Children acquire language remarkably quickly.
She acquired a reputation for being tough but fair.

senses.def: to buy or get something, especially a company or property
examples: The tech giant acquired the startup for $2 billion.
The museum recently acquired a rare painting.

note: More formal than "get". "An acquired taste" is something you learn to like slowly.

senses.def: the process of getting something, especially knowledge or a skill
examples: Her research focuses on second language acquisition.
The acquisition of new skills is essential in today's job market.

senses.tr: satın alma, devralma; yeni edinilen şey
senses.def: the act of buying a company or property, or something that has been bought
examples: The merger was the largest acquisition in the company's history.
The painting is the gallery's newest acquisition.

senses.def: a unit for measuring land, equal to about 4,050 square meters
examples: They bought a farm with 200 acres of land.
The fire destroyed thousands of acres of forest.

note: One acre is about 0.4 hectares, roughly four Turkish dönüm.

senses.def: from one side of something to the other
examples: We walked across the bridge to the old town.
She swam across the lake in under an hour.

senses.def: on the other side of something
examples: There's a coffee shop across the street from my office.

senses.def: in every part of a place or group
examples: The storm caused power outages across the state.
The policy is popular across all age groups.

senses.def: from one side to the other, or measuring from one side to the other
examples: The river is too wide to swim across.
The crater is about two miles across.

note: "Come across" = rastlamak, bulmak. "Across the board" = affecting everyone or everything.

senses.def: a particular thing that someone does
examples: Holding the door for her was a simple act of kindness.
The bombing was condemned as an act of terrorism.

senses.def: a law passed by a government; one main part of a play; or a pretended way of behaving
examples: Congress passed the Clean Air Act in 1970.
Don't believe her tears; it's all an act.

senses.def: to do something to deal with a situation, or to behave in a particular way
examples: We need to act quickly before the problem gets worse.
He's been acting strangely all week.

senses.def: to perform a role in a play, movie or TV show
examples: She has been acting since she was a child.

note: "Act as" = to do the job of: "She acted as interpreter." "Get your act together" (informal) = organize yourself.

senses.def: the process of doing something to achieve a goal or deal with a problem
examples: The government must take action to reduce pollution.
It's time to stop talking and put the plan into action.

senses.def: a thing that someone does
examples: You must take responsibility for your actions.
Her quick action saved the child's life.

senses.def: exciting events, especially in movies, or the main activity in a place
examples: I love action movies with lots of car chases.
Times Square is where all the action is on New Year's Eve.

note: Say "take action", not "make action".

senses.def: to make a device, system or process start working
examples: You need to activate your new credit card before using it.
Smoke from the toaster activated the fire alarm.

senses.def: the act of making a device, system or chemical process start working
examples: Account activation can take up to 24 hours.
The study measured brain activation during memory tasks.

senses.def: always busy doing things, especially physical activities
examples: My grandmother is still very active at 85.
Staying active helps you sleep better.

senses.def: taking part in something and doing things to make it happen
examples: She has been an active member of the club for years.
Parents should take an active role in their children's education.

senses.def: operating or working now
examples: Scientists are monitoring the active volcano closely.

senses.def: a person who works to bring about political or social change
examples: Climate activists gathered outside city hall.
She has been a civil rights activist for over thirty years.

senses.def: something you do for interest, pleasure or to achieve a goal
examples: The camp offers activities like hiking, swimming and canoeing.
Reading is my favorite weekend activity.

senses.def: a situation in which a lot is happening or people are busy doing things
examples: There was a lot of activity in the kitchen before dinner.
Police noticed suspicious activity near the bank.

senses.def: a person who performs in plays, movies or TV shows
examples: He became a famous actor after starring in a hit TV series.
Several actors auditioned for the role.

senses.def: a person, group or country that takes part in an event or process
examples: Banks were key actors in the financial crisis.

note: Today "actor" is often used for both men and women.

senses.def: a woman who performs in plays, movies or TV shows
examples: She won an award for best actress last year.
The young actress landed her first major role at sixteen.

note: Many women in the profession now prefer to be called "actor".

senses.def: real or existing in fact, often in contrast to what was expected or believed
examples: The actual cost of the project was twice the estimate.
Is that an actual photo or was it edited?

note: False friend: "actual" does NOT mean "current" (güncel). Turkish "aktüel" = current / up-to-date.

senses.def: used to say what is really true, often when it is surprising or different
examples: He looks young, but he's actually over fifty.
I didn't expect to like the movie, but I actually enjoyed it.

senses.tr: aslında, açıkçası (konuşmada düzeltme veya kibar itiraz)
senses.def: used in speech to correct someone politely, add information or change the subject
examples: "You're from Chicago, right?" "Actually, I'm from Detroit."
Actually, could I ask you a quick favor?

note: False friend: it does not mean "currently" (şu anda). Use "currently" or "at the moment" for that.

senses.def: (of a problem or bad situation) very serious or severe
examples: There is an acute shortage of nurses in rural hospitals.
She felt an acute sense of embarrassment.

senses.def: (of an illness) coming quickly and being severe, but often for a short time
examples: He was rushed to the hospital with acute appendicitis.

senses.def: (of the senses or the mind) very sharp and sensitive
examples: Dogs have an acute sense of smell.

note: Medical opposite: chronic (long-lasting). An "acute angle" is less than 90 degrees (dar açı).

senses.def: an advertisement: a notice, picture or video that promotes a product, job or service
examples: I saw an ad for cheap flights to Mexico.
The video was interrupted by three ads in a row.

note: Informal short form of "advertisement". British English also uses "advert".

senses.def: to change your behavior or ideas to deal with a new situation
examples: It took the kids a few months to adapt to their new school.
Businesses must adapt quickly to changing markets.

senses.def: to change something so that it suits a new purpose, or to make a book into a movie or play
examples: The recipe can be adapted for people who don't eat meat.
The novel was adapted for television last year.

note: Don't confuse with "adopt" (to take as your own: evlat edinmek, benimsemek).

senses.def: the process of changing to suit a new situation or environment
examples: The animals show remarkable adaptation to desert life.
Cities are planning for adaptation to rising sea levels.

senses.def: a movie, play or TV show that is based on a book or another work
examples: The film is a faithful adaptation of the novel.

senses.def: to put something together with something else to increase the size, number or amount
examples: Add a pinch of salt to the boiling water.
We're adding a new bedroom to the house.

senses.def: to put numbers together to find the total
examples: If you add 7 and 5, you get 12.
Add up all your expenses for the month.

senses.def: to say something more
examples: "And don't be late," she added as I left.

note: "It doesn't add up" (informal) = it doesn't make sense.

senses.def: the condition of being unable to stop using or doing something, especially something harmful
examples: He finally sought help for his drug addiction.
Experts warn about smartphone addiction among teenagers.

senses.def: a thing or person that is added to something else
examples: The new library is a great addition to the neighborhood.
They're expecting a new addition to the family in May.

senses.def: the act of adding something, or the process of adding numbers together
examples: The kids are learning addition and subtraction.
The addition of lemon juice gives the sauce a fresh taste.

note: "In addition" (= also) starts a sentence; "in addition to" (= besides) is followed by a noun or -ing form.

senses.def: more than what was first mentioned or is usual
examples: There's an additional charge for checked bags.
The project will require additional funding.

senses.def: used to introduce an extra fact or point
examples: The hotel is close to the beach. Additionally, it offers free parking.
Additionally, all employees will receive a small bonus.

note: Fairly formal; in conversation, "also" or "plus" is more natural.

senses.def: details of where someone lives or works, or where email or a website can be found
examples: Please write your name and address on the form.
What's your email address?

senses.def: to think about a problem and start dealing with it
examples: The city needs to address the shortage of affordable housing.
The report fails to address the main issue.

senses.def: to speak to a person or group, especially formally
examples: The president addressed the nation on television last night.

senses.def: a formal speech given to an audience
examples: She gave the commencement address at the university.

note: In American English the noun is often stressed /ˈædres/. "Address" an issue is very common in news and work English.

senses.def: enough in amount or good enough in quality for a particular need
examples: Many families don't have adequate health insurance.
Make sure you get adequate sleep before the exam.

senses.def: acceptable but not very good
examples: The food was adequate, but nothing special.

senses.def: in a way that is enough or good enough for a particular need
examples: Many schools are not adequately funded.
Make sure the room is adequately ventilated while painting.

senses.def: to follow a rule, law or belief exactly
examples: All staff must adhere to the safety guidelines.
The company strictly adheres to environmental regulations.

senses.def: to stick firmly to a surface
examples: The label won't adhere to a wet surface.

note: Formal. Always followed by "to".

senses.def: next to or very near something else
examples: The hotel is adjacent to the convention center.
We booked two adjacent rooms on the fifth floor.

note: Formal; in everyday speech "next to" is more common.

senses.def: to change something slightly to make it fit, work better or suit new conditions
examples: You can adjust the height of the chair with this lever.
Prices are adjusted for inflation every year.

senses.def: to get used to a new situation by changing your behavior or ideas
examples: It took me weeks to adjust to the time difference.
Kids usually adjust quickly to a new school.

senses.def: a small change made to something to correct or improve it
examples: The mechanic made a few adjustments to the brakes.
We'll need to make some adjustments to the budget.

senses.def: the process of getting used to a new situation
examples: Moving to a new country requires a big adjustment.

senses.def: to manage and organize the work of a company, organization or country
examples: The fund is administered by a small team of volunteers.
Local governments administer most public schools.

senses.def: to give someone medicine or treatment, or to organize a test
examples: The nurse administered the vaccine in his left arm.
The exam is administered twice a year.

senses.def: to manage or organize the work of an organization or system
examples: She was hired to administrate the new scholarship program.
The website is administrated by a small IT team.

note: Less common than "administer", which most careful writers prefer.

senses.def: the activities involved in planning, organizing and running a business or institution
examples: She has a degree in business administration.
Too much money is spent on administration and not enough on teaching.

senses.def: the government of a country, especially the US president and officials during one period
examples: The new administration promised to lower taxes.

senses.def: the act of giving medicine or treatment to someone
examples: The administration of the drug must be carefully monitored.

note: In US news, "the Administration" often means the president's government.

senses.def: connected with organizing and managing the work of a business or institution
examples: She works as an administrative assistant at a law firm.
The new system reduced administrative costs by 20%.

note: "Administrative leave" = being sent home from work, usually with pay, during an investigation.

senses.def: a person whose job is to manage and organize the affairs of a business or institution
examples: Hospital administrators are struggling to cut costs.
School administrators met with parents to discuss safety.

senses.def: a person who manages a computer system or network
examples: Contact your system administrator to reset your password.

senses.tr: hayran olmak, takdir etmek, saygı duymak
senses.def: to respect someone for what they have done or for their qualities
examples: I really admire her courage and honesty.
He was widely admired for his work with refugees.

senses.def: to look at something with pleasure because it is beautiful or impressive
examples: We stopped to admire the view from the top of the hill.

senses.def: the act of allowing someone to enter a school, hospital or organization
examples: She applied for admission to several law schools.
Hospital admissions rose sharply during the flu season.

senses.def: the money you pay to enter a place, or the right to enter
examples: Admission to the museum is free on Sundays.

senses.def: a statement admitting that something bad is true
examples: His resignation was seen as an admission of guilt.

senses.def: to agree, often unwillingly, that something is true or that you did something wrong
examples: I have to admit that the movie was better than I expected.
He finally admitted stealing the money.

senses.def: to allow someone to enter a place, or to accept someone into a hospital or school
examples: She was admitted to the hospital with chest pains.
Only ticket holders will be admitted.

note: Admit (to) doing something, not "admit to do". Past forms double the t: admitted, admitting.

senses.def: a young person who is developing from a child into an adult
examples: Adolescents need more sleep than many adults realize.
The clinic specializes in treating adolescents with eating disorders.

senses.def: connected with the period between childhood and adulthood
examples: The study looks at adolescent brain development.

note: More formal and scientific than "teenager".

senses.def: to legally take another person's child into your family as your own
examples: They adopted a baby girl from Colombia.
We adopted our cat from a local shelter.

senses.def: to start using a particular method, idea or attitude, or to formally approve a plan
examples: Many companies have adopted a four-day work week.
The committee voted to adopt the new rules.

note: Don't confuse with "adapt" (to change to fit). Adoptive parents adopt an adopted child.

senses.def: the act of legally taking another person's child as your own
examples: The couple decided to put the baby up for adoption.
The adoption process can take years.

senses.def: the decision to start using something, or the formal approval of a plan
examples: The adoption of electric cars has been faster than expected.

senses.def: a fully grown person who is legally responsible for their actions
examples: Tickets cost $15 for adults and $8 for children.
Children must be accompanied by an adult.

senses.def: fully grown or developed, or typical of a grown person
examples: An adult elephant can weigh over six tons.
Let's discuss this in an adult way.

senses.def: intended only for adults, especially because of sexual content
examples: The channel shows adult content after midnight.

note: Also pronounced /ˈædʌlt/ in American English.

senses.def: progress or a new development in science, technology or knowledge
examples: Recent advances in medicine have saved millions of lives.
The book describes major advances in artificial intelligence.

senses.def: to develop or improve, or to move forward
examples: Technology has advanced rapidly over the last decade.
The troops advanced toward the capital.

senses.def: done or given before something happens
examples: We received advance warning of the storm.
Advance tickets are cheaper than buying at the door.

senses.def: money paid to someone before the usual time
examples: She asked her boss for an advance on her salary.

note: "In advance" = önceden: "Book your tickets in advance."

senses.def: using the most modern and recently developed ideas, methods or technology
examples: The hospital uses advanced imaging equipment.
This phone has a very advanced camera.

senses.def: at a high or difficult level of study or skill
examples: She is taking an advanced course in French.
The cancer was already at an advanced stage.

senses.def: something that helps you be more successful than others
examples: Speaking Spanish is a big advantage in this job.
The home team has a clear advantage.

senses.def: a good or useful feature of something
examples: One advantage of living downtown is that you don't need a car.

note: "Take advantage of" can be positive (use an opportunity) or negative (exploit someone unfairly).

senses.def: an unusual, exciting or sometimes dangerous experience or journey
examples: Backpacking through South America was the adventure of a lifetime.
The kids love reading adventure stories.

senses.def: excitement and the enjoyment of doing new or risky things
examples: She has a real sense of adventure.

senses.def: negative, harmful or unfavorable
examples: The drug has few adverse side effects.
Flights were delayed due to adverse weather conditions.

note: Formal. Don't confuse with "averse" (unwilling): "not averse to risk".

senses.def: to tell the public about a product or service to persuade them to buy or use it
examples: The company spent millions advertising its new phone.
Cigarettes can no longer be advertised on TV.

senses.def: to make something publicly known, such as a job opening or an event
examples: The position was advertised online last week.
We advertised for a roommate on a local website.

note: American spelling ends in -ise, not -ize: advertise.

senses.def: a notice, picture or video that tells people about a product, job or service
examples: The magazine is full of advertisements for luxury watches.
She answered an advertisement for a part-time job.

note: American stress: ad-ver-TISE-ment. Everyday speech usually says "ad"; on TV/radio, "commercial".

senses.def: the activity or business of telling people about products and services to make them buy them
examples: She works in advertising for a firm in Manhattan.
The company cut its advertising budget this year.

note: Uncountable: "a lot of advertising", not "advertisings".

senses.def: an opinion or suggestion about what someone should do
examples: Can I give you a piece of advice?
You should get legal advice before signing the contract.

note: Uncountable: "some advice", "a piece of advice", never "an advice" or "advices". Noun advice /s/, verb advise /z/.

senses.def: to tell someone what you think they should do
examples: My doctor advised me to cut down on sugar.
I'd advise against driving in this snow.

senses.def: to give expert help on a subject, or formally to inform someone of something
examples: She advises the government on energy policy.
Passengers are advised that the flight is delayed.

senses.def: a person who publicly supports a particular idea, policy or group
examples: She is a passionate advocate for animal rights.
Advocates of the plan say it will create jobs.

senses.def: to publicly support or recommend a particular idea or course of action
examples: Many doctors advocate a plant-based diet.
The group advocates for better working conditions.

senses.def: a lawyer who defends someone in court
examples: The defendant was represented by a court-appointed advocate.

note: Pronunciation: noun /ˈædvəkət/, verb /ˈædvəkeɪt/. "Play devil's advocate" = argue the opposite side for discussion.

senses.def: connected with beauty, art and the appreciation of beautiful things
examples: The building has little aesthetic value.
Some people get cosmetic surgery for aesthetic reasons.

senses.def: a set of ideas or a style that controls how something looks
examples: The café has a minimalist aesthetic with white walls and wooden tables.

note: American English sometimes uses the spelling "esthetic". "Aesthetics" (noun) is the study of beauty.

senses.def: events or matters of public or political importance; usually plural
examples: She writes about foreign affairs for a major newspaper.
The minister refused to discuss the internal affairs of the party.

senses.def: an event or situation, often one that people talk about
examples: The whole affair has damaged his reputation.
The wedding was a small, family affair.

senses.def: a secret sexual relationship, especially when one person is married
examples: He admitted to having an affair with a coworker.

note: "That's my affair" = that's my business, not yours. "State of affairs" = the general situation.

senses.def: to cause a change in someone or something
examples: The new tax will affect millions of families.
Lack of sleep can affect your concentration.

senses.def: to make someone have strong feelings, especially sadness
examples: She was deeply affected by her father's death.

note: Affect is the verb; effect is usually the noun: "Stress affects health" / "Stress has an effect on health." Don't say "affect on".

senses.def: a feeling of liking or loving someone or something and caring about them
examples: He has a deep affection for his grandparents.
Cats show affection by rubbing against your legs.

senses.def: to have enough money to pay for something; usually with can, could or be able to
examples: We can't afford a new car right now.
Many young people can't afford to buy a home.

senses.def: to be able to do something without causing serious problems for yourself
examples: We can't afford to make any more mistakes.
I can't afford to take a day off this week.

note: Almost always with can/can't/could/be able to. Use "afford to do", not "afford doing".

senses.def: cheap enough for ordinary people to pay for
examples: The city badly needs more affordable housing.
The store sells stylish clothes at affordable prices.

senses.def: feeling fear, or worried that something bad might happen
examples: My little brother is afraid of the dark.
Don't be afraid to ask questions in class.

senses.def: used in "I'm afraid" to politely say something unpleasant or disappointing
examples: I'm afraid we're fully booked tonight.
"Is there any coffee left?" "I'm afraid not."

note: Not used before a noun: "the child was afraid", but "a frightened child" (not "an afraid child").

senses.def: later than something; following something in time or order
examples: Let's go for a walk after dinner.
Your name comes after mine on the list.

senses.def: at a time later than when something happens
examples: I'll call you after I finish work.
After she graduated, she moved to Seattle.

senses.def: later in time; afterward
examples: They lived happily ever after.
He got sick on Monday and died the week after.

senses.def: trying to find or catch someone, or named to honor someone
examples: The police are after him for robbery.
She was named after her grandmother.

note: After a conjunction, use present tense for future: "after I finish", not "after I will finish". "Look after" = take care of.

senses.tr: (kötü bir olayın) sonrası, ardından gelen durum
senses.def: the situation that follows an important, usually bad, event such as a war or disaster
examples: In the aftermath of the hurricane, thousands were left homeless.
The country struggled in the aftermath of the war.

note: Usually in the phrase "in the aftermath of"; it suggests something negative.

senses.def: the part of the day from about noon until about six in the evening
examples: I have a dentist appointment on Tuesday afternoon.
We spent the afternoon at the beach.

note: Use "in the afternoon" but "on Monday afternoon" and "this/yesterday afternoon" (no preposition).

senses.def: at a later time, after an event that has been mentioned
examples: We went to a movie and had dinner afterwards.
Shortly afterwards, the police arrived.

note: "Afterward" (without -s) is more common in American English; "afterwards" is more British.

senses.def: one more time, or on another occasion
examples: Could you say that again, please?
It's great to see you again!

senses.def: back to a previous place or condition
examples: She was happy to be home again after the long trip.
It took him weeks to feel healthy again.

note: "Then again" introduces a contrasting idea: "It's expensive. Then again, it's very good quality."

senses.def: opposing or disagreeing with someone or something
examples: Most residents are against the new airport.
It's against the law to text while driving.

senses.def: competing with an opponent, or protecting from something harmful
examples: We're playing against the best team in the league.
Get vaccinated against the flu every fall.

senses.def: touching or pressing on something, or hitting it
examples: He leaned his bike against the wall.
The rain beat against the windows all night.

note: Opposite in the "opinion" sense: "for" (Are you for or against the plan?).

senses.def: the number of years that a person has lived or a thing has existed
examples: She started playing the piano at the age of five.
Children under the age of 12 get in free.

senses.def: a particular period of history
examples: We live in the digital age.
The Bronze Age lasted for about 2,000 years.

senses.def: a very long time; used informally in the plural
examples: I haven't seen you for ages!
It took ages to find a parking space.

senses.def: to become older, or to make someone or something look or become older
examples: He has aged a lot since his wife died.
The wine is aged in oak barrels.

note: American spelling: aging (British: ageing).

senses.def: of a particular age
examples: The program is open to children aged 8 to 12.
The victim, a man aged 45, was taken to the hospital.

senses.def: very old; also "the aged" meaning old people as a group
examples: She takes care of her aged parents.
The center provides care for the aged.

note: Pronounced /eɪdʒd/ for "of the age of", but often /ˈeɪdʒɪd/ when it means "very old" (my aged parents).

senses.def: a business that provides a particular service, often for other companies or people
examples: We booked our trip through a travel agency.
She found her job through a recruitment agency.

senses.def: a government organization responsible for a particular area
examples: The Environmental Protection Agency issued new rules on air pollution.
Several federal agencies are investigating the case.

senses.def: a list of things to be discussed at a meeting
examples: The budget is the first item on the agenda.
Please send me the agenda before the meeting.

senses.def: a list of goals or issues that a person or group considers important, sometimes kept secret
examples: Health care is high on the president's agenda.
I think he has a hidden agenda.

note: False friend: an "agenda" is not a diary/planner (ajanda). For that, Americans say "planner" or "calendar".

senses.def: a person whose job is to act for or manage the business of other people
examples: Our real estate agent showed us five houses in one day.
The actor's agent negotiated a bigger salary.

senses.def: a person who works secretly for a government to get information
examples: FBI agents raided the office early in the morning.
He was a secret agent during the Cold War.

senses.def: a substance or thing that causes a change or has a particular effect
examples: Bleach is a powerful cleaning agent.

note: "Free agent" = a player or person free to sign with any team or do as they like.

senses.def: made up of many separate units combined together
examples: Aggregate demand fell sharply during the recession.
The study looks at aggregate data, not individual cases.

senses.def: a total formed by combining several separate amounts or things
examples: The team won 5–3 on aggregate over two games.
In the aggregate, the changes made a big difference.

senses.def: to combine different amounts or pieces of information into one total or group
examples: The website aggregates news stories from hundreds of sources.
The results were aggregated across all schools.

note: Formal/technical. Pronunciation: noun/adjective /ˈæɡrɪɡət/, verb /ˈæɡrɪɡeɪt/.

senses.def: angry feelings or threatening, violent behavior toward others
examples: Some dogs show aggression toward strangers.
Violent video games have been linked to aggression in children.

senses.def: an attack by one country on another without a good reason
examples: The invasion was condemned as an act of aggression.

senses.def: angry and behaving in a threatening way, ready to attack
examples: The man became aggressive when the bartender refused to serve him.
Keep away from that dog; it's aggressive.

senses.def: acting with determination and force to succeed or achieve a goal
examples: The company launched an aggressive marketing campaign.
Doctors chose an aggressive treatment for the tumor.

note: In business English, "aggressive" can be positive (bold, ambitious); compare "assertive" for confident but not hostile.

senses.def: used after a period of time to say how far back in the past something happened
examples: We moved to Denver five years ago.
I talked to her just a few minutes ago.

note: Use with the simple past, not the present perfect: "I saw him two days ago" (not "have seen"). Use "before" for earlier than a past time.

senses.def: to have the same opinion as someone
examples: I agree with you about the new design.
Most experts agree that exercise improves mental health.

senses.def: to say yes to a request or suggestion
examples: She agreed to help me move this weekend.

senses.def: to decide something together with someone after discussion
examples: The two sides finally agreed on a price.
We agreed to meet at noon.

note: "Agree" is a verb: say "I agree", not "I am agree" (a common Turkish-speaker error).

senses.def: an arrangement or contract made between people, groups or countries
examples: The two countries signed a trade agreement last month.
We have a verbal agreement, but nothing in writing.

senses.def: the state of having the same opinion
examples: We're all in agreement that the plan needs changes.
She nodded in agreement.

senses.def: connected with farming
examples: The region is famous for its agricultural products.
Much of the land is used for agricultural purposes.

senses.def: the science or work of farming, including growing crops and raising animals
examples: Agriculture is still the main source of income in the area.
Climate change poses a serious threat to agriculture.

senses.def: used to show surprise, pleasure, sympathy or sudden understanding
examples: Ah, so that's why the door was locked!
Ah, this coffee is exactly what I needed.

note: "Ah, well" expresses accepting something disappointing.

senses.def: further forward in space, or in front of someone
examples: There's a gas station a mile ahead.
She walked ahead of us, showing the way.

senses.def: in or into the future
examples: We have a busy week ahead.
It's important to plan ahead.

senses.def: winning or more advanced than others
examples: Our team was ahead by ten points at halftime.

note: "Go ahead" = devam et / buyur (permission). "Ahead of schedule" = earlier than planned.

senses.def: a serious illness caused by the HIV virus, which destroys the body's ability to fight infection
examples: New treatments have greatly reduced deaths from AIDS.
The charity funds AIDS research in Africa.

note: Short for Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome. Always written in capital letters; Turkish uses the same abbreviation.

senses.def: money, food or other help given to countries or people in need
examples: The government sent emergency aid to the flood victims.
Most students at the college receive financial aid.

senses.def: a device or tool that helps you do something
examples: My grandfather wears a hearing aid.
Visual aids make a presentation easier to follow.

senses.def: to help someone or make something easier
examples: Fiber aids digestion.
The new software aids doctors in diagnosing cancer.

note: The verb is formal; in everyday speech use "help". "Aid" and "aide" (assistant) sound the same.

senses.def: a person who helps someone in an important job, especially a politician
examples: A senior White House aide spoke to reporters.
The senator's aides refused to comment.

senses.def: a person who assists a teacher, nurse or other professional
examples: She works as a teacher's aide at an elementary school.

senses.def: the purpose of doing something; what you hope to achieve
examples: The main aim of the project is to reduce waste.
She moved to New York with the aim of becoming an actress.

senses.def: to try or plan to achieve something
examples: We aim to finish the work by Friday.
The program is aimed at helping small businesses.

senses.def: to point a weapon or object at someone or something
examples: He aimed the camera at the stage and waited.

note: "Be aimed at" = intended for: "a book aimed at teenagers".

senses.def: the mixture of gases around the earth that we breathe
examples: Let's open a window and get some fresh air.
Air pollution is a major problem in big cities.

senses.def: the space above the ground, or travel by plane
examples: The kids threw their hats in the air.
Most of the goods are shipped by air.

senses.def: a particular feeling or quality that a person or place seems to have
examples: She has an air of confidence about her.

senses.def: to broadcast a program, or to let fresh air into a room
examples: The show airs every Sunday night at nine.

note: "On air" = being broadcast live. "Up in the air" = not yet decided.

senses.def: any vehicle that can fly, such as a plane or helicopter
examples: The airline has ordered fifty new aircraft.
A military aircraft crashed during a training exercise.

note: Plural is the same: one aircraft, two aircraft.

senses.def: a company that provides regular flights for passengers and goods
examples: The airline canceled dozens of flights because of the storm.
Which airline are you flying with?

senses.def: a place where planes take off and land, with buildings for passengers
examples: I'll pick you up at the airport at six.
We got to the airport two hours before our flight.

note: Say "at the airport" for location and "to the airport" for movement.

senses.def: a loud sound or device that warns people of danger or wakes them up
examples: The fire alarm went off in the middle of the night.
I set my alarm for 6:30.

senses.def: a sudden feeling of fear or worry that something bad might happen
examples: The news caused alarm among parents.
There's no cause for alarm.

senses.def: to make someone feel worried or afraid
examples: The rapid spread of the virus alarmed health officials.

senses.def: although; used to add something that makes the previous statement less strong
examples: The economy is growing, albeit slowly.
He accepted the offer, albeit with some reluctance.

note: Formal. Usually followed by an adjective, adverb or phrase, not a full clause.

senses.def: a collection of songs released together as one recording
examples: The band's new album comes out next month.
It's one of the best-selling albums of all time.

senses.def: a book with empty pages for keeping photos, stamps or similar things
examples: My mom keeps all our baby pictures in a photo album.

senses.def: drinks such as beer, wine and whiskey that can make people drunk
examples: You must be 21 to buy alcohol in the United States.
He stopped drinking alcohol two years ago.

senses.def: a clear liquid used in drinks, medicines and cleaning products
examples: Clean the cut with rubbing alcohol.

senses.def: containing alcohol, or connected with alcohol
examples: The bar also serves non-alcoholic cocktails.
Alcoholic drinks are not allowed in the park.

senses.def: a person who is addicted to alcohol
examples: His father was an alcoholic who never sought help.

senses.def: able to think quickly and notice things; watching carefully for danger
examples: Coffee helps me stay alert during long drives.
Drivers should stay alert for deer on this road.

senses.def: a warning about danger, or a situation in which people watch for danger
examples: Police are on high alert after the threats.
I got a news alert on my phone about the earthquake.

senses.def: to warn someone about a danger or a situation that needs action
examples: A neighbor alerted the police after hearing screams.

senses.def: a creature from another planet
examples: The movie is about aliens who invade Earth.
Do you believe aliens have visited our planet?

senses.def: (formal or legal) a person who is not a citizen of the country where they live
examples: Legal aliens must carry their green card at all times.

senses.def: strange, unfamiliar and sometimes frightening
examples: The idea of working from home was alien to my parents.
Life in the city felt alien to him at first.

note: "Illegal alien" is considered offensive by many; "undocumented immigrant" is now common.

senses.def: to arrange things in a straight line or in the correct position relative to each other
examples: Align the text to the left side of the page.
The mechanic aligned the front wheels.

senses.tr: uyumlu hale getirmek; (align with) safında yer almak
senses.def: to change something so it matches something else, or to publicly support a group
examples: We need to align our budget with our goals.
The party aligned itself with the labor unions.

senses.def: having more than one possible meaning, so that it is unclear
examples: The wording of the contract is ambiguous.
Her reply was deliberately ambiguous.

note: Opposite: unambiguous / clear. Ambiguous = more than one meaning; vague = not detailed enough.

senses.def: to accept or deal with something unpleasant
examples: I can't bear the thought of leaving her alone.
The pain was almost too much to bear.

senses.def: to take responsibility for something, or to carry the weight of something
examples: The company will bear the cost of the repairs.
You bear some of the blame for this.

senses.def: a large, heavy wild animal with thick fur
examples: We saw a black bear near the campsite.

note: Irregular verb: bear – bore – borne. "Bear in mind" means "remember and consider".

senses.def: to heat a liquid until it bubbles and turns to steam, or to reach that temperature
examples: Wait until the water boils before you add the pasta.
She boiled the eggs for exactly seven minutes.

senses.def: to cook food in very hot, bubbling water
examples: Boil the potatoes until they are soft enough to mash.

note: "Boil down to" means "to be basically about": It all boils down to money. American English says "bring to a boil".

senses.def: confident and willing to take risks or say what you think
examples: The new mayor made a bold decision to ban cars from downtown.
It was a bold move to quit her job and start a company.

senses.def: very clear and strong in color or shape, so it is easy to notice; printed in thick letters
examples: The poster uses bold colors to catch people's attention.
Key terms are printed in bold.

senses.def: a weapon that explodes, either dropped from a plane or left somewhere
examples: Police evacuated the station after a bomb was found in a bag.
The bomb exploded just after midnight.

senses.def: to attack a place with bombs
examples: Enemy planes bombed the bridge to cut off supply routes.

senses.def: (informal) to fail badly, especially a movie, show, or test
examples: The movie bombed at the box office despite its huge budget.

note: The final b is silent: /bɑːm/. Informal "bomb" (fail) is American; in British English "go down a bomb" means succeed.

senses.def: an attack in which a bomb is exploded or dropped
examples: Dozens of people were injured in the bombing at the market.
No group has claimed responsibility for the bombing.

senses.def: a feeling or shared experience that connects people closely
examples: The two sisters share a strong bond.
Playing on the same team helped build a bond between the boys.

senses.def: a document promising that a government or company will pay back money it has borrowed, with interest
examples: Many retirees invest in government bonds because they are low-risk.

senses.def: to develop a close relationship with someone
examples: The new employees bonded over lunch during their first week.

senses.def: one of the hard parts that make up the skeleton of a person or animal
examples: He broke a bone in his wrist when he fell off his bike.
The dog buried a bone in the backyard.

note: Idioms: "have a bone to pick with someone" (want to complain to them), "bone dry" (completely dry).

senses.def: extra money added to someone's pay, usually as a reward for good work
examples: Every employee received a year-end bonus after a record year.
Her bonus depends on how many sales she makes.

senses.def: something good that you get in addition to what you expected
examples: The hotel is close to the beach, and free breakfast is a bonus.

senses.def: a set of printed pages fixed together inside a cover, or the same text in electronic form
examples: I read a great book about the history of New York.
She has written three books on climate change.

senses.def: to arrange in advance to have a seat, room, ticket, or appointment
examples: We booked a table for eight o'clock.
The flights were fully booked weeks ago.

note: "Do something by the book" means following the rules exactly. Americans also say "make a reservation" for book.

senses.def: an arrangement made in advance to reserve a room, seat, or ticket
examples: You can make a booking online or by phone.
The hotel canceled our booking without any warning.

note: More common in British English; Americans usually say "reservation". "Booking fee" is common in both.

senses.def: a sudden period of fast growth in business, sales, or popularity
examples: The city grew rapidly during the oil boom of the 1970s.
There has been a boom in online shopping.

senses.def: a loud, deep sound, like an explosion
examples: We heard a loud boom as the thunder rolled over the hills.

senses.def: to grow or become successful very quickly
examples: Business is booming now that tourists are coming back.

note: Opposite: bust or slump. "Baby boomers" are people born during the population boom after 1945.

senses.def: to increase something or help it become more successful
examples: The government cut taxes to boost the economy.
Winning the first game really boosted the team's confidence.

senses.def: something that helps or encourages someone or something
examples: The new factory will give a major boost to local employment.

note: A "booster" or "booster shot" is an extra dose of a vaccine.

senses.def: a strong shoe that covers the foot, ankle, and sometimes part of the leg
examples: You'll need waterproof boots for the hike.
She bought a pair of leather boots for the winter.

senses.def: to start a computer so it is ready to use
examples: My laptop takes forever to boot up in the morning.

note: In British English, the boot is a car's storage space; Americans call it the "trunk".

senses.def: the official line that separates two countries or regions
examples: We crossed the border into Canada early in the morning.
The town is right on the border with Mexico.

senses.def: a strip around the edge of something, often for decoration
examples: The invitation had a thin gold border.

senses.def: to share a border with another country or area
examples: Turkey borders eight countries, including Greece and Georgia.

note: "Border on" also means "come close to": His behavior bordered on rude.

senses.def: feeling tired and impatient because something is not interesting or you have nothing to do
examples: The kids got bored after an hour in the car.
I'm bored with doing the same thing every day.

note: Common trap: "I am bored" (I feel it) vs. "I am boring" (I make others feel it).

senses.def: not interesting, making you feel tired and impatient
examples: The lecture was so boring that half the class fell asleep.
Filling out tax forms is boring but necessary.

note: The thing is boring; the person is bored. Don't say "I am boring" when you mean "I am bored".

senses.def: used in "be born" to talk about the beginning of someone's life
examples: I was born in Izmir in 1995.
Their first child was born last spring.

senses.def: having a natural ability for something
examples: She's a born teacher who can explain anything clearly.

note: Always passive: "I was born", never "I born". Do not confuse with "borne" (past participle of bear).

senses.def: to take and use something that belongs to someone else, planning to give it back
examples: Can I borrow your charger for a minute?
They borrowed money from the bank to buy a house.

senses.def: to take an idea, word, or method from somewhere else and use it
examples: English has borrowed many words from French.

note: Borrow = take from someone; lend = give to someone. Say "Can I borrow your pen?", not "Can you borrow me...".

senses.def: the person in charge of you at work
examples: I need to ask my boss if I can leave early on Friday.
She's been her own boss since she opened the bakery.

senses.def: to tell people what to do in an annoying way
examples: Stop bossing your little brother around!

senses.def: used to talk about two people or things together
examples: Both my parents are teachers.
You can park on both sides of the street.

senses.def: the two people or things, considered together
examples: I couldn't decide between the shirts, so I bought both.
Both of them arrived late.

note: "Both X and Y" is the pattern: Both Ali and Can passed. For negatives, use "neither": Neither of them came.

senses.def: to make the effort to do something, usually in negative sentences
examples: He didn't even bother to say goodbye.
Don't bother cooking tonight; we'll order pizza.

senses.def: to annoy, worry, or interrupt someone
examples: Sorry to bother you, but do you know where the station is?
It really bothers me when people talk during movies.

senses.def: a glass or plastic container with a narrow neck, used for liquids
examples: Always carry a bottle of water when you go running.
They opened a bottle of wine to celebrate.

senses.def: to put a liquid into bottles
examples: The juice is bottled at a factory near the orchards.

note: "Bottle up" your feelings means hiding them instead of expressing them.

senses.def: the lowest part or surface of something
examples: The keys were at the bottom of my bag.
Sign your name at the bottom of the page.

senses.def: in the lowest or last position
examples: The plates are on the bottom shelf.
Our team finished in the bottom three this season.

collocations: from the bottom of my heart
note: "The bottom line" is the most important fact. "Get to the bottom of" means find the real cause.

senses.def: to move quickly away from a surface after hitting it, or to make something do this
examples: The ball bounced off the wall and hit the window.
Kids love bouncing on the trampoline.

senses.def: to be returned because there is not enough money in the account or the address is wrong
examples: My email bounced because I typed the address wrong.

note: "Bounce back" means recover quickly after a problem: The economy bounced back.

senses.def: certain or very likely to happen (bound to do something)
examples: With so many guests, something is bound to go wrong.
You're bound to feel nervous on your first day.

senses.def: forced by law, duty, or a promise to do something
examples: The company is legally bound to protect your data.

senses.def: traveling toward a particular place
examples: The train was bound for Chicago when it broke down.

note: Also the past form of "bind". "Out of bounds" means a place you are not allowed to go.

senses.def: a line that marks the edge of an area and separates it from another
examples: The river forms the boundary between the two counties.
A fence marks the boundary of our property.

senses.def: the limit of what is acceptable or of what is known
examples: It's healthy to set clear boundaries with your coworkers.
Scientists keep pushing the boundaries of medicine.

note: "Border" is mainly for countries; "boundary" is for any edge or limit, including personal and abstract ones.

senses.def: to bend your head or body forward to show respect or to say thank you
examples: The actors bowed as the audience stood and clapped.
He bowed his head in prayer.

senses.def: the act of bending your head or body forward as a sign of respect
examples: The pianist took a bow at the end of the concert.

senses.def: to finally agree to do what others want (bow to)
examples: The company bowed to public pressure and withdrew the ad.

note: Pronounced /baʊ/ (like "now") for bending. "Bow" /boʊ/ is a different word: a ribbon knot or a weapon for arrows.

senses.def: a deep round dish used for food or liquid
examples: I had a bowl of soup for lunch.
Mix the flour and eggs in a large bowl.

senses.def: (American) a big college football game played after the regular season
examples: Millions of people watch the Super Bowl every year.

note: "Bowl" as a verb is used in bowling and cricket.

senses.def: a container with flat sides and a base, often with a lid
examples: We packed all our books into cardboard boxes for the move.
She gave me a box of chocolates.

senses.def: a small square on a form where you write or put a mark
examples: Check the box if you agree to the terms.

note: "Think outside the box" means think creatively. "Box" as a verb also means to fight in boxing.

senses.def: a male child or young man
examples: A little boy was flying a kite in the park.
They have two boys and a girl.

senses.def: (informal, American) used to express surprise or strong feeling
examples: Boy, was I glad to get home after that trip!

senses.def: a man or boy that someone is having a romantic relationship with
examples: She's bringing her boyfriend to dinner on Sunday.
Her ex-boyfriend still texts her sometimes.

note: Means a romantic partner. For a male friend, say "a friend" or "a guy friend".

senses.def: the organ inside your head that controls thinking, feeling, and movement
examples: Sleep is essential for a healthy brain.
The accident caused minor brain damage.

senses.def: intelligence, or a very intelligent person who plans something
examples: She has the brains to become a great scientist.
He was the brains behind the whole project.

note: "Pick someone's brain" means ask an expert for advice. "Rack your brain" means think very hard.

senses.def: a part of a tree that grows out from the trunk
examples: A bird built its nest on a high branch.
The storm brought down several large branches.

senses.def: a local office or store that belongs to a larger organization
examples: The bank is closing several of its rural branches.

senses.def: a part or division of a subject, family, or government
examples: Neurology is a branch of medicine.

note: "Branch out" means start doing something new: The company branched out into clothing.

senses.def: a product or group of products made by a company under a particular name
examples: Which brand of coffee do you usually buy?
The company spent millions building its brand.

senses.def: to give a product a particular name, image, or identity
examples: The phones are branded with the store's own logo.

senses.def: to describe someone unfairly as a bad type of person
examples: He was branded a traitor for criticizing the government.

note: "Brand-new" means completely new. Use "brand" for products like food or clothes; for cars and machines, "make" is also common.

senses.def: willing to do things that are dangerous, painful, or difficult
examples: The brave firefighter ran back into the burning house.
It was brave of you to admit your mistake.

senses.def: to deal with an unpleasant situation in order to do something
examples: Thousands of fans braved the cold to watch the parade.

note: "Put on a brave face" means pretend to be fine when you are upset.

senses.def: an action that breaks a law, rule, or agreement
examples: Selling customer data was a clear breach of contract.
The minister resigned over a breach of security rules.

senses.def: a break in a wall or system that allows something to get through
examples: The data breach exposed the passwords of millions of users.

senses.def: to break a law, rule, or agreement
examples: The supplier breached the agreement by delivering late.

note: Formal and legal. Don't confuse with "breech" (the back part of a gun, or a baby born feet first).

senses.def: a basic food made from flour, water, and usually yeast, then baked
examples: I bought a loaf of fresh bread from the bakery.
Would you like some bread with your soup?

note: Uncountable: "some bread" or "a loaf / slice of bread", not "a bread". The "breadwinner" earns the family's money.

senses.def: to separate into pieces or stop working because of force, or to make this happen
examples: Be careful not to break those glasses.
The screen will break if you drop the phone on concrete.

senses.def: to fail to obey a rule or law, or to not keep a promise
examples: He was fined for breaking the speed limit.
Never break a promise to a child.

senses.def: a short time when you stop working or studying to rest
examples: Let's take a ten-minute break and then continue.
Students get a two-week break in the spring.

note: Irregular verb: break – broke – broken. "Give me a break!" (informal) means "Stop it, that's ridiculous".

senses.def: a time when a vehicle or machine stops working
examples: We had a breakdown on the highway and waited two hours for a tow truck.

senses.def: the failure of a relationship, system, or discussion
examples: The breakdown of the peace talks led to more fighting.
She went through a nervous breakdown after years of stress.

senses.def: a detailed list that divides something into its parts
examples: Can you send me a breakdown of the costs?

note: The noun is one word (breakdown); the verb is two (break down): The car broke down.

senses.def: the first meal of the day, eaten in the morning
examples: I usually have eggs and toast for breakfast.
The hotel serves breakfast until ten.

note: No article in general use: "have breakfast", not "have a breakfast" (unless described: "a big breakfast"). Pronounced /ˈbrekfəst/.

senses.tr: atılım, çığır açan gelişme, büyük ilerleme
senses.def: an important discovery or development that helps solve a problem
examples: Researchers made a major breakthrough in cancer treatment.
After weeks of talks, negotiators finally achieved a breakthrough.

senses.def: either of the two soft parts on a woman's chest that can produce milk
examples: Doctors recommend regular checks for breast cancer.
The baby fell asleep at her mother's breast.

senses.def: meat from the front part of a chicken or other bird
examples: Grill the chicken breasts for about six minutes per side.

note: For the general front of the body, use "chest". Pronounced /brest/, not like "beast".

senses.def: the air you take into your lungs and let out again
examples: Take a deep breath and try to relax.
I was out of breath after running up the stairs.

note: Breath /breθ/ is the noun; breathe /briːð/ is the verb. "Don't hold your breath" means "don't expect it to happen soon".

senses.def: to take air into your lungs and send it out again
examples: Breathe in slowly through your nose.
The smoke was so thick that we could hardly breathe.

note: Verb with -e: breathe /briːð/. "Breathe new life into" means make something active or successful again.

senses.def: the process of taking air into the lungs and letting it out
examples: Her breathing became slow and steady as she fell asleep.
Breathing exercises can help reduce anxiety.

note: "Breathing room/space" also means extra time or freedom: The loan gave us some breathing room.

senses.def: a particular type of animal, especially a dog, cat, or farm animal, developed by people
examples: Labradors are one of the most popular dog breeds in America.

senses.def: to produce young animals, or to keep animals in order to produce young
examples: Salmon swim upstream to breed.
The farm breeds horses for racing.

senses.def: to cause a feeling or situation to develop
examples: Poverty often breeds crime and frustration.

note: Irregular verb: breed – bred – bred. "Familiarity breeds contempt" is a common saying.

senses.def: a small block of baked clay used for building walls and houses
examples: They live in an old brick house near the river.
Workers laid the bricks one by one.

note: "Hit a brick wall" means reach a point where you cannot make progress.

senses.def: a woman who is getting married or has just gotten married
examples: The bride wore her grandmother's lace dress.
Everyone stood up as the bride walked down the aisle.

note: The man is the "groom" (or bridegroom). In Turkish "gelin" also means daughter-in-law, but English "bride" does not.

senses.def: a structure built over a river, road, or railroad so people can cross it
examples: The new bridge cut travel time across the river in half.
They walked across the Brooklyn Bridge at sunset.

senses.def: to reduce the difference or distance between two groups or things
examples: The program aims to bridge the gap between rich and poor students.

note: "Burn your bridges" means destroy a relationship so you can't go back. "We'll cross that bridge when we come to it" = deal with it later.

senses.def: lasting only a short time
examples: After a brief pause, the speaker continued.
We made a brief stop in Denver on the way.

senses.def: using few words
examples: Please keep your answers brief and to the point.

senses.def: to give someone the information they need about a situation
examples: The general briefed reporters on the latest developments.

note: "In brief" means "in a few words". A "briefing" is a meeting where people receive information.

senses.def: for a short time
examples: The power went out briefly during the storm.
She worked briefly as a waitress before college.

senses.def: in a few words
examples: Let me briefly explain how the system works.

senses.def: full of light or shining strongly
examples: It was a bright, sunny morning.
The lights were so bright that I had to close my eyes.

senses.def: strong and easy to see
examples: She painted the kitchen a bright yellow.

senses.def: intelligent and quick to learn; likely to be successful
examples: He's a bright student with a bright future ahead of him.

note: "Look on the bright side" means focus on the good parts of a bad situation.

senses.def: extremely intelligent, skilled, or impressive
examples: She's a brilliant scientist who has won several awards.
That's a brilliant idea!

senses.def: very bright
examples: The sky turned a brilliant orange at sunset.

note: In British English "brilliant!" casually means "great!"; Americans more often say "awesome" or "great".

senses.def: to take someone or something with you to the place where you are going or where the speaker is
examples: Can you bring a salad to the party?
