Don't forget to bring your passport.

senses.def: to cause a particular situation or feeling
examples: The new factory will bring hundreds of jobs to the area.
Her music brings joy to millions of people.

note: Irregular verb: bring – brought – brought. Bring = toward the speaker; take = away from the speaker.

senses.def: wide from one side to the other
examples: He has broad shoulders from years of swimming.
A broad river runs through the valley.

senses.def: including many different things or people; general rather than detailed
examples: The store offers a broad range of products.
There is broad agreement on the main goals.

note: "In broad daylight" means openly during the day, used about surprising crimes. Opposite: narrow.

senses.def: a fast internet connection that is always on
examples: Many rural homes still don't have access to broadband.
We upgraded to faster broadband so we could stream movies.

note: Common in news and policy language. In everyday American speech, people often just say "high-speed internet".

senses.def: to send out a program on television, radio, or the internet
examples: The game will be broadcast live on national TV.
The station broadcasts news every hour.

senses.def: a program sent out on television, radio, or the internet
examples: Millions watched the live broadcast of the ceremony.

note: Past forms are usually the same: broadcast – broadcast – broadcast.

senses.def: a person who presents programs on radio or television
examples: She worked as a sports broadcaster for twenty years.

senses.def: a company that sends out radio or television programs
examples: The public broadcaster refused to air the controversial ad.

senses.def: in a general way, without paying attention to details
examples: Broadly speaking, the plan was a success.
The two reports are broadly similar.

senses.def: with a wide smile
examples: He smiled broadly when he heard the good news.

senses.def: damaged, cracked, or no longer working properly
examples: Be careful, there's broken glass on the floor.
He's been off work with a broken leg.

senses.def: ended or destroyed, especially a relationship or promise
examples: She grew up in a broken home.
Voters are tired of broken promises.

note: "Broken English" means English spoken with many mistakes. For machines, Americans also say "out of order".

senses.def: a boy or man who has the same parents as you
examples: My older brother lives in Ankara.
She has two brothers and a sister.

note: English doesn't separate abi and küçük kardeş; say "older" or "younger brother". "Big Brother" also means government surveillance.

senses.def: having the color of soil or coffee
examples: She has long brown hair and green eyes.
Use brown sugar for a richer flavor.

senses.def: the color of soil or coffee
examples: The living room is decorated in warm browns and creams.

senses.def: to cook food until it turns brown on the outside
examples: Brown the onions in a little oil before adding the meat.

note: "Brown bread" and "brown rice" mean whole-grain.

senses.def: a computer program used to find and view pages on the internet
examples: Try clearing your browser history if the page won't load.
The website works in every major browser.

note: Related verb "browse" also means look around a store without a clear plan to buy.

senses.def: a tool with stiff hairs or wires on a handle, used for cleaning, painting, or hair
examples: Use a small brush to paint the corners.
She keeps a hair brush in her bag.

senses.def: to clean or tidy something with a brush
examples: Brush your teeth twice a day.
He brushed the snow off the car.

senses.def: to touch something lightly while moving past it
examples: Her hand brushed mine as she reached for the menu.

note: "Brush up on" means improve a skill you have partly forgotten: I need to brush up on my Spanish.

senses.def: very violent and cruel
examples: The country suffered under a brutal dictatorship.
Police are investigating a brutal attack in the park.

senses.tr: çok sert, dayanılmaz; (dürüstlük) kaba ama net
senses.def: very harsh or unpleasant; direct without trying to be kind
examples: The winter was brutal, with weeks of freezing temperatures.
I appreciated her brutal honesty about my essay.

note: "Brutally honest" means honest in a way that may hurt. "Police brutality" is a common news phrase.

senses.def: a ball of air or gas inside a liquid, or floating in the air
examples: The kids were blowing soap bubbles in the yard.
Small bubbles rose to the top of the glass.

senses.def: a situation where prices rise very fast and then suddenly fall
examples: Many investors lost everything when the housing bubble burst.

senses.def: a closed group or situation that keeps you away from other views or realities
examples: Social media can trap you in a bubble of people who think like you.

note: "Bubbly" describes a cheerful, lively person.

senses.def: (informal) a US dollar
examples: I bought this jacket for twenty bucks at a thrift store.
Can you lend me a few bucks for lunch?

senses.def: a male deer, rabbit, or similar animal
examples: A large buck stood at the edge of the forest.

note: Informal. "Pass the buck" = avoid responsibility by blaming others. "More bang for your buck" = better value.

senses.def: (informal) a friend
examples: I'm going camping with some buddies from college.
He and his workout buddy meet at the gym every morning.

senses.def: (informal, American) used to address a man, sometimes in an unfriendly way
examples: Hey buddy, you dropped your wallet!

note: Very common in American English. "Mate" is the British and Australian equivalent.

senses.def: the amount of money a person or organization has and a plan for spending it
examples: We have a budget of five hundred dollars for the trip.
The city council approved next year's budget.

senses.def: to plan carefully how much money to spend
examples: I budget about two hundred dollars a month for groceries.

senses.def: cheap
examples: We flew with a budget airline to save money.

senses.def: something that protects against harm or reduces the effect of a problem
examples: Savings act as a buffer against unexpected expenses.
Leave a buffer of thirty minutes in case of traffic.

senses.def: (of a video) to pause while more data loads
examples: The video kept buffering because the Wi-Fi was slow.

note: A "buffer zone" is a neutral area between two opposing countries or forces.

senses.def: (informal) any small insect
examples: There were bugs everywhere after the rain.
A bug flew into my coffee.

senses.def: a mistake in a computer program that stops it working correctly
examples: The update fixed a bug that made the app crash.

senses.def: (informal) a minor illness caused by an infection
examples: Half the office has caught a stomach bug.

senses.def: (informal) to annoy someone
examples: It really bugs me when people are late.

note: "Bug" as a verb also means put a secret microphone somewhere: The room was bugged.

senses.def: to make something by putting parts or materials together
examples: They're building a new hospital downtown.
My grandfather built this house himself.

senses.def: to develop something gradually, such as a relationship or business
examples: It takes years to build trust with customers.
She built her company from nothing.

senses.def: the shape and size of someone's body
examples: He has a strong, athletic build.

note: Irregular verb: build – built – built. "Build on" means use past success as a base for more.

senses.def: a structure with walls and a roof, such as a house or office
examples: The tallest building in the city has eighty floors.
Smoking is not allowed anywhere in the building.

senses.def: the process or business of constructing things
examples: The building of the new stadium took three years.

note: "Building blocks" are the basic parts that something is made from.

senses.def: the main or largest part of something
examples: The bulk of the work was done by volunteers.
Rent takes up the bulk of my salary.

senses.def: large quantities (used in "in bulk")
examples: Buying rice in bulk is much cheaper.

senses.def: the large size or weight of something or someone
examples: Despite his bulk, he moved surprisingly fast.

note: "The bulk of" is formal but very common in news and academic writing.

senses.def: a small piece of metal fired from a gun
examples: The bullet missed him by inches.
Police found several bullets at the scene.

note: "Bite the bullet" = do something unpleasant you've been avoiding. "Bullet points" are the dots in a list.

senses.def: a number of similar things growing or tied together
examples: He bought her a bunch of flowers.
Grab a bunch of bananas from the store.

senses.def: (informal) a large amount or group of people or things
examples: I have a whole bunch of emails to answer.
They're a nice bunch of people.

note: "A bunch of" for "a lot of" is very common in spoken American English: a bunch of stuff.

senses.def: a difficult duty or responsibility that causes worry or hard work
examples: The new tax will place a heavy burden on small businesses.
She didn't want to be a burden to her children.

senses.def: to give someone a duty or problem that is difficult to deal with
examples: I don't want to burden you with my problems.

note: "The burden of proof" is a legal phrase: the duty to prove something is true.

senses.def: a system of official rules and procedures, especially when it seems too slow or complicated
examples: Getting a work visa involves a lot of bureaucracy.
The new mayor promised to cut red tape and bureaucracy.

senses.def: the officials and departments that run a government or large organization
examples: The federal bureaucracy employs millions of people.

note: Usually negative. Spelling is tricky: bureau + cracy. "Red tape" is the informal equivalent.

senses.def: the act or ceremony of putting a dead body in the ground
examples: The burial took place in the family's hometown.
Archaeologists discovered an ancient burial site.

note: Pronounced /ˈberiəl/, like "berry-al", not "bury-al" with /ʌ/.

senses.def: to be on fire, or to destroy or damage something with fire or heat
examples: The old barn burned to the ground.
I burned the toast again.

senses.def: to use fuel or energy
examples: A brisk walk burns about three hundred calories an hour.

senses.def: an injury or mark caused by fire, heat, or acid
examples: She suffered minor burns on her hands while cooking.

note: Past form: burned (American) or burnt (British; also used as an adjective in American: burnt toast). "Burnout" = exhaustion from work.

senses.def: to break open suddenly because of pressure from inside, or to make something do this
examples: A water pipe burst in the basement during the cold night.
The balloon burst with a loud bang.

senses.def: to move or start doing something suddenly and with force
examples: The kids burst into the room shouting.
She burst into tears when she heard the news.

senses.def: a short, sudden period of activity, energy, or noise
examples: He finished the race with a final burst of speed.

note: Irregular verb: burst – burst – burst. "Bursting with" means very full of: bursting with pride.

senses.def: to put a dead body in the ground
examples: He was buried next to his wife in the village cemetery.

senses.def: to hide something in the ground or under other things
examples: Dogs often bury bones in the backyard to save them for later.
The report was buried under a pile of papers on my desk.

note: Pronounced /ˈberi/, same as "berry". "Bury the hatchet" means end an argument and become friends again.

senses.def: a large vehicle that carries passengers along a fixed route
examples: I take the bus to work every morning.
We missed the last bus and had to walk home.

note: Say "on the bus" (not "in the bus") and "by bus" (no article). Plural: buses.

senses.def: a plant like a small tree with many stems growing close together
examples: The cat was hiding behind a bush in the yard.
We planted rose bushes along the fence.

note: "Beat around the bush" means avoid saying something directly (Turkish: lafı dolandırmak).

senses.def: the activity of making, buying, and selling goods or services for money
examples: She studied business at college.
Business has been slow since the holidays.

senses.def: a company, store, or other organization that makes money
examples: He runs a small business that repairs bikes.

senses.def: something that concerns a particular person
examples: How much I earn is none of your business.

note: Pronounced /ˈbɪznəs/ with two syllables. "On business" means traveling for work.

senses.def: a man who works in business, especially one who owns or runs a company
examples: A local businessman donated money to rebuild the library.
He became a successful businessman by thirty.

note: Plural: businessmen. Gender-neutral options: businessperson, business owner, entrepreneur.

senses.def: having a lot of things to do and little free time
examples: I'm too busy to go out tonight.
She's busy working on her thesis.

senses.def: full of people, traffic, or activity
examples: The restaurant gets really busy on Friday nights.
They live on a busy street.

senses.def: (American) of a phone line, being used
examples: I tried calling, but the line was busy.

note: Pattern: busy + -ing (busy cooking), not "busy to cook". British English says the line is "engaged".

senses.def: used to introduce something that contrasts with what was just said
examples: The hotel was expensive but very comfortable.
I'd love to come, but I have to work.

senses.def: except; apart from
examples: Everyone but my brother came to the wedding.
I've had nothing but problems with this car.

note: "All but" means "almost" (all but impossible); "anything but" means "definitely not" (anything but easy).

senses.def: a soft yellow food made from cream, used in cooking and spread on bread
examples: Spread some butter on the toast while it's hot.
Melt the butter in a pan over low heat.

senses.def: to spread butter on something
examples: She buttered the bread and added a slice of cheese.

note: "Butter someone up" means be very nice to someone to get something. Uncountable: some butter.

senses.def: a small round object sewn onto clothes to fasten them
examples: A button fell off my coat on the way to work.

senses.def: a small part of a machine or screen that you press to make it work
examples: Press the red button to stop the machine.
Click the button below to download the file.

senses.def: to fasten clothes with buttons
examples: Button up your jacket; it's freezing outside.

collocations: at the push of a button
note: "Push someone's buttons" means deliberately annoy them.

senses.def: to get something by paying money for it
examples: We want to buy a house next year.
Did you buy anything at the mall?

senses.def: (informal) to believe something someone says
examples: He said the dog ate his homework, but the teacher didn't buy it.

senses.def: something you buy, especially at a good price
examples: At that price, the laptop is a really good buy.

note: Irregular verb: buy – bought – bought. "Buy time" means delay something to get more time.

senses.def: used to show how something is done, or who does it
examples: We traveled to Boston by train.
The novel was written by a young Nigerian author.

senses.def: not later than a particular time
examples: Please send me the report by Friday.

senses.def: near or beside someone or something
examples: She was sitting by the window reading a book.

senses.def: past someone or something
examples: A police car drove by with its lights flashing.
Time goes by so fast.

note: "By Friday" = no later than Friday; "until Friday" = continuing up to Friday.

senses.def: (informal) goodbye
examples: Bye! See you tomorrow.
She waved bye to her friends from the bus window.

note: Informal. "Bye-bye" sounds childish or very casual.

senses.def: a small room for sleeping on a ship, or the area where passengers sit on a plane
examples: Our cabin on the cruise ship had a small window.
The cabin crew served drinks after takeoff.

senses.def: a small, simple wooden house, especially in the woods or mountains
examples: We rented a log cabin by the lake for the weekend.

note: "Cabin fever" is the restless feeling from being stuck indoors too long.

senses.def: a group of senior government members who make important decisions
examples: The president announced several changes to his cabinet.
She served in the cabinet as secretary of state.

senses.def: a piece of furniture with shelves or drawers, used for storing things
examples: The glasses are in the kitchen cabinet above the sink.

note: A "cabinet reshuffle" is when a leader changes which ministers do which jobs.

senses.def: a set of wires covered in plastic that carries electricity or signals
examples: Plug the cable into the back of the TV.
Workers are laying fiber-optic cables under the street.

senses.def: a television system that sends programs through cables
examples: Many young people cancel cable and just use streaming services.

note: A "cable car" (teleferik) is pulled by a cable up a hill or mountain.

senses.def: a small place where you can buy drinks and simple meals
examples: Let's meet at the cafe across from the library.
She spends hours working on her laptop in cafes.

note: Also spelled "café". Americans often say "coffee shop". A "cafeteria" is a self-service restaurant, e.g. in a school.

senses.def: a sweet baked food made from flour, eggs, sugar, and butter
examples: We ordered a chocolate cake for her birthday.
Would you like another slice of cake?

collocations: have your cake and eat it too
note: "A piece of cake" means very easy. "Cake" covers both Turkish "pasta" and "kek"; "pasta" in English means noodles.

senses.def: to find a number or amount using mathematics
examples: Use this app to calculate how much tax you owe.
Scientists calculated the distance to the star.

senses.def: to judge or guess what will probably happen
examples: We calculated that the trip would take about four hours.

note: A "calculated risk" is one taken after careful thought. A "calculating" person is coldly selfish.

senses.def: the process of using numbers to find an amount, or the result of this
examples: By my calculation, we'll run out of money in March.
The engineers made a few mistakes in their calculations.

senses.def: careful planning to get what you want, often in a selfish way
examples: Her kindness seemed to be based on cold calculation.

senses.def: to phone someone
examples: I'll call you when I get to the airport.
Call 911 if anyone is hurt.

senses.def: to give someone or something a name, or to describe them in a certain way
examples: They called their daughter Elif after her grandmother.
Critics called the plan a disaster.

senses.def: an act of speaking to someone on the phone
examples: I got a call from the bank this morning.

senses.def: a public request for something to happen
examples: There are growing calls for the minister to resign.

note: "Call off" = cancel. "A close call" = a narrow escape from danger. "It's your call" = it's your decision.

senses.def: not excited, nervous, or upset
examples: Try to stay calm and explain what happened.
She remained calm even when the plane started shaking.

senses.def: without strong wind or big waves
examples: The sea was calm enough for swimming.

senses.def: to make someone or something quieter and more relaxed
examples: The mayor tried to calm angry residents at the meeting.
Calm down, it's not a big deal.

senses.def: a quiet, peaceful time or situation
examples: A strange calm settled over the city after the protests.

note: The l is silent in American English: /kɑːm/. Saying "calm down" to an angry person can sound rude.

senses.def: a device for taking photographs or recording video
examples: My phone's camera takes better pictures than my old digital one.
Security cameras recorded the robbery.

note: "On camera" = being filmed. "Off camera" = not being filmed. Usually two syllables in speech: /ˈkæmrə/.

senses.def: a place where people stay in tents or simple buildings for a short time
examples: We set up camp next to the river.
Thousands of refugees are living in camps near the border.

senses.def: (American) a place where children go in summer to do activities
examples: The kids are going to summer camp for two weeks.

senses.def: to stay in a tent for a short time, usually for fun
examples: We camped in the mountains for three nights.

note: "Camp" can also mean a group with the same opinion: the two camps in the debate.

senses.def: a series of planned activities to achieve a political, social, or business goal
examples: The company launched an advertising campaign for its new phone.
Her election campaign focused on health care.

senses.def: to work in an organized way to achieve something or to win an election
examples: Parents are campaigning for safer roads near the school.
He campaigned in every state before the election.

note: The g is silent: /kæmˈpeɪn/.

senses.def: the activity of staying in a tent or simple shelter, usually on vacation
examples: We go camping in Yosemite every summer.
Bring warm clothes; camping in the desert gets cold at night.

note: In Turkish "kamping" means a campsite; in English "camping" is the activity. The place is a "campsite" or "campground".

senses.def: the buildings and land of a university, college, or company
examples: First-year students are required to live on campus.
The company's new campus has its own gym and cafeteria.

note: Say "on campus", not "in campus". Plural: campuses.

senses.def: used to say that someone is able to do something or that something is possible
examples: She can speak four languages.
Smoking can cause serious health problems.

senses.def: used to ask for or give permission, or to make a request
examples: Can I use your phone for a minute?
You can leave early today if you want.

senses.def: a metal container for food or drink
examples: He opened a can of soda and sat down.

note: Past: could. Negative: cannot / can't. British English often says "tin" for a food can.

senses.def: a long artificial waterway for boats or for carrying water
examples: The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
Venice is famous for its canals.

senses.def: a tube inside the body that carries food, air, or other substances
examples: The dentist said I need a root canal.

note: A TV "kanal" is a "channel" in English, not a canal.

senses.def: to decide that something arranged will not happen
examples: Our flight was canceled because of the snowstorm.
I had to cancel my dentist appointment.

senses.def: to end an agreement, order, or subscription
examples: I canceled my gym membership after two months.

note: American spelling: canceled, canceling (British: cancelled). "Cancel out" means balance so there is no effect.

senses.def: a serious disease in which cells in the body grow in an uncontrolled way
examples: Smoking is the leading cause of lung cancer.
Her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer last year.

senses.def: a person who is trying to be elected or who is applying for a job
examples: Three candidates are running for mayor.
We interviewed ten candidates for the position.

senses.def: someone or something likely to be chosen for something
examples: The old factory is a strong candidate for redevelopment.

senses.def: a stick of wax with a string in the middle that you burn to give light
examples: She blew out the candles on her birthday cake.
We lit candles when the power went out.

note: "Burn the candle at both ends" means work too hard and sleep too little.

senses.def: the negative form of can
examples: I cannot believe how quickly the year went by.
Visitors cannot enter the building without an ID.

note: Written as one word. "Can't" is the usual spoken form; "cannot" is more formal or emphatic.

senses.def: a strong, heavy cloth used for tents, bags, and shoes
examples: He wore old canvas sneakers.
The tent was made of thick canvas.

senses.def: a piece of this cloth used for painting on, or a painting on it
examples: The artist stretched a large canvas over a wooden frame.

note: "Canvass" (double s) is a different word: to ask people for votes or opinions.

senses.def: a soft, flat hat with a hard curved part at the front
examples: He always wears a baseball cap backward.

senses.def: a cover that protects the end of a pen, bottle, or tube
examples: Put the cap back on the toothpaste.

senses.def: an upper limit on an amount of money
examples: The city placed a cap on rent increases.

senses.def: to put a limit on an amount
examples: Interest rates on student loans are capped at five percent.

note: "To cap it all" means "as the final bad thing".

senses.def: the ability or power to do something
examples: The new software has the capability to translate in real time.
Some countries are developing nuclear capability.

note: Common in plural for skills or features: the phone's camera capabilities.

senses.def: having the ability or power to do something
examples: The stadium is capable of holding fifty thousand people.
I'm perfectly capable of making my own decisions.

senses.def: good at your work; skilled
examples: She's a very capable manager.

note: Pattern: capable OF doing something, not "capable to do".

senses.def: the number of people or things that a place or container can hold
examples: The concert hall has a capacity of two thousand.
The hospital is already full to capacity.

senses.def: the ability to understand or do something
examples: Children have an amazing capacity for learning languages.

senses.def: an official position or role
examples: She attended the meeting in her capacity as company lawyer.

senses.def: the city where a country's government is based
examples: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, not Istanbul.

senses.def: money or property used to start a business or to invest
examples: They raised enough capital to open a second restaurant.

senses.def: (of a letter) in the large form used at the start of a sentence or name
examples: Names of countries always start with a capital letter.

senses.def: involving the death penalty
examples: Capital punishment was abolished in many states.

note: Don't confuse with "Capitol", the building where the US Congress meets.

senses.def: an economic system in which businesses are owned privately and run for profit
examples: Critics argue that capitalism increases inequality.
The country moved from communism to capitalism in the 1990s.

senses.def: based on or supporting capitalism
examples: Most Western countries have capitalist economies.
The book criticizes capitalist values.

senses.def: a person who supports capitalism or who owns a lot of business wealth
examples: Venture capitalists invested millions in the startup.

senses.def: the person in charge of a ship or plane
examples: The captain announced that we would land in twenty minutes.

senses.def: the leader of a sports team
examples: She was named captain of the soccer team.

senses.def: an officer of middle rank in the army, navy, or police
examples: A police captain spoke to reporters outside the station.

senses.def: to catch a person or animal, or to take control of a place by force
examples: Police captured the suspect after a two-day search.
Rebels captured the city's airport.

senses.def: to record or show something accurately in words, pictures, or film
examples: The photo perfectly captures the joy of the moment.

senses.def: the act of catching or being caught
examples: The soldier managed to avoid capture for weeks.

senses.def: a road vehicle with an engine and four wheels that carries a few people
examples: She drives an old car to work every day.
We rented a car at the airport.

senses.def: (American) a separate part of a train
examples: The dining car is at the back of the train.

note: "Get in/out of a car", but "get on/off a bus or train". British "car park" = American "parking lot".

senses.def: a chemical element found in all living things, and in coal, diamonds, and graphite
examples: Diamonds are made of pure carbon.
Trees absorb carbon from the air.

senses.def: carbon dioxide or other carbon gases, especially as a cause of climate change
examples: The city plans to cut carbon emissions by half by 2035.

note: Your "carbon footprint" is the amount of carbon dioxide your activities produce. "Carbonated" drinks are fizzy.

senses.def: a folded piece of stiff paper with a message, sent on special occasions
examples: I sent my grandmother a birthday card.

senses.def: a small plastic card used for paying or identifying yourself
examples: Can I pay by card?
Show your ID card at the entrance.

senses.def: one of a set of cards used for playing games
examples: We stayed up late playing cards.

note: "Put your cards on the table" = be honest about your plans. "In the cards" (American) = likely to happen.

senses.def: to feel that something is important or to be worried about it
examples: I don't care what other people think.
He really cares about the environment.

senses.def: to look after someone who is sick, young, or old (care for)
examples: She quit her job to care for her elderly father.

senses.def: the process of looking after someone and providing what they need
examples: The patients receive excellent care at this hospital.

senses.def: attention and effort to avoid damage or mistakes
examples: Handle the package with care; it's fragile.

note: "Take care" also means goodbye. "I couldn't care less" means "I don't care at all".

senses.def: the series of jobs someone has in one area of work over their life
examples: She began her career as a reporter in Chicago.
He's thinking about a career in medicine.

note: Stress on the second syllable: ca-REER. Don't confuse with "carrier".

senses.def: giving attention to what you are doing to avoid accidents or mistakes
examples: Be careful crossing the street.
You need to be careful with your money.

senses.def: done with a lot of attention to detail
examples: After careful consideration, we decided not to move.

senses.def: with a lot of attention to avoid mistakes, damage, or danger
examples: Read the instructions carefully before you start.
He carefully placed the vase on the shelf.

senses.def: not giving enough attention to what you are doing, so that you make mistakes
examples: I lost points on the test because of careless mistakes.
It was careless of you to leave the door unlocked.

senses.def: the goods carried by a ship, plane, or truck
examples: The ship was carrying a cargo of grain to Egypt.
Cargo planes land at the airport throughout the night.

note: Turkish "kargo" usually means a parcel delivery; in English that is a "package" or "delivery", not cargo.

senses.def: thick material that covers a floor
examples: We're replacing the old carpet with wood floors.
Take your shoes off so you don't get mud on the carpet.

senses.def: a thick layer of something on the ground
examples: A carpet of autumn leaves covered the path.

note: A "rug" covers part of a floor; "carpet" usually covers it all. "Roll out the red carpet" = welcome someone grandly.

senses.def: a vehicle pulled by horses, used especially in the past
examples: Tourists can ride a horse-drawn carriage through Central Park.

senses.def: (British) a separate section of a train for passengers
examples: The first carriage was packed, so we walked to the back.

senses.def: (American) a baby carriage, a small vehicle for pushing a baby
examples: She pushed the baby carriage slowly through the park.

note: For a train section, Americans say "car" and the British say "carriage". A modern baby carriage is usually called a "stroller".

senses.def: a long, pointed orange vegetable that grows under the ground
examples: Chop the carrots and add them to the soup.
Kids often eat raw carrots as a snack.

senses.def: something offered to persuade someone to do something
examples: The government is using tax breaks as a carrot to attract investors.

note: "Carrot and stick" means using both rewards and punishments (Turkish: havuç ve sopa).

senses.def: to hold something and take it from one place to another
examples: Can you help me carry these boxes upstairs?
The bus carries about fifty passengers.

senses.def: to have something with you all the time
examples: I always carry an umbrella in my bag.

senses.def: to involve something as a result or a risk
examples: The crime carries a sentence of up to ten years in prison.

note: "Carry out" = do or complete (carry out research). "Carry on" = continue. "Get carried away" = become too excited.

senses.def: a film or TV show made from drawings, usually for children
examples: My kids watch cartoons every Saturday morning.

senses.def: a funny drawing in a newspaper or magazine, often about politics
examples: The newspaper published a cartoon mocking the senator.

note: A "caricature" exaggerates a real person's features; a "cartoon" is broader.

senses.def: to make an object or pattern by cutting wood, stone, or another hard material
examples: He carved a small bird out of a piece of wood.
Someone carved their initials into the tree.

senses.def: to cut cooked meat into slices
examples: Dad always carves the turkey on Thanksgiving.

senses.def: to create a position or reputation through hard work (carve out)
examples: She has carved out a successful career in tech.

note: "Carved in stone" means fixed and impossible to change: The plan isn't carved in stone.

senses.def: a particular situation or example of something
examples: In some cases, patients recover without any treatment.
Take an umbrella in case it rains.

senses.def: a matter decided in court, or a crime investigated by the police
examples: The case will go to trial next month.
Detectives are still working on the case.

senses.def: an example of a disease or illness
examples: There have been thousands of new flu cases this week.

senses.def: a container or cover that protects something
examples: I need a new case for my phone.

note: "In case" = as a precaution (take a coat in case it gets cold), not the same as "if". "Make a case for" = argue in favor of.

senses.def: money in the form of coins and bills
examples: Do you take cash or only cards?
I don't carry much cash anymore.

senses.def: to exchange a check for money
examples: I need to cash this check at the bank.

note: Uncountable: "a lot of cash". "Cash in on" means profit from a situation, often unfairly.

senses.def: a building where people play games for money, such as cards or roulette
examples: They lost a lot of money at a casino in Las Vegas.
The new casino brought jobs but also problems to the town.

note: Turkish "gazino" is usually a music venue; the English "casino" is only for gambling.

senses.def: all the actors in a play, movie, or TV show
examples: The movie has an amazing cast of young actors.

senses.def: to look in a direction, or to make light, a shadow, or doubt fall on something
examples: She cast a quick glance at the clock.
The new evidence casts doubt on his story.

senses.def: to vote
examples: Over a million people cast their votes by mail.

senses.def: to choose an actor for a particular role
examples: She was cast as the lead in the new series.

note: Irregular: cast – cast – cast. A "cast" is also the hard cover put on a broken arm or leg (alçı).

senses.def: a large, strong building with thick walls and towers, built in the past for defense
examples: We visited a medieval castle on top of the hill.
The kids built a sand castle on the beach.

note: The t is silent: /ˈkæsl/. "Build castles in the air" means make unrealistic plans.

senses.def: relaxed and not formal
examples: You can wear casual clothes to the office on Fridays.
It was a casual dinner with a few friends.

senses.def: not showing much care or interest
examples: His casual attitude toward safety worried the team.

senses.def: not regular or serious; happening by chance
examples: To a casual observer, the two paintings look identical.

note: "Business casual" is a dress code: neat but not a suit and tie.

senses.def: a person who is killed or injured in a war or accident
examples: The earthquake caused heavy casualties.
There were no casualties in the fire, thanks to the alarm.

senses.def: someone or something that suffers as a result of an event
examples: Small shops were the first casualties of the recession.

note: Includes both injured and killed people. "Fatality" means only someone who died.

senses.def: a small furry animal often kept as a pet
examples: Our cat sleeps on the sofa all afternoon.
Istanbul is famous for its street cats.

senses.def: a large wild animal of the cat family
examples: Lions and tigers are the best-known big cats.

collocations: let the cat out of the bag
note: "Let the cat out of the bag" means reveal a secret by accident.

senses.def: a complete list of items, such as products for sale or books in a library
examples: The store sends out a new catalog every season.
You can search the library's online catalog.

senses.def: a long series of bad things
examples: The report describes a catalog of errors by hospital staff.

senses.def: to make a list of things in an organized way
examples: Volunteers are cataloging thousands of old photographs.

note: American spelling: catalog. British spelling: catalogue.

senses.def: to stop and hold a moving object, or to capture a person or animal
examples: The dog jumped up to catch the ball.
Police finally managed to catch the thief.

senses.def: to get on a bus, train, or plane before it leaves
examples: I have to catch the 7:15 train.

senses.def: to get an illness
examples: Wear a coat or you'll catch a cold.

senses.def: the act of catching something; also a hidden problem
examples: What a great catch by the goalkeeper!
The flights are so cheap; what's the catch?

note: Irregular verb: catch – caught – caught. "Catch up" = reach the same level; "catch on" = become popular.

senses.def: a group of people or things with similar features
examples: The film was nominated in three categories.
Most of our customers fall into the 25 to 40 age category.

note: "Categorically" means completely and definitely: He categorically denied the claims.

senses.tr: (yemek ve içecek) hizmeti vermek, catering yapmak
senses.def: to provide food and drinks for a party or event
examples: A local restaurant catered the wedding.
The company caters for events of up to five hundred people.

senses.def: to provide what a particular group of people needs or wants (cater to)
examples: The hotel caters to business travelers.

note: American English prefers "cater to"; British English uses "cater for". "Cater to" can also mean satisfy demands too much.

senses.def: an agreement in which each side gives up some of what it wants
examples: After hours of talks, they finally reached a compromise.
Marriage is all about compromise.

senses.def: to reach an agreement by both sides accepting less than they wanted
examples: Neither side is willing to compromise on this issue.

senses.def: to put something at risk or weaken it, or to act against your principles
examples: The data breach compromised millions of accounts.
I won't compromise my principles for money.

senses.def: to work together with other people or groups to achieve a shared goal
examples: The two hospitals agreed to cooperate on the new cancer study.
Local residents cooperated with police during the search.

senses.def: to be helpful by doing what someone asks you to do
examples: The suspect refused to cooperate and asked for a lawyer.
If the weather cooperates, we'll eat outside tonight.

note: Also spelled co-operate, mostly in British English. "If the weather cooperates" is a common informal expression.

senses.def: involving people or groups working together toward a shared aim
examples: The research was a cooperative effort between three universities.
The countries launched a cooperative program to clean up the river.

senses.def: willing to help and do what people ask
examples: The staff at the hotel were very cooperative when we lost our keys.
Most witnesses were cooperative, but one refused to talk.

senses.def: a business or farm owned and run by the people who work in it or use it
examples: The farmers formed a cooperative to sell their coffee directly.

note: Informally shortened to "co-op" for the noun (a food co-op, a co-op apartment).

senses.def: to organize the different parts of an activity and the people involved so that they work well together
examples: She coordinated the relief effort after the flood.
We need someone to coordinate the volunteers on race day.

senses.tr: (hareket, renk vb.) uyum sağlamak, uyumlu hale getirmek
senses.def: to make body movements work well together, or to make colors or clothes match
examples: Young children find it hard to coordinate their hand and eye movements.
She always coordinates her scarf with her shoes.

senses.def: one of a pair of numbers that show the exact position of a point on a map or graph
examples: The pilot radioed the coordinates of the crash site.

note: The verb ends in /eɪt/; the noun "coordinate" usually ends in /ət/.

senses.def: the organizing of people or groups so that they work together efficiently
examples: Better coordination between agencies could have prevented the disaster.
The event required close coordination with city officials.

senses.def: the ability to control your body so that different parts move well together
examples: Dancing is a great way to improve balance and coordination.
Too much alcohol affects your coordination.

senses.def: a person whose job is to organize an activity and the people involved in it
examples: The wedding coordinator made sure everything ran on time.
Contact the program coordinator if you have questions about the schedule.

senses.def: (informal) a police officer
examples: A cop pulled him over for running a red light.
The neighbors called the cops because the party was too loud.

note: Informal but very common in American English. "Good cop, bad cop" describes two people using friendly and tough methods together.

senses.tr: başa çıkmak, üstesinden gelmek, baş etmek
senses.def: to deal successfully with a difficult situation or problem
examples: She's coping well with the stress of her new job.
The hospital couldn't cope with the sudden rise in patients.

note: Almost always followed by "with": cope with pressure, NOT "cope pressure".

senses.def: a soft reddish-brown metal used for electrical wires, pipes, and coins
examples: Thieves stripped the copper wiring from the empty building.
Copper prices rose sharply as demand for electric cars grew.

senses.def: having a reddish-brown color like the metal
examples: She has long copper hair and green eyes.

note: In British slang, "copper" also means a police officer; Americans say "cop".

senses.def: something made to look exactly like something else, or one example of a book, newspaper, etc.
examples: Please keep a copy of the receipt for your records.
The novel sold over a million copies in its first year.

senses.def: to make something that is exactly the same as something else
examples: Copy the file onto a USB drive before you reinstall the system.
He copied the address from the envelope.

senses.def: to behave like someone else, or to cheat by using another person's work
examples: Kids often copy what they see their parents do.
The teacher caught two students copying during the exam.

senses.def: the legal right to be the only one who can publish, copy, or perform a piece of creative work
examples: The band sued the website for copyright infringement.
Who holds the copyright on these photographs?

note: Spelled with -right, not -write: it is about the right to copy.

senses.def: the most important or central part of something
examples: Trust is at the core of any good relationship.
The core of the problem is a lack of funding.

senses.def: the hard center of some fruits, or the central part of a planet
examples: He ate the apple and threw the core in the trash.
The Earth's core is extremely hot.

senses.def: most important; main or essential
examples: Honesty is one of the company's core values.
Math and reading are core subjects in every school.

note: "To the core" means completely: "She was shocked to the core."

senses.def: the place where two sides, edges, or streets meet
examples: There's a coffee shop on the corner of Main and Fifth.
Put the lamp in the corner of the room.

senses.def: a difficult situation that is hard to escape from
examples: The company has backed itself into a corner with these promises.

senses.def: to trap a person or animal so they cannot escape
examples: Reporters cornered the senator as he left the building.

note: "Cut corners" = do something cheaply or carelessly. "Around the corner" can also mean "very soon".

senses.def: connected with a large company or companies in general
examples: She left her corporate job to open a bakery.
Critics say corporate interests have too much influence on politics.

note: "Climb the corporate ladder" means to get promoted step by step inside a company.

senses.def: a large business company, especially one that is legally treated as a single unit
examples: He works for a multinational corporation with offices in 40 countries.
Large corporations often pay lower tax rates than small businesses.

senses.def: accurate or true, with no mistakes
examples: Is this the correct address for the restaurant?
You're correct: the meeting was moved to Thursday.

senses.def: right or suitable for a particular situation
examples: What's the correct way to address a judge in court?

senses.def: to make something right by fixing its mistakes, or to point out someone's mistake
examples: The teacher corrected our essays over the weekend.
Correct me if I'm wrong, but didn't you say ten o'clock?

senses.def: a change that makes something more accurate or removes a mistake
examples: The newspaper printed a correction the next day.
I made a few corrections to your report in red.

senses.def: a short drop in prices after a period of rising, especially on the stock market
examples: Analysts expect a market correction after months of rapid growth.

note: In American English, a "correctional facility" is a prison.

senses.def: in a way that is accurate or right, with no mistakes
examples: Make sure the form is filled out correctly before you submit it.
If I remember correctly, the store closes at nine.

senses.tr: ilişkili olmak, bağlantılı olmak, korelasyon göstermek
senses.def: if two things correlate, they are closely connected and one changes when the other changes
examples: Income levels correlate strongly with life expectancy.
Researchers found that screen time correlated with poor sleep in teenagers.

note: Academic word. Remember: things that correlate are not necessarily causing each other.

senses.def: a connection between two things in which one changes as the other changes
examples: There is a strong correlation between smoking and lung disease.
The study found no correlation between coffee intake and memory.

note: Common phrase: "correlation does not imply causation" (a link does not prove one thing causes the other).

senses.def: to match something or be similar or equal to it
examples: Your story doesn't correspond with what the witness said.
Each number on the map corresponds to a hiking trail.

senses.def: to exchange letters or emails with someone regularly
examples: The two scientists corresponded for years before they finally met.

senses.def: the letters or emails that someone sends and receives, or the activity of writing them
examples: The museum holds her private correspondence from the 1940s.
Please keep all correspondence with the insurance company.

senses.def: a close connection or similarity between two things
examples: There is little correspondence between what he says and what he does.

note: Uncountable when it means letters: "a lot of correspondence", not "correspondences".

senses.def: a journalist who reports on a particular subject or from a particular country
examples: She worked as a war correspondent in the Middle East for ten years.
Our White House correspondent has the latest details.

senses.tr: karşılık gelen, buna bağlı, aynı dönemdeki
senses.def: matching or connected with something just mentioned
examples: Sales rose 12% compared with the corresponding period last year.
Higher prices led to a corresponding drop in demand.

senses.def: a long narrow passage inside a building, with doors to rooms on each side
examples: His office is at the end of the corridor on the left.
Students waited in the corridor outside the exam room.

senses.def: a long strip of land or air space linking two places, often used for travel or trade
examples: The new rail line will serve the busy Boston–Washington corridor.

collocations: at the end of the corridor
note: In American homes and schools, "hallway" or "hall" is more common than "corridor".

senses.def: using power dishonestly or illegally, especially by taking money
examples: The corrupt official accepted bribes from construction firms.
Voters were tired of a corrupt system that favored the rich.

senses.def: (of computer data) damaged so that it cannot be used correctly
examples: I couldn't open the attachment because the file was corrupt.

senses.def: to make someone dishonest or immoral
examples: Power corrupts, and absolute power corrupts absolutely.

senses.def: dishonest or illegal behavior, especially by people in positions of power
examples: The mayor was arrested on corruption charges.
Corruption in the police force had become a serious problem.

senses.def: the amount of money needed to buy, make, or do something
examples: The cost of living in this city has doubled in ten years.
The company will cover the cost of your travel.

senses.def: something lost or given up in order to achieve something
examples: He finished the race, but at the cost of a serious knee injury.

senses.def: to have a particular price, or to cause the loss of something
examples: How much does it cost to fix the roof?
One careless mistake cost him his job.

note: Irregular verb: cost – cost – cost. "At all costs" means "no matter what happens".

senses.def: costing a lot of money, often more than you want to pay
examples: Replacing the old pipes will be a costly repair.
Long court cases are costly for both sides.

senses.def: causing serious problems or losses
examples: The goalkeeper's costly error gave the other team the win.

note: "Costly" is an adjective, not an adverb. Say "a costly mistake" or "it proved costly".

senses.def: clothes worn to look like someone or something else, for a party, play, or film
examples: My son wants to wear a dinosaur costume for Halloween.
The actors were still in costume after the show.

senses.def: the typical clothes of a particular country or historical period
examples: Dancers in traditional costume performed at the festival.

note: In American English a "costume party" is what the British call a "fancy-dress party". Turkish "kostüm" (suit) is "suit" in English.

senses.def: a small house, especially in the countryside or by a lake
examples: We rented a cottage by the lake for the summer.
The old stone cottage had a garden full of roses.

note: "Cottage cheese" is a soft white cheese similar to Turkish lor peyniri.

senses.def: a plant grown in warm places for the soft white fibers around its seeds
examples: The region grows cotton, wheat, and corn.
Cotton was the main crop in the American South for centuries.

senses.def: cloth or thread made from this plant
examples: I prefer cotton shirts in hot weather because they breathe.

note: A small ball of cotton for cleaning skin is a "cotton ball" in American English; "cotton wool" is British.

senses.def: used as the past form of "can" to talk about ability or permission in the past
examples: She could speak three languages by the age of ten.
We couldn't hear anything because of the noise.

senses.def: used to say that something is possible
examples: It could rain later, so take an umbrella.
That could be the reason he hasn't called.

senses.def: used to make polite requests or suggestions
examples: Could you pass me the salt, please?
You could ask your brother to help you move.

note: "Could have + past participle" = a past possibility that didn't happen: "You could have told me!" The "l" is silent.

senses.def: a group of elected people who govern a city, town, or county
examples: The city council voted to build a new public library.
She was elected to the town council last year.

senses.def: a group of people chosen to give advice, make rules, or manage an organization
examples: The UN Security Council met to discuss the crisis.
The student council organized a fundraiser for the flood victims.

note: Don't confuse with "counsel" (advice, or a lawyer), which sounds the same.

senses.def: an elected member of a city, town, or county council
examples: Local councillors met with residents to discuss the new parking rules.
She served as a councillor for twelve years before running for mayor.

note: British spelling. American English uses "councilor" or, more often, "council member" / "councilman" / "councilwoman".

senses.def: professional advice and support given to help someone deal with personal problems
examples: After the accident, he went to counselling to deal with his anxiety.
The school offers free counselling to students going through a hard time.

note: British spelling. American English spells it "counseling" (one l).

senses.def: a person trained to give advice and support to people with personal or practical problems
examples: My high school counselor helped me choose a college.
She sees a counselor once a week to talk about her divorce.

senses.def: a person who looks after children at a summer camp
examples: He worked as a camp counselor every summer during college.

note: American spelling; British is "counsellor". Don't confuse with "councilor" (council member).

senses.def: to say numbers in order, or to find the total number of things
examples: Close your eyes and count to twenty.
Election workers counted the votes late into the night.

senses.def: to be important, or to be accepted as valid
examples: Every second counts in an emergency.
The goal didn't count because he was offside.

senses.def: an act of counting, or the total number found by counting
examples: At the last count, more than 300 people had signed up.
I lost count of how many times he called.

note: "Count on someone" = rely on them: "You can always count on me."

senses.def: a long flat surface where customers are served in a shop or bank, or a work surface in a kitchen
examples: Please pay at the counter before you leave.
She left the groceries on the kitchen counter.

senses.tr: karşılık vermek, cevap vermek, karşı koymak
senses.def: to respond to criticism or an attack by arguing against it or acting against it
examples: The minister countered that the new tax would only affect the wealthy.
The company cut prices to counter the threat from cheaper rivals.

note: "Over-the-counter" medicine can be bought without a prescription. "Run counter to" means "be opposite to".

senses.def: a person or thing with the same role or function as another in a different place or situation
examples: The foreign minister met his French counterpart in Paris.
Women still earn less than their male counterparts in many industries.

senses.def: very many; too many to be counted
examples: I've told you countless times to lock the door.
The vaccine has saved countless lives.

senses.def: an area of land with its own government and borders, or the people who live there
examples: Japan is one of the safest countries in the world.
The whole country was watching the final game.

senses.def: land outside towns and cities, with fields and farms
examples: They sold their apartment and moved to the country.

senses.def: a style of popular music from the southern and western US
examples: My dad only listens to country on long road trips.

note: "The country" (with "the") often means rural areas, not the nation.

senses.def: land outside towns and cities, with fields, farms, and woods
examples: We spent the weekend biking through the Vermont countryside.
The train passed through miles of beautiful open countryside.

note: Uncountable: "the countryside", never "a countryside" or "countrysides".

senses.tr: ilçe, bölge, idari bölge (ABD'de eyaletin alt birimi)
senses.def: an area within a state or country that has its own local government
examples: Los Angeles County has more people than many US states.
The county fair is held every August.

note: In the US, a county is the level between a city and a state. Don't confuse with "country".

senses.def: a sudden, illegal, often violent seizure of power from a government
examples: The president was overthrown in a military coup.
The army attempted a coup but failed within hours.

senses.def: a surprising and impressive success
examples: Signing such a famous designer was a real coup for the small company.

note: Pronounced /kuː/: the p is silent. Short for French "coup d'état".

senses.def: two, or a small number of people or things
examples: I'll be ready in a couple of minutes.
We stayed at the beach for a couple of days.

senses.def: two people who are married or in a romantic relationship
examples: A young couple moved into the apartment next door.
They've been a couple since high school.

senses.def: to join or combine one thing with another
examples: Low wages, coupled with high rents, are pushing families out of the city.

note: In casual American speech, "a couple" often means "about two or three", not exactly two. "Coupled with" = together with.

senses.def: the ability to do something dangerous or difficult, or to face pain, without fear
examples: It took a lot of courage to speak out against her boss.
The firefighters showed great courage during the rescue.

senses.def: a series of lessons or lectures on a subject
examples: She's taking an online course in web design.
This course covers American history from 1865 to today.

senses.def: the direction something moves in, or the way a situation develops
examples: The storm changed course and headed out to sea.
The discovery changed the course of medical history.

senses.def: one part of a meal served at a time
examples: For the main course, I'll have the grilled salmon.

note: "Of course" = certainly. Also: golf course, race course. Don't confuse with "coarse" (rough), which sounds the same.

senses.def: the place where legal cases are judged, or the judge and jury who decide them
examples: The case will go to court next month.
The court ruled that the law was unconstitutional.

senses.def: an area marked for playing games like tennis or basketball
examples: The kids play basketball on the court behind the school.

senses.def: to try to win someone's support, or to act in a way that risks something bad
examples: Both candidates are courting young voters.
Driving that fast is courting disaster.

note: "Settle out of court" = reach an agreement before a judge decides.

senses.def: polite behavior that shows respect for other people
examples: He didn't even have the courtesy to call and say he'd be late.
Treat every customer with courtesy, even when they're rude.

senses.def: used to say who gave or allowed something, often for free
examples: The photos appear courtesy of the city museum.
Drinks were provided courtesy of the hotel.

note: A "courtesy car" or "courtesy shuttle" is provided free by a business.

senses.def: a child of your aunt or uncle
examples: My cousin and I grew up in the same neighborhood.
We have dozens of cousins on my mother's side.

note: English uses one word for all four Turkish relations (amca, dayı, hala, teyze çocuğu). Pronounced /ˈkʌzn/, like "buzz-n".

senses.def: to put something over or on something to hide, protect, or decorate it
examples: Cover the pot and let the rice cook for 15 minutes.
Snow covered the whole town overnight.

senses.def: to include or deal with a subject, or to report on an event
examples: The exam will cover chapters one through five.
She covered the election for a national newspaper.

senses.def: to be enough money to pay for something, or to protect someone with insurance
examples: My salary barely covers the rent.
Does your insurance cover dental care?

senses.def: something that goes over or protects something, or a place that gives shelter
examples: Don't judge a book by its cover.
When the shooting started, everyone ran for cover.

note: "Cover for someone" = do their work while they're away. "Cover up" = hide a mistake or crime.

senses.def: the way news or sports events are reported on TV, radio, or in newspapers
examples: The trial received wide coverage in the national media.
Live coverage of the game starts at seven.

senses.def: the amount of protection an insurance policy gives, or the area a service reaches
examples: Many part-time workers don't have health coverage.
There's no cell phone coverage up in the mountains.

senses.def: having a layer of something on it
examples: The kids came home covered in mud.
The hills were covered with wildflowers.

senses.def: having a roof or cover over it
examples: We waited for the bus in a covered shelter.

senses.def: a large female farm animal kept for milk or meat
examples: The farmer milks the cows twice a day.
A herd of cows was blocking the country road.

note: "Cash cow" = a product that makes steady profit. "Holy cow!" is an informal exclamation of surprise.

senses.def: a thin line on a surface where it has broken but not split apart
examples: There's a long crack in the windshield.
Water was leaking through a crack in the ceiling.

senses.def: to break without separating into pieces, or to break something open
examples: The ice cracked under his weight.
Crack two eggs into a bowl and whisk them.

senses.def: to solve a difficult problem or code, or to lose control under pressure
examples: Police finally cracked the case after six months.
He cracked under the pressure of the final interview.

note: "Crack down on" = deal with something much more strictly. "Crack a joke" = tell a joke.

senses.def: an activity that needs skill in making things by hand
examples: The market sells local crafts like pottery and woven baskets.
Woodworking is a craft that takes years to master.

senses.def: the skills needed for a particular job or art
examples: She spent years perfecting her craft as a writer.

senses.def: to make something carefully and skillfully
examples: Each chair is crafted by hand from solid oak.
The speech was carefully crafted to appeal to young voters.

note: "Craft" can also mean a boat or aircraft; the plural is still "craft". "Crafty" means clever in a dishonest way.

senses.def: an accident in which a vehicle hits something
examples: Three people were injured in a car crash on the highway.
Investigators are still looking into the cause of the plane crash.

senses.def: to hit something violently, or to make a vehicle do this
examples: He crashed his dad's car into a tree.
The helicopter crashed shortly after takeoff.

senses.def: to suddenly stop working, or to suddenly lose a lot of value
examples: My laptop crashed and I lost the whole document.
Stock prices crashed after the bank collapsed.

note: A "crash course" is a short, intensive course. Informally, "crash" can mean sleep somewhere: "Can I crash on your couch?"

senses.def: to move on your hands and knees, or with your body close to the ground
examples: The baby is just starting to crawl.
Soldiers crawled under the barbed wire.

senses.def: (of traffic or time) to move very slowly
examples: Traffic crawled along the freeway for an hour.

senses.def: to be full of people, insects, or other things moving around
examples: The kitchen floor was crawling with ants.

note: "Make your skin crawl" = make you feel disgusted or afraid. As a noun, "crawl" is also a swimming stroke.

senses.def: not sensible; very foolish or strange
examples: It's crazy to drive in this snow without proper tires.
That's the craziest idea I've ever heard.

senses.def: mentally ill (offensive), or very angry or upset
examples: The noise from the construction is driving me crazy.

senses.def: very enthusiastic about or in love with someone or something
examples: My nephew is crazy about dinosaurs.
He's crazy about her.

note: Informal. Using it to mean "mentally ill" can be offensive. "Like crazy" = very much or very fast.

senses.def: the thick fatty part of milk, used in cooking or on desserts
examples: Do you take cream in your coffee?
She served the strawberries with whipped cream.

senses.def: a thick substance you put on your skin
examples: Rub some cream on your hands to stop them from cracking.
The doctor gave me an antibiotic cream for the cut.

senses.def: having a pale yellowish-white color
examples: They painted the living room walls cream.

note: "The cream of the crop" = the best people or things in a group. Americans say "sunscreen" more than "sun cream".

senses.def: to make something new exist or happen
examples: The new factory will create 500 jobs.
Click here to create a new account.

senses.def: to cause a particular situation, feeling, or impression
examples: The delay created a lot of confusion at the airport.
Soft lighting helps create a relaxing atmosphere.

senses.def: the act or process of making something new or causing it to exist
examples: The plan focuses on job creation in rural areas.
Since its creation in 1995, the charity has helped thousands of families.

senses.def: something new that someone has made, especially something original or artistic
examples: The chef's latest creation is a chocolate and chili dessert.

senses.def: the making of the world by God, or the whole world and everything in it
examples: Many cultures have their own stories about the creation of the world.

senses.def: using imagination and skill to produce new ideas or works of art
examples: She's a very creative person who's always making something.
We need some creative solutions to cut costs.

senses.def: connected with producing art, writing, music, or design
examples: He teaches creative writing at the community college.

note: "Creative accounting" is a polite way of saying dishonest bookkeeping.

senses.def: the ability to use imagination and skill to produce new ideas or works of art
examples: The new office layout is designed to encourage creativity.
Strict rules can kill children's creativity.

senses.def: a person who has made, invented, or started something
examples: The show's creator also wrote most of the episodes.
Content creators earn money from ads on their videos.

senses.def: God, as the maker of the world
examples: Many religions believe in one Creator of all things.

senses.def: any living thing that can move, such as an animal, or an imaginary being
examples: The deep ocean is full of strange creatures we know little about.
The movie is about a creature that lives under the lake.

senses.def: a person of a particular type
examples: My grandfather is a creature of habit: same breakfast every day for forty years.

note: "Creature comforts" = things that make life physically comfortable, like good food and a warm bed.

senses.def: the quality that makes people believe or trust someone or something
examples: The scandal badly damaged the senator's credibility.
Citing reliable sources gives your essay more credibility.

senses.def: able to be believed or trusted
examples: Police received a credible threat against the school.
The witness gave a credible account of what happened.

senses.def: good enough to be taken seriously or likely to succeed
examples: She is the only credible candidate running against the mayor.

note: Don't confuse with "credulous" (too ready to believe things). "Incredible" now usually means "amazing".

senses.def: an arrangement to receive goods or money now and pay for them later
examples: They bought the furniture on credit.
Small businesses are struggling to get credit from banks.

senses.def: praise or approval for something good that someone has done
examples: She never gets credit for all the extra work she does.
To his credit, he admitted the mistake right away.

senses.def: a unit that measures a completed part of a college course
examples: You need 120 credits to graduate.

senses.tr: (hesaba) para yatırmak, alacak kaydetmek; (başarıyı) birine atfetmek
senses.def: to add money to a bank account, or to say that someone deserves praise for something
examples: The refund will be credited to your account within five days.
She credits her coach with saving her career.

note: "The credits" are the list of names at the end of a film. "Take credit for" = claim you did something.

senses.def: to move slowly and quietly so that you are not seen or heard
examples: He crept upstairs so he wouldn't wake the baby.
The cat crept toward the bird in the grass.

senses.def: to increase or change slowly, often without being noticed
examples: Prices have been creeping up all year.
A few errors crept into the final report.

senses.def: (informal) an unpleasant person, especially one who makes others feel uncomfortable
examples: Some creep kept staring at her on the train.

note: Irregular verb: creep – crept – crept. "Give someone the creeps" = make them feel uneasy.

senses.def: all the people who work on a ship, plane, or train
examples: The plane had 150 passengers and six crew on board.
The crew abandoned the ship when the fire spread.

senses.def: a group of people who work together on a particular job
examples: A film crew was shooting a scene on our street.
Road crews worked through the night to clear the snow.

note: "Crew" is a group noun; you can say "the crew is" or "the crew are". American English prefers "is".

senses.def: an illegal act, or illegal activities in general
examples: He was arrested for a crime he didn't commit.
Violent crime has fallen in most big cities.

senses.def: something that seems wrong, wasteful, or shameful
examples: It's a crime to throw away all that good food.

note: You "commit" a crime, not "do" or "make" one.

senses.def: a person who has committed a crime
examples: The police caught the criminals at the border.
Many career criminals start offending as teenagers.

senses.def: connected with crime or with the laws dealing with crime
examples: He has no criminal record.
The company is facing a criminal investigation.

senses.def: (informal) morally very wrong or shocking
examples: It's criminal how much they charge for a cup of coffee here.

senses.def: a time of great difficulty or danger when important decisions must be made
examples: The country is in the middle of an economic crisis.
Thousands fled during the refugee crisis.

senses.def: a time of serious personal or emotional difficulty
examples: At 45, he went through a midlife crisis and bought a motorcycle.

note: Plural: crises /ˈkraɪsiːz/.

senses.def: standards used to judge or decide something (plural of criterion)
examples: Applicants must meet strict criteria to receive the scholarship.
What criteria do you use to choose a new employee?

note: Criteria is plural: "these criteria are". The singular is "criterion", though many people wrongly say "a criteria".

senses.def: a standard or principle used to judge something or make a decision
examples: Price was not the only criterion we considered when buying the car.
The main criterion for admission is academic performance.

note: Irregular plural: criterion → criteria.

senses.def: a person whose job is to write opinions about books, films, music, food, etc.
examples: The film was praised by critics but failed at the box office.
She works as a restaurant critic for a city magazine.

senses.def: a person who openly says they disapprove of someone or something
examples: Critics of the plan say it will raise taxes for the middle class.

note: Trap for Turkish speakers: "critic" is a person; "kritik" (criticism, review) is "criticism" or "critique".

senses.def: saying what you think is bad about someone or something
examples: The report was highly critical of the hospital's management.
Why are you always so critical of my friends?

senses.def: extremely important because the result depends on it
examples: The next 48 hours are critical for the investigation.
Clean water is critical to public health.

senses.def: very serious or dangerous, especially in illness
examples: Two victims are in critical condition at the hospital.

senses.def: carefully judging the good and bad qualities of something
examples: The course teaches students critical thinking skills.

note: "Critical acclaim" = praise from critics.

senses.def: in a way that judges carefully or points out faults
examples: Students should learn to read news sources critically.
He spoke critically about the government's response.

senses.tr: ağır şekilde, ciddi biçimde; son derece
senses.def: seriously or dangerously, or extremely
examples: Two people were critically injured in the fire.
It is critically important to finish on time.

senses.def: by critics who review books, films, etc.
examples: The album was critically acclaimed but sold poorly.

senses.def: the act of saying what is wrong with someone or something, or a comment that does this
examples: The new policy has faced strong criticism from teachers.
She doesn't take criticism well.

senses.def: the work of judging and discussing books, art, music, etc.
examples: He studied literary criticism in graduate school.

note: "Constructive criticism" is helpful, meant to improve something.

senses.def: to say what you think is bad or wrong about someone or something
examples: The mayor was criticized for ignoring the housing crisis.
Stop criticizing everything I cook!

note: American spelling with -ize; British also uses "criticise". Pattern: criticize someone FOR something.

senses.def: a careful written or spoken analysis of the good and bad points of something
examples: The book offers a sharp critique of modern consumer culture.
Each student must write a critique of a classmate's essay.

senses.def: to analyze and judge the strengths and weaknesses of something
examples: The teacher critiqued our designs one by one.

note: More formal and academic than "criticism", and not necessarily negative.

senses.def: a plant grown in large amounts, especially for food
examples: Corn and soybeans are the main crops in Iowa.
The drought destroyed most of this year's crop.

senses.def: a group of people or things that appear at the same time
examples: This year's crop of graduates faces a tough job market.

senses.def: to cut off the edges of a picture, or to cut hair very short
examples: Crop the photo so only the two of us are in it.

note: Phrasal verb "crop up" = happen or appear unexpectedly: "Something cropped up at work."

senses.def: to go from one side of something to the other
examples: Look both ways before you cross the street.
Thousands of migrants try to cross the border every month.

senses.def: to come into your mind briefly, or to put one leg or arm over the other
examples: It never crossed my mind that she might be lying.
He sat back and crossed his arms.

senses.def: a mark (X or +), or the symbol of Christianity
examples: Put a cross next to the answers you're not sure about.
She wore a small gold cross around her neck.

senses.def: a mix of two different things, breeds, or types
examples: The dog is a cross between a poodle and a Labrador.

note: "Cross your fingers" = hope for luck. In British English, "cross" can also be an adjective meaning "annoyed".

senses.def: a large number of people gathered together in one place
examples: A crowd of fans waited outside the stadium.
The crowd cheered when the band came on stage.

senses.def: a particular group of people, especially friends with similar interests
examples: He started hanging out with the wrong crowd in high school.

senses.def: to gather together in large numbers, often filling a space
examples: Tourists crowded around the street performer.

senses.def: full of people, often too many
examples: The subway is always crowded during rush hour.
We couldn't find a table in the crowded restaurant.

senses.def: full of competitors or things
examples: The startup is entering a crowded market for food delivery apps.

senses.def: a circle of gold and jewels that a king or queen wears on the head
examples: The queen's crown is kept in a museum in London.
She wore a paper crown at her birthday party.

senses.def: the title of champion in a sports competition
examples: The team is hoping to defend its crown next season.

senses.def: to officially make someone a king or queen, or to make something complete with a final success
examples: She was crowned Miss America in 2019.
Winning the final crowned a perfect season.

note: A "crown" is also a cap a dentist puts on a damaged tooth. "Crowning achievement" = the best thing someone has done.

senses.def: extremely important because it affects what happens next
examples: Getting enough sleep is crucial for good health.
The goalkeeper made a crucial save in the final minute.

senses.def: in a natural state, before being processed
examples: The price of crude oil fell below $70 a barrel.
Crude rubber is treated with chemicals to make tires.

senses.def: simple and not made or done with much skill or detail
examples: The prisoners made a crude knife from a spoon.
This is only a crude estimate of the costs.

senses.def: rude and offensive, especially about sex
examples: He made a crude joke that embarrassed everyone at dinner.

note: In news, "crude" alone often means crude oil: "Crude rose 2% on Monday."

senses.def: wanting to cause pain or suffering to others, or causing great suffering
examples: It's cruel to keep a dog chained up all day.
Losing in the last second was a cruel blow for the team.

note: "You have to be cruel to be kind" = sometimes hurting someone is for their own good.

senses.def: a vacation on a large ship that visits several places
examples: My parents went on a Caribbean cruise for their anniversary.
The cruise stops in five ports along the coast.

senses.def: to travel by ship for pleasure, or to move at a steady comfortable speed
examples: We cruised around the Greek islands for a week.
The plane was cruising at 35,000 feet.

senses.def: to win or succeed easily
examples: The home team cruised to a 5-0 victory.

senses.def: to press something so hard that it breaks or loses its shape
examples: Crush two cloves of garlic and add them to the pan.
His car was crushed by a falling tree.

senses.def: to defeat someone or something completely, often using force
examples: The army crushed the rebellion within days.
We crushed them 42 to 7.

senses.def: to make someone feel extremely sad or disappointed
examples: She was crushed when she didn't get the part.

senses.def: a strong but usually short-lived romantic feeling for someone
examples: I had a huge crush on my English teacher in eighth grade.

note: "Have a crush on someone" is very common, informal, and not serious love.

senses.def: to produce tears because you are sad, hurt, or very emotional
examples: The baby cried all night.
She cried when she read her father's letter.

senses.def: to shout something loudly
examples: "Watch out!" she cried, as the car came toward us.

senses.def: a loud sound expressing a strong feeling, or a shout
examples: We heard a cry for help from the river.
The crowd let out a cry of joy.

note: "A far cry from" = very different from. "Crying shame" = a very sad or unfair situation.
