examples: Strict rules govern the use of personal data.
Her decisions are governed by fear rather than logic.

senses.def: the way a country, company, or organization is controlled and how decisions are made
examples: Investors are demanding better corporate governance.
The report criticized the poor governance of the city's schools.

note: Formal; common in business, politics, and academic writing.

senses.def: the group of people who officially control a country or state
examples: The government announced new measures to reduce inflation.
Many people don't trust the government to protect their privacy.

senses.def: the system or activity of governing a country
examples: She studied government and economics in college.
The country moved toward democratic government.

note: In American English "the administration" often means the president's government. Pronounced /ˈɡʌvərmənt/ in fast speech.

senses.def: the elected head of a US state, or the official head of a region or colony
examples: The governor declared a state of emergency after the floods.
She is running for governor of Texas.

senses.def: a person who leads or is on the board of an institution such as a central bank
examples: The central bank governor warned that rates could rise again.

senses.def: to take hold of something suddenly and roughly
examples: He grabbed my arm to stop me from falling.
The thief grabbed her bag and ran.

senses.def: to quickly get or take something, often because you are busy
examples: Let's grab a coffee before the meeting.
I'll grab a seat near the front.

senses.def: to get someone's attention or interest
examples: The headline was designed to grab readers' attention.

note: "Up for grabs" means available for anyone to try to get: The top job is up for grabs.

senses.def: a smooth, attractive way of moving, or a calm and polite way of behaving
examples: The dancer moved across the stage with grace.
She accepted defeat with grace and congratulated her rival.

senses.def: extra time allowed before something must be done or paid
examples: The bank gave us a ten-day grace period to pay the bill.

senses.def: in Christianity, God's kindness and love toward people
examples: They believe they were saved by the grace of God.

note: "Saving grace" = the one good thing about something bad. "Say grace" = pray before a meal.

senses.def: a letter or number given to show the quality of a student's work
examples: She got good grades in all her science classes.
What grade did you get on the history test?

senses.def: one of the school years in the US, from first to twelfth
examples: My son is in third grade this year.

senses.def: a level of quality, size, or rank
examples: The factory uses only high-grade steel.

senses.def: to give a mark to a student's work, or to sort things by quality
examples: The teacher spent the weekend grading essays.
Eggs are graded by size.

note: American: "grade" for both school marks and school year (British: "mark" and "year"). Turkish "sınıf" = grade, not "class".

senses.def: slowly and in small steps over a period of time
examples: The patient's condition gradually improved over the next few weeks.
Add the flour gradually, stirring all the time.

note: Opposite: suddenly, abruptly.

senses.def: a person who has completed a university degree, or (in the US) high school
examples: She is a graduate of Stanford Law School.
Many recent college graduates struggle to find jobs.

senses.def: to complete your studies and receive a degree or diploma
examples: He graduated from high school in 2019.
She graduated with honors in chemistry.

senses.def: relating to studies done after a first university degree
examples: He's applying to graduate school next fall.

note: Noun /ˈɡrædʒuət/, verb /ˈɡrædʒueɪt/. Say "graduate from a school", not "graduate a school" (a common Turkish-speaker error).

senses.def: the seeds of plants like wheat and rice used as food, or one such seed
examples: The country exports large amounts of grain.
Choose whole grain bread for more fiber.

senses.def: a very small piece of something like sand or salt, or a small amount of a quality
examples: There's a grain of sand in my shoe.
There's a grain of truth in what he said.

senses.def: the natural pattern of lines in wood or fabric
examples: Sand the wood in the direction of the grain.

note: "Take something with a grain of salt" (US) = don't completely believe it. "Go against the grain" = be unusual or unnatural for you.

senses.def: impressive in size, appearance, or importance
examples: The hotel has a grand staircase in the lobby.
They have grand plans to rebuild the city center.

senses.def: including everything; final
examples: The grand total came to over two thousand dollars.

senses.def: (informal) a thousand dollars
examples: He paid ten grand for that used car.

note: "Grand" meaning $1,000 never takes -s: "five grand".

senses.def: the father of your mother or father
examples: My grandfather taught me how to fish when I was six.
Her grandfather emigrated from Italy in the 1950s.

note: Informal: grandpa. To specify the side of the family, say maternal (mother's) or paternal (father's) grandfather.

senses.def: the mother of your mother or father
examples: My grandmother makes the best apple pie.
She was raised by her grandmother after her parents died.

note: Babaanne = paternal grandmother; anneanne = maternal grandmother. English uses one word for both.

senses.tr: büyükanne veya büyükbaba; (çoğul) büyükanne ve büyükbaba
senses.def: a parent of your father or mother
examples: We spend every Thanksgiving with my grandparents.
Many grandparents help take care of their grandchildren.

senses.def: money given by a government or organization for a particular purpose, such as research
examples: The lab received a federal grant to study climate change.
She applied for a grant to fund her documentary.

senses.def: to officially give or allow someone something they have asked for
examples: The judge granted him permission to leave the country.
She was granted asylum in Canada.

senses.def: to admit that something is true, especially before arguing a different point
examples: I grant that the plan is expensive, but it will save money long term.

note: "Take something/someone for granted" = not appreciate it because you expect it to always be there.

senses.def: related to drawings, images, and design, especially in printing or on screens
examples: She works as a graphic designer for an ad agency.
The novel was adapted into a graphic novel.

senses.def: showing or describing something unpleasant, especially violence or sex, in very clear detail
examples: The movie contains graphic violence.
He gave a graphic description of the accident.

senses.def: a picture, chart, or design, especially one on a computer screen
examples: The article includes a graphic showing the rise in prices.

senses.def: pictures, designs, and images, especially those made by computer
examples: The new video game has amazing graphics.
You'll need a powerful graphics card to run this software.

senses.def: to take and hold something firmly
examples: She grasped the rope with both hands.
He grasped my hand and shook it warmly.

senses.def: to understand something, especially something difficult
examples: It took me a while to grasp the main idea of the theory.
They failed to grasp how serious the situation was.

senses.def: understanding of a subject, or a firm hold on something
examples: She has a good grasp of French grammar.
Success is finally within our grasp.

senses.def: a common plant with thin green leaves that covers fields, parks, and lawns
examples: The kids were lying on the grass in the park.
Please keep off the grass.

note: "The grass is always greener on the other side" = other people's situations always seem better (Komşunun tavuğu komşuya kaz görünür).

senses.def: feeling or showing thanks because someone has helped you or been kind
examples: I'm really grateful for all your help with the move.
We'd be grateful if you could reply by Friday.

note: Grateful TO a person FOR a thing. "I would be grateful if…" is a polite formal request in emails.

senses.def: a place in the ground where a dead person is buried
examples: They put flowers on their mother's grave every spring.
He took the secret to his grave.

senses.def: very serious and worrying
examples: Officials expressed grave concern about the safety of the dam.
This is a grave mistake that could cost lives.

note: The adjective is formal. "Turn in his grave" = a dead person would be very upset about something happening now.

senses.def: the natural force that pulls objects toward each other and makes things fall to the ground
examples: The moon's gravity causes the ocean tides.
Astronauts train to work without gravity.

senses.def: how serious or important a situation is
examples: He didn't seem to understand the gravity of the situation.

senses.def: having the color of smoke or clouds on a rainy day; (of hair) turning white with age
examples: It was a cold, gray morning in November.
My dad's hair started going gray in his forties.

senses.def: the color between black and white
examples: The walls are painted a soft gray.

note: American spelling: gray; British: grey. "A gray area" = something unclear, not clearly right or wrong.

senses.def: very good, enjoyable, or useful
examples: We had a great time at the concert.
That's a great idea!

senses.def: very large in amount, size, or degree
examples: The new law will be of great importance to small businesses.
She lived to a great age.

senses.def: very important, famous, or talented
examples: He's one of the greatest writers of his generation.

senses.def: very much; to a large degree
examples: Your help is greatly appreciated.
Prices vary greatly from one region to another.

note: Formal. Usually used with verbs and past participles, not adjectives: say "very happy", not "greatly happy".

senses.def: having the color of grass and leaves
examples: She has bright green eyes.
The hills turn green after the spring rains.

senses.def: relating to protecting the environment
examples: The city is investing in green energy like wind and solar.
More companies are trying to go green.

senses.def: the color of grass, or an area of grass in a town or on a golf course
examples: The room was decorated in green and white.

note: "Give the green light" = give permission. "Green" can also mean inexperienced: He's still green.

senses.def: a glass building used for growing plants that need warmth and protection
examples: My aunt grows tomatoes in a small greenhouse behind the house.

senses.def: relating to gases that trap heat in the earth's atmosphere
examples: Cars and power plants produce large amounts of greenhouse gases.
The greenhouse effect is warming the planet.

senses.def: to say hello to someone or welcome them when they arrive
examples: The host greeted each guest at the door.
She greeted me with a warm hug.

senses.def: to react to something in a particular way
examples: The announcement was greeted with loud applause.
The news was greeted with anger by local residents.

senses.def: a pattern of straight lines that cross each other to form squares
examples: The streets of Manhattan are laid out in a grid.
Draw a grid on the paper before you start the chart.

senses.def: a network of power lines that carries electricity across an area
examples: The storm knocked out the power grid for three days.
They live off the grid, using solar panels and well water.

note: "Off the grid" = living without public electricity, or hard to contact.

senses.def: deep sadness, especially because someone has died
examples: She was overcome with grief after her husband's death.
Grief counselors were sent to the school after the accident.

senses.def: (informal) trouble or annoyance caused by someone
examples: My boss gave me a lot of grief for being late.

note: "Good grief!" expresses surprise or annoyance. Verb: grieve (for somebody).

senses.def: to smile widely, showing your teeth
examples: He grinned at me from across the room.
She was grinning from ear to ear after the exam.

senses.def: a wide smile
examples: He had a big grin on his face when he heard the news.

note: "Grin and bear it" = accept something unpleasant without complaining.

senses.def: to crush something into very small pieces or powder
examples: I grind fresh coffee beans every morning.
The meat was ground and made into burgers.

senses.def: to rub hard surfaces together, or to make something sharp or smooth by rubbing
examples: He grinds his teeth in his sleep.

senses.def: hard, boring work that continues for a long time
examples: After vacation, it's back to the daily grind.

note: Irregular: grind – ground – ground. "Grind to a halt" = slowly stop completely.

senses.def: a tight hold on something, or control or power over something
examples: Keep a firm grip on the handrail.
The country is in the grip of a severe drought.

senses.def: to hold something very tightly
examples: She gripped the steering wheel nervously.
The child gripped his mother's hand in the crowd.

senses.def: to strongly affect someone or hold their attention
examples: Fear gripped the town after the attacks.
The novel gripped me from the first page.

note: "Get a grip!" (informal) = calm down and control your emotions. "Gripping" = very exciting (a gripping story).

senses.def: a store that sells food and household items (often "grocery store")
examples: I'm stopping at the grocery store on my way home.
The neighborhood grocery closes at nine.

senses.def: (plural) food and other things you buy at a grocery store
examples: Can you help me carry the groceries inside?
We spend about $150 a week on groceries.

note: In American English "grocery store" usually means any supermarket.

senses.def: total, before taxes or costs are taken away
examples: Her gross salary is $80,000, but she takes home much less.
The country's gross domestic product grew by two percent.

senses.def: (informal) very unpleasant or disgusting
examples: Ew, that's gross! There's hair in my soup.

senses.def: very obvious and unacceptable
examples: The hospital was accused of gross negligence.

senses.def: to earn a total amount of money before costs are taken away
examples: The film grossed $300 million worldwide.

note: Opposite of gross (income) is net. "Gross" meaning disgusting is very common in informal American English.

senses.def: the solid surface of the earth, or the soil
examples: She dropped her keys on the ground.
The ground was too hard to dig after the frost.

senses.def: an area of land used for a purpose, or an area of knowledge or discussion
examples: The lecture covered a lot of ground in an hour.
The school sports grounds are open to the public on weekends.

senses.def: (usually plural) a reason for saying or doing something
examples: She was fired on the grounds of misconduct.
There are no grounds for complaint.

senses.def: to stop a plane from flying, or to punish a child by not letting them go out
examples: All flights were grounded because of the storm.
My parents grounded me for a week.

note: "Ground" is also the past form of "grind". "Common ground" = shared opinions or interests.

senses.def: a number of people or things that are together or connected in some way
examples: A group of students was waiting outside the library.
The children worked in small groups.

senses.def: a company that owns several other companies, or a band of musicians
examples: The hotel is owned by a large media group.

senses.def: to put people or things into groups, or to form a group
examples: The books are grouped by subject.
We grouped together under a tree to stay dry.

senses.def: to increase in size, number, or amount, or to become an adult
examples: The town has grown rapidly over the last ten years.
Children grow so fast at this age.

senses.def: to plant and take care of plants, or to let hair get longer
examples: We grow our own vegetables in the backyard.
He's growing a beard for the winter.

senses.def: to gradually become something
examples: The sky grew dark as the storm approached.
She's growing tired of his excuses.

note: Irregular: grow – grew – grown. "Grow up" = become an adult; "grow" alone is used for size and plants.

senses.def: the process of getting bigger or developing physically or mentally
examples: A healthy diet is important for a child's growth.
Travel can be a great opportunity for personal growth.

senses.def: an increase in amount, size, or economic activity
examples: The economy saw strong growth last quarter.
There has been rapid growth in online shopping.

senses.def: a lump of cells that grows abnormally in or on the body
examples: The doctor found a small growth on his skin.

senses.def: a firm promise that something will happen or be done
examples: There's no guarantee that the plan will work.
The laptop comes with a two-year guarantee.

senses.def: to promise that something will happen or that something is true
examples: We guarantee delivery within 24 hours.
Hard work doesn't guarantee success.

note: For products, American English often uses "warranty". Stress is on the last syllable: guar-an-TEE.

senses.def: a person whose job is to protect a place or people, or to stop prisoners from escaping
examples: A security guard checked our bags at the entrance.
The prisoner attacked a guard and tried to escape.

senses.def: the state of watching carefully to protect someone or be ready for danger
examples: Soldiers were on guard outside the palace.
The question caught me off guard.

senses.def: to protect a place or person from danger, or to watch someone to stop them escaping
examples: Two dogs guard the farm at night.
She closely guards her privacy.

note: "Guard against something" = try to prevent it. "Guarded" = careful not to show feelings (a guarded response).

senses.def: a member of a small, unofficial armed group that fights against a government or army
examples: The guerrillas hid in the mountains and attacked army convoys.
Thousands of guerrillas laid down their weapons under the peace deal.

note: Also used as an adjective: "guerrilla marketing" = cheap, surprising advertising methods.

senses.def: to give an answer or opinion without knowing all the facts
examples: Can you guess how old she is?
I guessed the answer correctly.

senses.def: (informal, I guess) used to say you think or suppose something is true
examples: I guess we should leave before the traffic gets bad.
It's not perfect, but I guess it'll do.

senses.def: an attempt to give an answer when you are not sure
examples: My guess is that he won't come.
Take a guess — you might be right.

collocations: your guess is as good as mine
note: "I guess" is very common in American speech and means "I think/suppose". "Guess what?" introduces surprising news.

senses.def: a person you have invited to your home or to an event
examples: We're having twenty guests for dinner on Saturday.
Wedding guests started arriving at noon.

senses.def: a person staying at a hotel, or someone invited to appear on a TV or radio show
examples: Hotel guests can use the pool for free.
Tonight's guest is a famous chef.

note: "Be my guest" = go ahead, you're welcome to do it.

senses.def: helpful advice or information, usually from someone with more experience
examples: Students can get career guidance from the school counselor.
Under her guidance, the team improved quickly.

note: Uncountable: "some guidance", not "a guidance".

senses.def: a person who shows tourists or visitors around a place
examples: Our tour guide spoke four languages.
We hired a local guide to take us up the mountain.

senses.def: a book or document that gives information or instructions about something
examples: I bought a guide to the restaurants in Chicago.
The website has a step-by-step guide to setting up your account.

senses.def: to show someone the way, or to influence and direct someone's actions or decisions
examples: The nurse guided him gently to his seat.
Let your values guide your decisions.

senses.def: an official rule or piece of advice about how something should be done
examples: The government issued new guidelines on healthy eating.
Please follow the safety guidelines when using the equipment.

note: Usually plural.

senses.def: the bad feeling you have when you know you have done something wrong
examples: She felt a lot of guilt about missing her son's game.
He was overcome with guilt after lying to his friend.

senses.def: the fact of having broken a law or done something wrong
examples: The evidence proved his guilt beyond doubt.

note: "Guilt-trip somebody" (informal) = make someone feel guilty so they do what you want.

senses.def: feeling bad because you have done something wrong or failed to do something
examples: I feel guilty about not calling my mom more often.
He had a guilty look on his face.

senses.def: having broken a law, especially as decided by a court
examples: The jury found her guilty of fraud.
He pleaded guilty to drunk driving.

note: Guilty OF a crime; feel guilty ABOUT something. A "guilty pleasure" is something you enjoy but feel a little embarrassed about.

senses.def: a musical instrument with six strings that you play with your fingers or a pick
examples: He's been learning to play the guitar for two years.
She sang while her brother played guitar.

senses.def: a weapon that fires bullets
examples: The robber pointed a gun at the cashier.
The debate over gun control continues in Congress.

senses.def: a tool that forces out a substance using pressure
examples: Use a glue gun to attach the decorations.

note: "Jump the gun" = do something too early. "Stick to your guns" = refuse to change your opinion.

senses.def: the tube that food passes through after the stomach, or (informal) the stomach or belly
examples: Healthy gut bacteria help with digestion.
He got a punch in the gut.

senses.def: (plural, informal) the courage to do something difficult
examples: It takes guts to quit a stable job and start a business.

senses.def: based on feeling or instinct rather than reasoning
examples: My gut feeling is that we shouldn't trust him.
She made a gut decision and it paid off.

note: "Trust your gut" = follow your instinct. "Gutted" (British, informal) = very disappointed.

senses.def: (informal) a man
examples: He's a really nice guy once you get to know him.
Some guy at the store asked me for directions.

senses.def: (plural, informal) used to talk to or about a group of people, men or women
examples: Hey guys, are you ready to go?
Thanks, you guys, that was really helpful.

note: "You guys" is very common in American English for any group, including women.

senses.def: a room or building with equipment for physical exercise
examples: I go to the gym three times a week before work.
The school gym was turned into a shelter during the storm.

senses.def: physical education as a school subject
examples: We have gym on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

note: Short for gymnasium. In English, "gymnasium" is never a type of school as it is in some European languages.

senses.def: something you do often and regularly, often without thinking, and that can be hard to stop
examples: Smoking is a hard habit to break.
She's in the habit of checking her phone first thing in the morning.

note: Habit is personal; custom is shared by a society.

senses.def: the natural place where a type of animal or plant lives
examples: Deforestation is destroying the natural habitat of orangutans.
The wetlands provide a habitat for hundreds of bird species.

senses.def: to publicly praise someone or something as very good or important
examples: The new drug has been hailed as a major breakthrough.
Critics hailed her first novel as a masterpiece.

senses.def: to wave or call to a taxi or person to get their attention
examples: We hailed a cab outside the hotel.

senses.def: small balls of ice that fall from the sky like rain
examples: The hail damaged dozens of cars in the parking lot.

note: "Hail from" = come from a place (formal): She hails from Ohio. "A hail of bullets/criticism" = a lot at once.

senses.def: the mass of thin threads that grows on your head, or one of these threads on the body
examples: She has long, curly hair.
There's a hair in my soup!

note: Uncountable for all the hair on your head (Her hair is long), countable for single hairs. Not "hairs are long".

senses.def: one of two equal parts of something
examples: Cut the apple in half.
The team scored twice in the second half.

senses.def: an amount equal to half of something
examples: I'll be there in half an hour.
Half the students failed the test.

senses.def: an amount equal to half of a group or thing
examples: Only half of the guests showed up.
I've read about half of the book.

senses.def: partly; not completely
examples: The door was half open.
I was only half listening to what he said.

note: Plural: halves. Say "half an hour" (American also: a half hour). Verb: halve /hæv/.

senses.def: at the middle point between two places or during a period of time
examples: We stopped for lunch halfway between Boston and New York.
I fell asleep halfway through the movie.

senses.def: at or in the middle
examples: At the halfway point of the race, she was in third place.

note: "Meet somebody halfway" = compromise with them.

senses.def: a passage in a building with rooms on either side, or the area inside the front door
examples: The bathroom is at the end of the hall.
Leave your shoes in the hall.

senses.def: a large room or building used for meetings, concerts, or other public events
examples: The concert hall was completely full.
The town meeting will be held at City Hall.

note: In the US, "hall" usually means a corridor; "residence hall" = university dormitory.

senses.def: to stop, or to make something stop, especially suddenly or officially
examples: The government halted construction of the pipeline.
Production was halted after a safety inspection.

senses.def: a stop or pause in movement or progress
examples: The car came to a halt at the red light.
Traffic ground to a halt because of the accident.

note: More formal than "stop"; common in news. "Halting" = slow and hesitant (halting English).

senses.def: the part of the body at the end of the arm, with fingers and a thumb
examples: Wash your hands before dinner.
She raised her hand to ask a question.

senses.def: help with doing something
examples: Can you give me a hand with these boxes?
I could use a hand in the kitchen.

senses.def: one of the pointers on a clock
examples: The minute hand pointed to twelve.

senses.def: to pass or give something to someone using your hands
examples: Could you hand me that pen?
She handed in her report on Friday.

note: "On the one hand… on the other hand" compares two points. "Get out of hand" = become impossible to control.

senses.def: the amount of something you can hold in one hand
examples: He grabbed a handful of nuts from the bowl.

senses.def: a small number of people or things
examples: Only a handful of people showed up to the meeting.
A handful of companies control most of the market.

senses.tr: başa bela, zapt edilmesi zor kişi
senses.def: (informal) a person, especially a child, who is difficult to control
examples: Their three-year-old is a real handful.

senses.def: to deal with a situation, problem, person, or task
examples: The manager handled the complaint very professionally.
I can't handle this much stress.

senses.def: to touch, hold, or move something with your hands
examples: Please handle the glasses carefully.

senses.def: the part of a door, tool, or container that you hold to use it
examples: The handle on the suitcase broke at the airport.
Turn the door handle and push.

note: "Fly off the handle" = suddenly get very angry. "Get a handle on something" = begin to understand or control it.

senses.def: the way someone deals with a situation, problem, or person
examples: The mayor was criticized for her handling of the crisis.
The case requires careful handling.

senses.def: the act of touching or moving things, or how easily a vehicle can be controlled
examples: Food handling rules are strict in restaurants.
The new model has excellent handling on wet roads.

note: "Shipping and handling" (US) = the delivery fee added to an online order.

senses.def: useful and easy to use
examples: This app has a handy feature for splitting bills.
A flashlight can come in handy during a power outage.

senses.def: near and easy to reach
examples: Keep your passport handy at the airport.

senses.def: good at using your hands to fix or make things
examples: He's very handy around the house.

note: "Come in handy" = turn out to be useful. Not related to Turkish/German "handy" (mobile phone).

senses.def: to attach something at the top so the lower part is free, or to be attached this way
examples: Hang your coat on the hook by the door.
A beautiful painting hangs above the fireplace.

senses.def: to kill someone by putting a rope around their neck and letting them drop
examples: The prisoners were hanged at dawn.

senses.def: (hang out, informal) to spend time somewhere or with someone in a relaxed way
examples: We used to hang out at the mall after school.

note: Past: hung. But for executions: hanged. "Hang up" = end a phone call; "hang on" = wait; "get the hang of" = learn how.

senses.def: to take place, especially without being planned
examples: What happened at the meeting yesterday?
The accident happened just after midnight.

senses.def: (happen to) to affect someone or something
examples: What happened to your car?
I don't know what I'd do if something happened to you.

senses.def: (happen to do) to do or be something by chance
examples: I happened to see her at the airport.
Do you happen to know his phone number?

note: Never passive: say "It happened", not "It was happened". "Do you happen to…?" makes a question more polite.

senses.def: in a happy or cheerful way
examples: The children played happily in the garden.
They've been happily married for thirty years.

senses.def: willingly; with pleasure
examples: I'd happily drive you to the airport.

senses.def: used to say that something is lucky or fortunate
examples: Happily, no one was hurt in the fire.

senses.def: the feeling of being happy
examples: Money can't buy happiness.
Her face was full of happiness when she saw her family.

senses.def: feeling or showing pleasure
examples: She looked really happy at the party.
They had a happy childhood on the farm.

senses.def: satisfied with something, or willing to do something
examples: Are you happy with the new design?
I'd be happy to help you with your application.

senses.def: used in greetings for special occasions
examples: Happy birthday, Sarah!
Happy New Year, everyone!

senses.def: behavior that repeatedly annoys, threatens, or upsets someone
examples: She filed a complaint about sexual harassment at work.
Online harassment has become a serious problem for teenagers.

note: Two pronunciations in US English: /həˈræsmənt/ or /ˈhærəsmənt/. Spelled with one r, two s's.

senses.def: an area of water near the coast, protected by walls, where ships can stay safely
examples: Fishing boats were tied up in the harbor.
The city's harbor is one of the busiest in the world.

senses.def: to keep a feeling, belief, or secret in your mind for a long time
examples: She still harbors doubts about his honesty.

senses.def: to hide or protect someone, especially a criminal, or to contain something harmful
examples: He was accused of harboring a fugitive.
Dirty sponges can harbor bacteria.

note: American spelling: harbor; British: harbour.

senses.def: difficult to do, understand, or deal with
examples: The exam was much harder than I expected.
It's hard to believe it's already December.

senses.def: solid and firm; not easy to bend or break
examples: The bed in the hotel was too hard.

senses.def: with a lot of effort or force
examples: She worked hard to pay for college.
It was raining hard all night.

note: "Hard" is both adjective and adverb. "Hardly" is NOT the adverb of hard; it means "almost not".

senses.def: almost not; almost none
examples: I could hardly hear what she was saying.
We hardly ever go out to eat anymore.

senses.def: used to say that something is not true, likely, or reasonable
examples: It's hardly surprising that he quit after the way they treated him.
This is hardly the time to ask for a raise.

note: Already negative: say "I can hardly see", not "I can't hardly see". Not the adverb of "hard" ("work hard", not "work hardly").

senses.def: the physical parts of a computer or electronic system
examples: The problem is with the hardware, not the software.
Upgrading the hardware made the system much faster.

senses.def: tools and equipment used in the house and garden
examples: I bought some screws and nails at the hardware store.

senses.def: military weapons and vehicles
examples: The army displayed its latest military hardware in the parade.

senses.def: physical or mental damage or injury
examples: Too much sun can cause serious harm to your skin.
I'm sure he meant no harm by his comment.

senses.def: to hurt someone or damage something
examples: The chemicals could harm wildlife in the river.
No animals were harmed during the filming.

note: "There's no harm in asking" = it's fine to ask; nothing bad can happen.

senses.def: causing damage or injury, especially to health or the environment
examples: Smoking is harmful to your health.
The factory released harmful chemicals into the river.

note: Harmful TO something.

senses.def: a peaceful state in which people or things agree or work well together
examples: People of different religions live in harmony in the village.
We need to live in harmony with nature.

senses.def: a pleasant combination of musical notes played or sung together
examples: The choir sang in perfect harmony.

senses.def: cruel, severe, or unkind
examples: The judge gave him a harsh sentence.
Her boss was harsh in his criticism.

senses.def: (of conditions or weather) very difficult to live in
examples: Few plants can survive the harsh desert climate.
The refugees faced harsh winter conditions.

senses.def: unpleasantly strong, bright, or loud
examples: The harsh lighting in the office gives me headaches.

senses.def: the time when crops are gathered, or the crops gathered
examples: Farmers are busy during the harvest in September.
Heavy rains ruined this year's wheat harvest.

senses.def: to gather crops, or to collect something for use
examples: The grapes are harvested by hand.
Scientists harvested stem cells from the samples.

senses.def: a piece of clothing that you wear on your head
examples: Wear a hat — it's freezing outside.
He took off his hat when he entered the church.

note: "Hats off to somebody" = they deserve praise. "Keep it under your hat" = keep it secret.

senses.def: to dislike someone or something very much
examples: I hate waking up early on weekends.
She hates it when people are late.

senses.def: (I hate to) used to say politely that you are sorry to do something
examples: I hate to interrupt, but we need to leave now.

senses.def: a very strong feeling of dislike
examples: The attack was described as a hate crime.
There was hate in his eyes.

senses.def: a very strong feeling of dislike for someone or something
examples: The war left a legacy of hatred between the two groups.
He made no secret of his hatred for his former boss.

note: More formal than "hate" as a noun; often used for long-lasting hatred between groups.

senses.def: (of a ghost) to appear regularly in a place
examples: Locals say the old house is haunted by a woman in white.

senses.tr: aklından çıkmamak, rahat vermemek, peşini bırakmamak
senses.def: to keep upsetting or troubling someone for a long time
examples: Memories of the war haunted him for the rest of his life.
That bad decision came back to haunt her.

note: "Haunting" = beautiful and sad, hard to forget (a haunting melody).

senses.def: to own, hold, or possess something
examples: Do you have a car?
She has two brothers and a sister.

senses.def: used with nouns to describe actions or experiences, like eating, drinking, or taking part in something
examples: Let's have lunch at the new café.
We had a great time at the party.

senses.def: (have something done) to arrange for someone else to do something for you
examples: I'm having my hair cut tomorrow.
We had the house painted last summer.

senses.def: used with a past participle to form perfect tenses
examples: Have you ever been to Japan?
They have just finished dinner.

note: Forms: have – has – had – had. Use "have" for meals and drinks (have lunch, have a coffee). "Have got" is more British.

senses.def: used to say that something is necessary or required
examples: I have to finish this report by tomorrow.
You don't have to come if you're too tired.

senses.def: used to say that something is certainly true or likely
examples: You have to be joking!
This has to be the best pizza in town.

note: Pronounced /ˈhæf tə/ in speech. "Don't have to" = not necessary; "mustn't" = not allowed. Past: had to.

senses.def: something that could be dangerous or cause damage
examples: Wet floors are a common safety hazard in restaurants.
Air pollution is a serious health hazard in big cities.

senses.def: (hazard a guess) to make a guess although you are not sure
examples: I'd hazard a guess that she's about forty.

note: "An occupational hazard" = a risk that comes with a particular job.

senses.def: used as the subject of a verb to refer to a man, boy, or male animal already mentioned
examples: My brother called; he says he'll be late.
Where's your dog? Is he friendly?

note: Turkish "o" has no gender; English uses he (male), she (female), it (things), they (unknown or non-binary).

senses.def: the top part of the body, containing the eyes, mouth, and brain
examples: She hit her head on the kitchen cabinet.
He shook his head and said no.

senses.def: your mind or ability to think
examples: I can't get that song out of my head.
Use your head and think before you act.

senses.def: the person in charge of a group or organization
examples: She's the head of the marketing department.
Heads of state met in Brussels for the summit.

senses.def: to move in a particular direction, or to lead a group or organization
examples: We're heading home after the game.
He was chosen to head the investigation.

collocations: off the top of my head
note: "Off the top of my head" = without checking. "Head over heels (in love)" = completely in love.

senses.def: a pain in your head
examples: I have a terrible headache from staring at the screen.
Loud music always gives me a headache.

senses.def: a problem or situation that causes worry or difficulty
examples: Finding parking downtown is a real headache.
The new tax rules are a headache for small businesses.

note: Say "I have a headache", not "my head is aching" (correct but less common).

senses.def: the title of a news story, printed in large letters
examples: The scandal made headlines around the world.
I only had time to read the headlines this morning.

senses.def: to be the main performer at a concert or event
examples: The band will headline the festival on Saturday night.

senses.def: the main office of an organization, or the place from which a military operation is controlled
examples: The company's headquarters are in Seattle.
Police headquarters released a statement late last night.

note: Same form for singular and plural; can take a singular or plural verb. Often shortened to HQ.

senses.def: to become healthy again, or to make a wound or injury healthy again
examples: The cut on my hand healed quickly.
It took months for her broken leg to heal.

senses.def: to end a bad situation or make someone feel better emotionally
examples: The leaders hope to heal the divisions in the country.
Time heals all wounds.

note: Don't confuse with "heel" (back of the foot), pronounced the same.

senses.def: the condition of a person's body or mind
examples: Regular exercise is good for your health.
My grandmother is in poor health.

senses.def: the work of providing medical services
examples: The government plans to increase spending on public health.

senses.def: how successful or strong something such as an economy or organization is
examples: Investors are worried about the health of the economy.

note: Uncountable: "good health", not "a good health".

senses.def: the services that provide medical care to people
examples: Many Americans struggle to afford healthcare.
She works as a healthcare assistant in a nursing home.

note: Also written "health care", especially as a noun in American English.

senses.def: physically strong and well, not sick
examples: She gave birth to a healthy baby girl.
Eating vegetables helps you stay healthy.

senses.def: good for your health
examples: Try to eat a healthy breakfast every day.

senses.def: successful, strong, or normal
examples: The company made a healthy profit last year.
A healthy debate is good for democracy.

senses.def: to notice sounds with your ears
examples: Can you hear me in the back row?
I heard a strange noise downstairs last night.

senses.def: to be told about something or receive news
examples: Did you hear that Mark got a new job?
I haven't heard from her in months.

senses.def: to listen to and judge a case in court
examples: The Supreme Court will hear the case next month.

note: Irregular: hear – heard – heard. Hear = notice a sound; listen = pay attention to it on purpose.

senses.def: the ability to hear
examples: His hearing got worse as he got older.
She wears a hearing aid in her left ear.

senses.def: an official meeting where facts about a case or problem are heard, for example in court
examples: The court hearing has been postponed until next week.
Congress held a hearing on online privacy.

note: "Hard of hearing" = partly deaf (polite).

senses.def: the organ in your chest that pumps blood around your body
examples: My heart was beating fast before the interview.
He died of a heart attack at sixty.

senses.def: the center of your feelings and emotions
examples: She has a kind heart.
Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

senses.def: the center or most important part of something
examples: The hotel is in the heart of the city.
Let's get to the heart of the problem.

note: "Learn something by heart" = memorize it (ezberlemek). "Lose heart" = become discouraged.

senses.def: the quality of being hot, or hot weather
examples: I can't stand the summer heat in Texas.
Cook the sauce over low heat.

senses.def: the system that keeps a building warm
examples: Can you turn the heat up? It's cold in here.

senses.def: pressure or strong emotion, especially anger
examples: In the heat of the moment, I said things I didn't mean.

senses.def: to make something hot or warm, or to become hot
examples: Heat the oil in a large pan.
The debate heated up as the election approached.

collocations: in the heat of the moment
note: "A heated argument" = an angry one. American English: "turn on the heat" (British: the heating).

senses.def: the process or system of keeping a building warm
examples: Our heating bills doubled this winter.
The apartment has central heating.

note: In American English people usually say "the heat" for the system: Turn on the heat.

senses.def: in some religions, the place where God lives and good people go after they die
examples: She believes her father is in heaven now.

senses.def: a place or situation that is extremely pleasant
examples: This chocolate cake is heaven!
Lying on the beach all day was pure heaven.

note: "For heaven's sake!" expresses annoyance. "Good heavens!" expresses surprise.

senses.def: to a great degree or in large amounts
examples: It rained heavily all night.
The company relies heavily on foreign investment.

senses.def: in a slow, heavy, or forceful way
examples: He sat down heavily on the sofa.
She was breathing heavily after the climb.

senses.def: weighing a lot and difficult to lift or move
examples: This suitcase is too heavy for me to carry.
Heavy trucks are banned from the bridge.

senses.def: larger in amount or more intense than usual
examples: Heavy rain caused flooding in the valley.
There was heavy traffic on the highway this morning.

senses.def: serious or difficult to deal with
examples: The conversation got a bit heavy after dinner.

note: Use "heavy" for traffic and rain where Turkish says "yoğun/şiddetli": heavy traffic, not "crowded traffic".

senses.def: the back part of your foot, below the ankle
examples: I have a blister on my heel from these new shoes.

senses.def: the raised part under the back of a shoe, or (heels) shoes with high heels
examples: She wore black heels to the interview.
The heel came off my boot.

note: "Achilles heel" = a weak point. "On the heels of" = right after. Sounds the same as "heal".

senses.def: how tall a person or thing is, or the distance from the ground
examples: He's about average height for his age.
The plane was flying at a height of 30,000 feet.

senses.def: the point when something is strongest, busiest, or most successful
examples: She was at the height of her career in the 1990s.
Hotels are expensive at the height of tourist season.

senses.def: (heights) a high place
examples: I've always been afraid of heights.

note: Pronounced /haɪt/ (no "th" sound), unlike length, width, depth.

senses.def: to make a feeling or effect stronger, or to become stronger
examples: The attack has heightened tensions between the two countries.
Music is used to heighten suspense in the film.

note: Used for feelings, effects, and awareness, not physical height.

senses.def: an aircraft with large spinning blades on top, which can fly straight up and stay in one place
examples: The injured hiker was rescued by helicopter.
A news helicopter circled over the scene of the accident.

note: "Helicopter parent" = a parent who is too involved in their child's life.

senses.def: in some religions, the place where bad people go after they die
examples: Many religions teach about heaven and hell.

senses.def: a very unpleasant experience or situation
examples: Working for that company was absolute hell.
Rush-hour traffic is hell in this city.

senses.def: (informal, rude) used to show anger or for emphasis
examples: What the hell are you doing?

note: Swear word in many expressions; avoid in formal situations. "A hell of a…" = very good/big: a hell of a game.

senses.def: used as a greeting, when answering the phone, or to get someone's attention
examples: Hello, my name is Anna. Nice to meet you.
Hello? Is anybody home?

senses.def: the act of saying hello
examples: Say hello to your parents for me.
She gave me a friendly hello.

note: "Say hello to X for me" = Turkish "X'e selam söyle". "Hi" is more casual.

senses.def: a hard hat that protects your head
examples: Always wear a helmet when you ride your bike.
The construction workers wore safety helmets.

senses.def: to make it easier for someone to do something by doing part of it or giving them what they need
examples: Can you help me carry these bags?
My brother helped me with my homework.

senses.def: to make a situation better or easier
examples: Taking deep breaths helps when I feel nervous.
Crying won't help.

senses.def: (can't help) to be unable to stop yourself from doing something
examples: I couldn't help laughing when he fell asleep in the meeting.

senses.def: the act of helping, or advice or money that makes things easier
examples: Thanks for your help with the move.
If you need help, just ask.

note: "Help yourself (to something)" = take as much as you want. "Can't help + -ing" = can't stop yourself.

senses.def: useful, or making a situation better
examples: Thanks for the advice — it was really helpful.
It might be helpful to make a list first.

senses.def: willing to help others
examples: The hotel staff were very friendly and helpful.

senses.def: for this reason; as a result
examples: The fruit is grown locally, hence the low price.
The data is incomplete and, hence, unreliable.

senses.def: (formal) from now
examples: The results will be announced three weeks hence.

note: Formal. Often followed directly by a noun: "hence the delay" (no verb needed).

senses.def: used as the object to refer to a woman, girl, or female animal already mentioned
examples: I called her yesterday, but she didn't answer.
Give the keys to her when she arrives.

senses.def: belonging to or connected with a woman, girl, or female animal already mentioned
examples: She left her phone on the train.
Her parents live in Florida.

note: "Her" is both object (I saw her) and possessive (her car). Turkish "onu/onun" has no gender.

senses.def: a plant whose leaves or seeds are used to flavor food or to make medicine
examples: Add fresh herbs like basil and parsley at the end.
She uses herbs to treat minor illnesses.

note: American English drops the h: /ɜːrb/ ("an herb"). British English says /hɜːb/ ("a herb").

senses.def: in, at, or to this place
examples: Come here and look at this.
I've lived here for ten years.

senses.def: used when giving something to someone or pointing something out
examples: Here's the book I promised you.
Here comes the bus!

senses.def: at this point in a situation or discussion
examples: Here we need to be careful about the numbers.

note: "Here you go/Here you are" = Turkish "buyurun" when handing something.

senses.def: the history, traditions, and buildings that a country or group has had for a long time and values
examples: The old town is part of the country's cultural heritage.
She is proud of her Mexican heritage.

note: "Heritage" is cultural; for money or property from a dead person, use "inheritance".

senses.def: a person admired for doing something brave or good
examples: The firefighter was treated as a hero after saving the children.
My mom has always been my hero.

senses.def: the main male character in a story, movie, or play
examples: The hero of the novel is a young detective.

note: Plural: heroes. "Unsung hero" = someone whose good work is not recognized.

senses.def: used to refer to something that belongs to a woman or girl already mentioned
examples: That isn't my coat — I think it's hers.
A friend of hers is coming to visit.

note: No apostrophe: hers, not her's.

senses.def: used as the object when a woman or girl does something to herself
examples: She cut herself while chopping vegetables.
My daughter taught herself to play piano.

senses.def: used to emphasize that a particular woman did something
examples: The CEO herself called to apologize.

note: "By herself" = alone or without help.

senses.def: to pause before speaking or acting because you are unsure or nervous
examples: She hesitated before answering the question.
He didn't hesitate to call the police when he saw the fire.

senses.def: (don't hesitate) used to tell someone they should feel free to do something
examples: Please don't hesitate to contact me if you have any questions.

note: "Please don't hesitate to contact me" is a very common polite email ending.

senses.def: (informal) used to get attention, greet someone, or show surprise or annoyance
examples: Hey, how's it going?
Hey! Watch where you're going!

note: Very common casual greeting in American English, like "hi".

senses.def: (informal) used to say hello
examples: Hi, I'm Tom. I just moved in next door.
Tell your sister I said hi.

note: "Say hi to X for me" = give X my greetings.

senses.def: kept or located where it cannot be seen or found
examples: Police found a hidden camera in the hotel room.
The village is hidden away in the mountains.

senses.def: not obvious or not easy to notice
examples: Watch out for hidden fees when you book a flight.
The movie has a hidden message about greed.

note: "A hidden gem" = an excellent place or thing that few people know about. "Hidden agenda" = a secret aim.

senses.def: to put something where it cannot be seen or found
examples: She hides her chocolate where the kids can't find it.
Where did you hide the presents?

senses.def: to go somewhere where you cannot be seen or found
examples: The children like to hide under the bed.
He tried to hide from the photographers.

senses.def: to keep feelings or information secret
examples: She couldn't hide her disappointment.
The company tried to hide the truth about the losses.

note: Irregular: hide – hid – hidden. "Go into hiding" = hide from the police or danger.

senses.def: a system in which people or things are arranged in levels of importance
examples: She quickly rose through the company hierarchy.
The army has a strict hierarchy.

senses.def: the group of people who control an organization
examples: The church hierarchy refused to comment.

senses.def: a long way from the bottom to the top, or far above the ground
examples: The city is surrounded by high mountains.
The shelf is too high for me to reach.

senses.def: greater than usual in amount, level, or quality
examples: Prices are very high in the city center.
She has high standards for her students.

senses.def: at or to a level far above the ground
examples: The eagle flew high above the valley.

senses.tr: zirve, en yüksek seviye; en yüksek sıcaklık
senses.def: the highest level or number
examples: Unemployment has reached a new high.
Tomorrow's high will be 85 degrees.

note: Use "tall" for people and narrow things (a tall man, tall tree); "high" for mountains, walls, and levels.

senses.tr: çok ses getiren, kamuoyunun dikkatini çeken, tanınmış
senses.def: getting a lot of attention from the media and the public
examples: The lawyer has worked on several high-profile cases.
Several high-profile executives resigned after the scandal.

note: Opposite: low-profile. "Keep a low profile" = avoid attention.

senses.def: to emphasize something so people notice it
examples: The report highlights the need for more teachers.
The accident highlighted the dangers of texting while driving.

senses.def: to mark text with a bright color or select it on a screen
examples: Highlight the important dates in yellow.

senses.tr: en önemli an, en güzel kısım; özet görüntüler
senses.def: the best or most interesting part of something
examples: The highlight of the trip was a boat tour of the bay.
We watched the game's highlights on TV.

senses.def: very; to a high degree
examples: It's highly unlikely that it will snow tomorrow.
She is a highly skilled surgeon.

senses.def: with great approval or respect
examples: I highly recommend this book.
Everyone speaks highly of her.

note: Not used for physical height: say "fly high", not "fly highly".

senses.def: a main road for traveling long distances between cities
examples: Traffic on the highway was backed up for miles.
Take the highway north for about twenty miles.

note: American English; British English says "motorway" for the biggest roads.

senses.def: extremely funny
examples: The movie was hilarious — I couldn't stop laughing.
He told a hilarious story about his trip to Paris.

note: Already strong; say "absolutely hilarious", not "very hilarious".

senses.def: an area of land higher than the land around it, but lower than a mountain
examples: Their house is on top of a hill overlooking the town.
We walked up a steep hill to the castle.

note: "Over the hill" (informal) = too old. "Capitol Hill" = the US Congress.

senses.def: used as the object to refer to a man, boy, or male animal already mentioned
examples: I saw him at the gym this morning.
Tell him to call me back.

note: Object form of "he": He likes her, and she likes him.

senses.def: used as the object when a man or boy does something to himself
examples: He hurt himself playing football.
My son made himself a sandwich.

senses.def: used to emphasize that a particular man did something
examples: The president himself attended the funeral.

note: "By himself" = alone or without help.

senses.def: something said or done indirectly to show what you are thinking, or a clue
examples: She dropped a hint that she wanted flowers for her birthday.
Can you give me a hint? I don't know the answer.

senses.def: a small amount or slight sign of something
examples: There was a hint of garlic in the sauce.
He spoke without a hint of regret.

senses.def: a useful piece of advice
examples: The website has helpful hints for first-time buyers.

senses.def: to suggest something indirectly
examples: The CEO hinted that more layoffs were coming.

note: "Take the hint" = understand what someone is suggesting indirectly.

senses.def: the area at either side of the body between the top of the leg and the waist
examples: My grandmother broke her hip when she fell.
She stood with her hands on her hips.

senses.def: (informal) fashionable and modern
examples: The neighborhood is full of hip cafés and galleries.

note: "Shoot from the hip" = speak or act quickly without thinking carefully.

senses.def: the male ruler of a country that has a royal family
examples: The king addressed the nation on television after the earthquake.
She was crowned queen when the old king died.

senses.def: the most important or successful person or thing in a particular field
examples: He was known as the king of rock and roll.
In the jungle, the lion is often called the king of the animals.

note: "King-size" (extra large) is common for beds and products: a king-size bed.

senses.def: a country whose head of state is a king or queen
examples: The United Kingdom is made up of four countries.
The ancient kingdom stretched from the mountains to the sea.

senses.def: one of the main groups into which living things are divided
examples: Fungi were once classified as part of the plant kingdom.

senses.def: to touch someone with your lips to show love or to say hello or goodbye
examples: She kissed her son on the forehead before he left for school.
They kissed for the first time under the streetlight.

senses.def: an act of touching someone with your lips
examples: He gave his grandmother a kiss on the cheek.
She blew him a kiss from the train window.

senses.def: a set of tools or equipment kept together for a particular purpose
examples: Every car should carry a basic first-aid kit.
The plumber opened his tool kit and got to work.

senses.tr: (kendin monte et) parça seti, maket seti
senses.def: a set of parts that you put together yourself to make something
examples: My son spent the weekend building a model airplane from a kit.

note: In British English, "kit" also means sports clothes (football kit). Americans say "uniform" or "gear".

senses.def: the room where food is prepared and cooked
examples: We usually eat breakfast at the kitchen table.
The restaurant's kitchen was closed for a health inspection.

senses.def: the joint in the middle of your leg where it bends
examples: She hurt her knee while skiing and needed surgery.
The kids knelt on their knees to look under the bed.

note: The k is silent: /niː/. Related verb: kneel – knelt – knelt.

senses.def: a tool with a sharp metal blade and a handle, used for cutting or as a weapon
examples: Use a sharp knife to slice the tomatoes.
Police found the knife used in the attack.

note: Plural: knives. The k is silent: /naɪf/.

senses.def: to hit a door or window with your hand so that people inside know you are there
examples: Someone knocked on the door just after midnight.
Please knock before you come into my office.

senses.def: to hit something by accident so that it moves or falls
examples: The cat knocked a glass off the table.

senses.def: the sound of someone hitting a door to get attention
examples: There was a loud knock at the door.

note: Phrasal verbs: knock down (demolish), knock out (make unconscious), knock over (make fall).

senses.def: to have information in your mind because you learned it or were told it
examples: Do you know what time the store closes?
I didn't know that she had moved to Chicago.

senses.def: to be familiar with a person or place
examples: I've known him since we were in high school.
She knows the city really well.

note: Irregular: know – knew – known. Not used in continuous form: say "I know", not "I am knowing".

senses.def: the information, understanding and skills you get from education or experience
examples: She has a deep knowledge of Japanese history.
The job requires basic knowledge of accounting software.

senses.def: the state of knowing about a particular fact or situation
examples: The deal was made without my knowledge.
To my knowledge, nobody has complained yet.

note: Uncountable: say "a lot of knowledge", never "knowledges" or "a knowledge" (except "a good knowledge of").

senses.def: a laboratory; a room or building for scientific experiments and testing
examples: The blood samples were sent to the lab for testing.
Students spend two hours a week in the chemistry lab.

note: Informal short form of "laboratory", used far more often in everyday speech.

senses.def: a small piece of paper or material attached to something that gives information about it
examples: Always read the label before taking any medicine.
The price was printed on a label inside the jacket.

senses.def: a company that produces music recordings, or a brand of clothing
examples: The band signed with a major record label last year.

senses.def: to attach a label to something, or to describe someone in a way that is often unfair
examples: Make sure all the boxes are clearly labeled.
He was unfairly labeled a troublemaker at school.

note: American spelling: labeled, labeling. British: labelled, labelling.

senses.def: work, especially physical work, or the workers who do it
examples: The repair cost $200 for parts and $150 for labor.
Many farms depend on cheap seasonal labor.

senses.def: the process of giving birth to a baby
examples: She went into labor two weeks early.

note: British spelling: labour. "Labor Day" is a US holiday in September.

senses.def: a room or building where scientists do experiments, research or tests
examples: The vaccine was developed in a university laboratory.
Samples were analyzed in a government laboratory.

note: American stress is on the first syllable: LAB-ruh-tor-ee. British stress: la-BOR-uh-tree.

senses.def: the state of not having something or not having enough of it
examples: The project failed because of a lack of funding.
Lack of sleep can affect your concentration.

senses.def: to not have something, or not have enough of it
examples: He's talented but lacks confidence.
The report lacked any real detail.

note: The verb takes a direct object: "She lacks experience", not "lacks of experience". The noun uses "of".

senses.def: a boy or young man
examples: He was just a lad of sixteen when he joined the navy.
The old farmer hired a local lad to help with the harvest.

note: Mainly British and informal. Americans usually say "boy", "kid" or "guy".

senses.def: a piece of equipment with steps between two long sides, used for climbing up and down
examples: He climbed a ladder to clean the gutters.
Hold the ladder steady while I change the bulb.

senses.def: a series of levels in an organization or society that people try to move up
examples: She worked her way up the corporate ladder.

note: A ladder is portable. Fixed stairs in a building are "stairs" or "a staircase" — both are "merdiven" in Turkish.

senses.def: a polite word for a woman
examples: An elderly lady asked me for directions to the station.
Ladies and gentlemen, please take your seats.

note: "The ladies' room" is a polite American term for a women's restroom. "First Lady" is the president's wife.

senses.def: a large area of water surrounded by land
examples: We rented a cabin by the lake for the summer.
In winter, the lake freezes over completely.

note: In names, "Lake" comes first and has no "the": Lake Van, Lake Superior.

senses.def: a device that produces light, especially one you can move around
examples: She switched on the lamp beside her bed and started reading.
The desk lamp was too dim to work by.

senses.def: the solid surface of the earth, or an area of ground owned by someone
examples: After three weeks at sea, the sailors finally saw land.
They bought a piece of land to build a house on.

senses.def: a country or region (literary)
examples: Immigrants came to this land looking for a better life.

senses.def: to come down from the air onto the ground or another surface
examples: Our flight landed in Denver an hour late.
A bird landed on the windowsill.

senses.def: to succeed in getting something good, such as a job or contract (informal)
examples: She landed a job at a major tech company.

senses.def: the act of bringing an aircraft or spacecraft down to the ground
examples: The pilot made an emergency landing in a field.
The first moon landing took place in 1969.

senses.def: the flat area at the top of a set of stairs or between two sets of stairs
examples: The kids left their shoes on the landing outside the bedroom.

note: Opposite of "takeoff". A "landing page" is the first web page a visitor arrives at.

senses.def: a person or company that rents a house, apartment or office to someone
examples: Our landlord raised the rent by ten percent this year.
Call the landlord if the heating stops working.

note: Trap: Turkish "ev sahibi" also means "host". In English, landlord = the person you pay rent to; host = the person who invites guests.

senses.def: a building or place that is easy to see and recognize and helps you know where you are
examples: The Golden Gate Bridge is San Francisco's most famous landmark.
Turn left at the old church; it's a good landmark.

senses.def: an event, discovery or decision that marks an important stage or change
examples: The court's ruling was a landmark in civil rights history.
It was a landmark decision for gay rights.

note: "Landmark" is often used before a noun: a landmark ruling/case/study (= very important, historic).

senses.def: everything you can see when you look across a large area of land
examples: The desert landscape was flat and empty for miles.
Wind farms have changed the rural landscape.

senses.def: the general situation in a particular area of activity
examples: Streaming services have transformed the media landscape.

note: "Landscape" also means horizontal page orientation (opposite: portrait).

senses.def: one of the parts of a road marked for a single line of traffic
examples: The truck suddenly moved into the left lane.
Only buses can use this lane during rush hour.

senses.def: a narrow road, especially in the countryside
examples: We walked down a quiet country lane lined with trees.

note: "Life in the fast lane" means an exciting, busy, often risky lifestyle.

senses.def: the system of words and grammar used by the people of a particular country or group
examples: She speaks three languages fluently.
English is the official language of the conference.

senses.def: a particular style of speaking or writing, or words of a certain type
examples: The contract is written in very technical language.
Watch your language — there are children here.

senses.def: the flat area formed by the top of your legs when you sit down
examples: The cat jumped onto my lap and fell asleep.
She sat with her hands folded in her lap.

senses.def: one trip around a track or one length of a swimming pool
examples: He swims thirty laps every morning before work.
The leader crashed on the final lap.

note: "Fall into your lap" means to get something good without effort.

senses.def: a small computer that runs on a battery and is easy to carry
examples: I always bring my laptop when I work from a café.
The battery on my old laptop only lasts an hour.

note: "Desktop" is the non-portable kind.

senses.def: big in size, amount or number
examples: They live in a large house with a big backyard.
A large number of people attended the protest.

note: Trap: "large" means big, not "wide" (= geniş in width). "At large" = not yet caught; "by and large" = generally.

senses.def: involving many people or things, or happening over a wide area
examples: The government launched a large-scale vaccination program.
Large-scale protests broke out across the country.

note: Opposite: small-scale. Used before a noun.

senses.def: to a great degree; mostly
examples: The success of the project was largely due to her hard work.
The town's economy is largely based on tourism.

senses.def: a device that produces a strong, narrow beam of light used for cutting, surgery, etc.
examples: The surgeon used a laser to correct her eyesight.
The factory uses lasers to cut sheets of metal.

note: "Laser-focused" means extremely concentrated on one goal.

senses.def: coming after all others; final
examples: We caught the last train home.
She was the last person to leave the office.

senses.def: most recent; the one before the present one
examples: I saw him last week at the gym.
Last night's game went into overtime.

senses.def: to continue for a particular length of time, or to stay in good condition
examples: The meeting lasted three hours.
These batteries last much longer than cheap ones.

senses.def: after everything or everyone else, or most recently
examples: Our team finished last in the league.
When did you last see your wallet?

note: No "the" before time words: "last week", not "the last week" (which means "the past seven days").

senses.def: arriving or happening after the expected or usual time
examples: Sorry I'm late — the traffic was terrible.
The train was twenty minutes late.

senses.def: near the end of a period of time
examples: The house was built in the late 1800s.
She's in her late thirties.

senses.def: after the expected or usual time, or near the end of a period
examples: He stayed up late watching movies.
The package arrived two days late.

senses.def: used about someone who has died, especially recently
examples: The award was named after her late husband.

note: The adverb is "late", not "lately": "I arrived late". "Lately" means "recently".

senses.def: recently; during the period just before now
examples: Have you talked to Mark lately?
I've been feeling really tired lately.

note: Usually with the present perfect: "I haven't seen her lately." It does not mean "late".

senses.def: at a time in the future, or after the time you are talking about
examples: I'll call you back later tonight.
Two years later, they got married.

senses.def: coming after something else, or happening in the future
examples: The issue will be discussed at a later date.
In later life, she became a painter.

note: Don't confuse with "latter" (/ˈlætər/), which means the second of two things mentioned.

senses.def: the most recent or newest
examples: Have you seen the latest episode of the show?
The latest figures show unemployment is falling.

senses.tr: en son haber, en son çıkan şey
senses.def: the newest thing, fashion or piece of news
examples: This phone is the latest in smartphone technology.
Stay tuned for the latest on the storm.

note: "At the latest" sets a deadline: "Send it by Friday at the latest."

senses.def: the second of two people or things just mentioned
examples: Given the choice of tea or coffee, most people chose the latter.
Of the two plans, the latter seems more realistic.

senses.def: near the end of a period of time
examples: The company grew quickly in the latter half of the decade.

note: Opposite: "the former" (the first of two). Formal; always used with "the".

senses.def: to make sounds and move your face in a way that shows you think something is funny
examples: Everyone laughed at his joke about the boss.
We laughed until we cried.

senses.def: to show that you think someone or something is silly or not serious
examples: The other kids laughed at him because of his accent.

senses.def: the sound you make when you think something is funny
examples: She has a loud, warm laugh.
The comedian got a big laugh from the audience.

note: "Laugh at" can mean mocking. The gh is pronounced /f/.

senses.def: the act or sound of laughing
examples: The room was full of laughter during the wedding speech.
The audience burst into laughter.

note: Uncountable: "a lot of laughter", not "laughters".

senses.def: to start a planned activity, especially a large or important one
examples: Police have launched an investigation into the fire.
The charity launched a campaign to reduce plastic waste.

senses.def: to make a new product available to the public
examples: The company will launch its new phone in September.

senses.def: to send a rocket or missile into the air or a boat into the water
examples: The rocket was launched from Florida early this morning.

senses.def: the act of starting or introducing something, or of sending a rocket into space
examples: The product launch was streamed live online.
The launch was delayed because of bad weather.

senses.def: an official rule made by a government that everyone must obey
examples: There's a law against texting while driving in most states.
Congress passed a new law on data privacy.

senses.def: the whole system of rules in a country, or the subject of study about them
examples: She studied law at Harvard.
Everyone is equal under the law.

senses.def: a statement describing what always happens in science or nature
examples: The law of gravity explains why objects fall.

senses.def: an area of short, cut grass, especially in front of or behind a house
examples: He mows the lawn every Saturday morning.
The kids were playing on the front lawn.

senses.def: a claim that a person or organization brings to a court of law against another
examples: The family filed a lawsuit against the hospital.
The company settled the lawsuit out of court.

note: Common verb pair: file a lawsuit (= dava açmak). You can also "sue" someone.

senses.def: a person trained to advise people about the law and represent them in court
examples: You should talk to a lawyer before signing that contract.
Her lawyer said she would appeal the decision.

note: In American English, "attorney" is common and more formal.

senses.def: to put someone or something down carefully in a flat position
examples: She laid the baby gently in the crib.
Lay the map on the table so we can all see it.

senses.def: to produce eggs
examples: Our chickens lay about six eggs a day.

senses.def: to prepare or establish something, especially the basis for later development
examples: These early studies helped lay the foundation for modern medicine.

note: Lay – laid – laid needs an object (lay the book down). Lie – lay – lain has no object (lie on the bed). "Lay off" = fire workers.

senses.def: a quantity or sheet of something that lies over a surface or between surfaces
examples: A thin layer of dust covered the furniture.
Wear several layers of clothing when you go hiking in winter.

senses.def: a level or part within a system or set of ideas
examples: Each new layer of bureaucracy slowed the project down.

senses.def: the way the parts of something, such as a page, room or building, are arranged
examples: We changed the layout of the kitchen to make more space.
The website has a clean, simple layout.

note: Noun is one word (layout); the phrasal verb is two words (lay out the plans).

senses.def: not willing to work or make an effort
examples: He's too lazy to cook, so he orders takeout every night.
The teacher said the essay was lazy and poorly researched.

senses.def: relaxed and without much activity
examples: We spent a lazy Sunday afternoon in the park.

senses.def: to go in front of someone or take them somewhere to show the way
examples: The guide led us through the old part of the city.
This path leads to the beach.

senses.def: to be in charge of a group, organization or activity
examples: She was chosen to lead the research team.
Who will lead the party into the next election?

senses.def: to cause something to happen as a result
examples: Too much stress can lead to serious health problems.

senses.def: a position ahead of others in a competition, or a piece of information that helps solve something
examples: Our team took the lead in the second half.
Police are following up several new leads.

note: Irregular: lead – led – led. The metal "lead" (kurşun) is pronounced /led/.

senses.def: a person who is in charge of a group, organization or country
examples: World leaders met in Geneva to discuss climate change.
She's a natural leader who inspires her team.

senses.def: a person, team or company that is ahead of others or the most successful
examples: The company is a world leader in solar technology.

senses.def: the position of being a leader, or the ability to lead people well
examples: Under her leadership, the company doubled its profits.
The job requires strong leadership skills.

senses.def: the people who lead an organization or group
examples: The party leadership refused to comment on the scandal.

senses.def: most important, successful or influential
examples: She is one of the country's leading experts on cancer.
Heart disease is the leading cause of death in the US.

senses.def: having the main part in a play or movie
examples: He played the leading role in the school musical.

note: A "leading question" is one asked in a way that pushes someone toward a particular answer.

senses.def: one of the flat, usually green parts that grow from a plant's stem or branch
examples: A single yellow leaf fell from the tree.
Add a bay leaf to the soup for extra flavor.

note: Plural: leaves. "Turn over a new leaf" means to start behaving better.

senses.def: a printed sheet of paper or a few pages given out free to advertise or inform
examples: Volunteers handed out leaflets about the election outside the station.
The leaflet explains how to recycle properly.

note: More common in British English. Americans usually say "flyer" or "pamphlet".

senses.def: a group of sports teams that play against each other to find the best
examples: The team finished third in the league last season.
He plays in a local basketball league on weekends.

senses.def: a level of quality or ability
examples: That restaurant is way out of my league — it's far too expensive.

note: "Be in league with" = to work secretly with someone, usually to do something bad.

senses.def: to let liquid or gas escape through a small hole, or to escape in this way
examples: The roof leaks every time it rains.
Gas was leaking from a broken pipe.

senses.def: to give secret information to the public or the media
examples: Someone leaked the report to the press before it was published.

senses.def: a small hole that lets liquid or gas escape, or a secret that is made public
examples: There's a leak in the kitchen faucet.
The government is investigating the leak of classified documents.

senses.def: to bend your body in a direction, or to rest against something for support
examples: She leaned forward to hear what he was saying.
He leaned his bike against the wall.

senses.def: to tend to support or prefer a particular opinion or choice
examples: Most voters in the district lean toward the left.

senses.def: having little fat, or using few resources
examples: Choose lean meat like chicken breast.
The startup runs a lean operation with just five employees.

note: "Lean on someone" = depend on them for support. Past: leaned (American) or leant (British).

senses.def: to jump high or a long way, or move somewhere suddenly and quickly
examples: The dog leaped over the fence and ran into the street.
She leaped out of bed when the alarm went off.

senses.def: a long or high jump, or a sudden large increase or change
examples: Sales took a huge leap after the ad campaign.
Moving abroad was a big leap for her.
