note: Past: leaped (common in American) or leapt. "Leap at the chance" = accept eagerly.

senses.def: to gain knowledge or a skill by studying, practicing or being taught
examples: I'm learning to play the guitar.
Kids learn languages faster than adults.

senses.def: to find out about something
examples: We learned about the accident from the local news.
She was shocked to learn that she had been fired.

note: Trap: don't say "learn someone something". Use "teach": She taught me Spanish.

senses.def: the process of gaining knowledge or skills
examples: The app makes language learning fun and easy.
Children with learning difficulties may need extra support.

senses.def: knowledge gained by a lot of study
examples: He was a man of great learning and wisdom.

note: "A steep learning curve" means you have to learn a lot quickly.

senses.def: to the smallest degree
examples: This is the least expensive hotel in town.
The problem appeared when we least expected it.

senses.def: the smallest in amount or degree
examples: The bus is the option that uses the least energy.

senses.def: the smallest amount or number
examples: It's the least I can do after all your help.

note: "At least" = not less than / anyway. "Not in the least" = not at all.

senses.def: material made from animal skin, used to make shoes, bags, jackets, etc.
examples: He bought a black leather jacket in Florence.
The sofa is made of real leather.

senses.def: to go away from a person or place
examples: What time do you leave for work?
She left the party early because she had a headache.

senses.def: to let something stay where it is, or to forget to take it
examples: I left my phone in the taxi.
Leave the door open, please.

senses.def: to stop living with someone or stop being part of a job or organization
examples: He left his job to start his own business.

senses.def: a period of time when you are allowed to be away from work
examples: She's on maternity leave until March.
He took two weeks of sick leave.

note: Irregular: leave – left – left. "Leave for" shows destination: "leave for Paris" (Paris'e gitmek üzere ayrılmak).

senses.def: a talk given to a group of people to teach them about a subject, especially at a university
examples: The professor gave a lecture on climate science.
I missed the morning lecture because I overslept.

senses.def: a long, serious talk criticizing someone or telling them how to behave
examples: My dad gave me a lecture about coming home late.

senses.def: to give a talk to teach people, or to criticize someone in a long, serious way
examples: She lectures in economics at a state university.
Stop lecturing me — I know I made a mistake.

note: Trap: Turkish "lektör" is not a lecturer. A "lecturer" is a university teacher (öğretim görevlisi).

senses.def: on the side of your body that is toward the west when you face north
examples: She wears her watch on her left wrist.
The bathroom is the second door on the left side.

senses.def: toward the left side
examples: Turn left at the next traffic light.

senses.def: the left side or direction, or political groups that support social equality and change
examples: The school is on your left after the bridge.
Many on the left criticized the new tax plan.

note: "Left" is also the past of "leave": I left early. "Left over" = remaining.

senses.def: one of the long parts of the body that connect the feet to the rest of the body
examples: He broke his leg playing soccer.
My legs were sore after the long hike.

senses.def: one of the parts that support a table, chair, etc.
examples: One leg of the table is shorter than the others.

senses.def: one part of a journey, race or competition
examples: The band starts the European leg of its tour next month.

note: "Pull someone's leg" = joke with them. "Break a leg!" = good luck (to performers).

senses.def: money or property left to someone after a person's death
examples: She left a large legacy to the local hospital.

senses.def: something, good or bad, that exists as a result of past events or a person's actions
examples: The president's legacy will be judged by future generations.
Pollution is the legacy of decades of heavy industry.

note: In tech, "legacy" describes old systems still in use: legacy software.

senses.def: connected with the law
examples: You should get legal advice before you sign anything.
The company is facing legal action from former employees.

senses.def: allowed by the law
examples: Is it legal to drive with headphones on?
The legal drinking age in the US is 21.

senses.def: an old story about people and events that may or may not be true
examples: According to legend, the lake was formed by a giant's tears.
The legend of King Arthur has been told for centuries.

senses.def: a very famous person, admired for their skill in a particular area
examples: He's a basketball legend who inspired a generation of players.

note: An "urban legend" is a modern story that many people believe but is probably false.

senses.def: very famous and much talked about, often because of special skill
examples: The chef is legendary for his perfect steaks.
The band's legendary 1985 concert is still talked about today.

senses.def: mentioned in old stories
examples: The dragon is a legendary creature found in many cultures.

senses.def: to make a law that affects or controls something
examples: Congress has been slow to legislate on artificial intelligence.
Several states have legislated against smoking in public places.

note: Formal. You can't "legislate morality" means laws cannot force people to be good.

senses.def: a law or set of laws passed by a parliament or government
examples: New legislation will ban single-use plastic bags.
The Senate passed the legislation by a narrow margin.

note: Uncountable: "a piece of legislation", not "a legislation".

senses.def: connected with making and passing laws
examples: Congress is the legislative branch of the US government.
The bill faced several legislative hurdles.

note: The three branches of US government: legislative, executive and judicial (yasama, yürütme, yargı).

senses.def: a group of people with the power to make and change laws
examples: The state legislature voted to raise the minimum wage.
The bill now goes to the legislature for approval.

note: Legislature = the body (meclis); legislation = the laws it makes (mevzuat); legislator = a member (milletvekili).

senses.def: having a fair and acceptable reason
examples: That's a perfectly legitimate question.
Customers have a legitimate reason to complain about the delays.

senses.def: allowed and recognized by law or by accepted rules
examples: Is this a legitimate business or a scam?
The election was seen as free and legitimate.

note: Informal short form: "legit" (That place is totally legit).

senses.def: time when you are not working or studying and can relax
examples: Most people spend their leisure time watching TV or online.
The hotel has excellent leisure facilities, including a pool and spa.

note: "At your leisure" = when it is convenient for you. American pronunciation: /ˈliːʒər/ (LEE-zher).

senses.def: a yellow fruit with sour juice, used in cooking and drinks
examples: Squeeze some lemon over the fish before serving.
She drinks hot water with lemon every morning.

senses.tr: (araba vb.) sürekli arıza çıkaran, çürük mal
senses.def: a product, especially a car, that has many faults (informal, American)
examples: The used car turned out to be a total lemon.

note: In the US, "lemonade" is usually a still drink of lemon juice, sugar and water, not a fizzy soda.

senses.def: to give something to someone for a time, expecting them to give it back
examples: Could you lend me twenty dollars until Friday?
The bank refused to lend them money for a new house.

senses.def: to add a particular quality to something, or to give help or support
examples: The candles lend a romantic feel to the room.
Can you lend me a hand with these boxes?

note: Irregular: lend – lent – lent. Lend = give temporarily; borrow = take temporarily. Turkish "ödünç almak" = borrow.

senses.def: the size of something from one end to the other
examples: The bridge is about two miles in length.
Measure the length and width of the room.

senses.def: the amount of time something lasts or the amount of writing in something
examples: The length of the movie is almost three hours.
Essays should be around 2,000 words in length.

note: "Go to great lengths" = make a big effort. "At length" = for a long time / in detail.

senses.def: very long in time or size, often too long
examples: After a lengthy discussion, they finally agreed on a plan.
The application process is lengthy and complicated.

note: Often slightly negative, suggesting something is longer than necessary.

senses.def: a curved piece of glass or plastic that makes things look larger, smaller or clearer
examples: She bought a new lens for her camera.
I wear contact lenses instead of glasses.

senses.def: a particular way of looking at or understanding something
examples: The book examines history through the lens of women's experience.

note: Plural: lenses. In Turkish "lens" usually means contact lens; in English it means any lens.

senses.def: used about a woman who is sexually attracted to other women, or connected with such women
examples: The film tells the story of a lesbian couple raising two kids.
She was one of the first openly lesbian politicians in the state.

senses.def: a woman who is sexually attracted to other women
examples: The group offers support for lesbians and gay men.

senses.def: to a smaller degree; not so much
examples: The second movie was less exciting than the first.
I've been eating less since I started the diet.

senses.def: a smaller amount of (used with uncountable nouns)
examples: You should spend less time on your phone.
The new model uses less fuel.

senses.def: a smaller amount
examples: The repair cost less than we expected.

note: Traditionally, use "less" with uncountable nouns (less money) and "fewer" with plurals (fewer people).

senses.tr: daha az, daha küçük, daha önemsiz
senses.def: not as great in size, amount or importance as something else
examples: He chose the lesser of two evils and voted for the moderate candidate.
The storm hit the coast hard and inland areas to a lesser extent.

note: Used before nouns or in fixed phrases, never with "than": say "less than", not "lesser than".

senses.def: a period of time when someone is taught something
examples: She takes piano lessons twice a week.
Today's lesson is about the American Civil War.

senses.def: an experience that teaches you something, especially what not to do
examples: Losing all my files taught me a lesson: always make backups.
The government must learn the lessons of the last crisis.

note: Turkish "ders" can also mean a school subject; for that, English says "subject": My favorite subject is math.

senses.def: to allow someone to do something or something to happen
examples: My parents never let me stay out after ten.
Don't let the dog sleep on the bed.

senses.def: used in "let's" to make a suggestion or in "let me" to offer something
examples: Let's grab lunch after the meeting.
Let me help you with those bags.

senses.def: to allow someone to use a room or building in return for rent (mainly British)
examples: They let the apartment to students during the school year.

note: Irregular: let – let – let. No "to" after let: "let me go", not "let me to go". "Let alone" = still less.

senses.def: causing or able to cause death
examples: The drug can be lethal if mixed with alcohol.
He was executed by lethal injection.

senses.def: very harmful or effective (informal)
examples: The striker is lethal in front of the goal.

note: Lethal = able to kill; fatal = actually caused death (a fatal accident).

senses.def: a written message that is sent to someone in an envelope or by email
examples: I received a letter from the bank about my account.
She wrote a cover letter to go with her application.

senses.def: a written symbol that represents a sound in a language
examples: The English alphabet has 26 letters.
Write your name in capital letters.

note: "Follow instructions to the letter" = exactly. A "cover letter" is "ön yazı" for a job application.

senses.def: the amount, degree or standard of something
examples: Pollution levels in the city have risen sharply.
This course is designed for students at an advanced level.

senses.def: the height of something, or a floor in a building
examples: The town is 2,000 feet above sea level.
The parking garage has four levels.

senses.def: having a flat surface that does not slope, or at the same height or position
examples: Make sure the shelf is level before you screw it in.

senses.def: to make something flat, or to destroy a building completely
examples: The earthquake leveled half the town.

note: "A level playing field" = a fair situation for everyone. American spelling: leveled, leveling.

senses.def: an extra amount of money that must be paid, such as a tax
examples: The city introduced a levy on plastic bags.
Airlines pay a levy on every ticket sold.

senses.def: to officially demand and collect a tax or fine
examples: The government plans to levy a new tax on sugary drinks.
A fine was levied on the company for polluting the river.

note: Formal. The verb is usually used with "tax", "fine" or "charge" as object: levy a tax on something.

senses.def: legally responsible for paying for something or for damage
examples: The landlord was held liable for the tenant's injuries.
You may be liable for any damage to the rental car.

senses.def: likely to do something or be affected by something, usually something bad
examples: Old bridges are liable to collapse in strong earthquakes.

note: "Be liable to" is often used for negative possibilities. "Liability" also means a person or thing that causes problems.

senses.def: respecting others' opinions and behavior and supporting personal freedom
examples: She grew up in a liberal household where everything could be discussed.
The city is known for its liberal attitudes.

senses.def: in US politics, supporting social change and government action to help people
examples: Liberal voters strongly supported the healthcare bill.

senses.def: a person who has liberal views
examples: He describes himself as a lifelong liberal.

note: In the US, "liberal" means left-leaning. In Europe and Turkey it often means pro-free-market. "Liberal arts" = humanities.

senses.def: the act of freeing a country, group or person from someone else's control
examples: The city celebrates its liberation from occupation every year.
The women's liberation movement grew rapidly in the 1970s.

senses.def: freedom to live as you choose without too many limits from authority
examples: The constitution protects basic civil liberties.
They fought for liberty and independence.

senses.def: the freedom or right to do something
examples: I'm not at liberty to discuss the details of the case.

note: "Take the liberty of doing" = do something without asking permission. "Take liberties" = act too freely.

senses.def: a building or room where books and other materials are kept for people to read or borrow
examples: I borrowed three novels from the public library.
She spends most afternoons studying in the university library.

senses.def: a collection of books, music, films or software
examples: The app gives you access to a huge music library.

note: Trap: "library" is not "kitapçı" (bookstore). You borrow from a library and buy from a bookstore.

senses.def: an official document that shows you have permission to do, own or use something
examples: You need a valid driver's license to rent a car.
The bar lost its liquor license after the incident.

senses.def: to officially give someone permission to do, own or use something
examples: The restaurant is licensed to serve alcohol.
The software is licensed to schools for free.

note: American English uses "license" for both noun and verb. British uses "licence" (noun) and "license" (verb).

senses.def: to be or put yourself in a flat position, for example on a bed
examples: I just want to lie on the couch and watch TV.
He was lying on the beach reading a book.

senses.def: to be in a particular place or state
examples: The town lies at the foot of the mountains.
The problem lies in poor communication.

senses.def: to say something that you know is not true
examples: He lied about his age to get the job.
Don't lie to me — I know what happened.

senses.def: a statement that you know is not true
examples: She told a lie to avoid getting in trouble.

note: Two verbs: lie – lay – lain (be flat) and lie – lied – lied (say false things). -ing form: lying.

senses.def: the state of being alive, or the period between birth and death
examples: The firefighter risked his life to save the children.
She spent her whole life in the same small town.

senses.def: the way a person lives or a particular part of someone's experience
examples: City life can be stressful.
He keeps his private life out of the media.

senses.def: living things in general
examples: Scientists are searching for signs of life on Mars.

note: Plural: lives /laɪvz/. "For life" = for the rest of your life (a life sentence).

senses.def: lasting or existing for the whole of your life
examples: They met in college and became lifelong friends.
His lifelong dream was to sail around the world.

note: Used before a noun only: a lifelong fan.

senses.def: the way a person or group lives, including their habits and the things they own
examples: Doctors recommend a healthier lifestyle with more exercise.
Moving to the countryside changed their whole lifestyle.

senses.def: the length of time that someone lives or something lasts
examples: Technology changed enormously during my grandmother's lifetime.
The battery has a lifetime of about five years.

note: "Once-in-a-lifetime" describes a very rare opportunity.

senses.def: to move something or someone to a higher position
examples: Can you help me lift this box onto the shelf?
She lifted the baby out of the car seat.

senses.def: to remove a rule or restriction
examples: The government lifted the ban on public gatherings.

senses.def: a free ride in someone's car, or (British) an elevator
examples: Can you give me a lift to the airport?
We took the lift to the fifth floor.

note: For the machine, Americans say "elevator"; "lift" is British. Americans also say "ride" more than "lift" for a car trip.

senses.def: the energy from the sun or a lamp that lets you see, or a device that produces it
examples: The room gets a lot of natural light in the morning.
Turn off the lights when you leave.

senses.def: not heavy
examples: This laptop is light enough to carry all day.
I'll just have a light lunch today.

senses.def: pale in color, or bright with natural light
examples: She was wearing a light blue dress.

senses.def: to make something start to burn, or to give light to a place
examples: It took us half an hour to light a fire with the wet wood.
The streets were lit by old gas lamps.

note: Verb past: lit (or lighted). "In light of" = considering. "Shed light on" = help explain.

senses.def: the type or arrangement of lights in a place
examples: The restaurant has soft, warm lighting.
Poor lighting in the parking lot makes people feel unsafe.

note: Don't confuse with "lightning" (şimşek, yıldırım).

senses.def: to find someone or something pleasant or enjoyable
examples: I really like this neighborhood.
Do you like working from home?

senses.def: used with "would" to say politely what you want
examples: I'd like a table for two, please.
Would you like some coffee?

senses.def: similar to someone or something, or in the same way as
examples: She looks just like her mother.
It tastes like chicken.

senses.def: the things that you enjoy, or a click showing approval online
examples: Tell me about your likes and dislikes.
The video got thousands of likes in an hour.

note: "Feel like doing" = want to do (canı istemek). "What is she like?" asks about character, not preferences.

senses.def: the chance of something happening
examples: Regular exercise reduces the likelihood of heart disease.
There's little likelihood that the bill will pass this year.

note: "In all likelihood" = very probably.

senses.def: probably going to happen or be true
examples: It's likely to rain later this afternoon.
The most likely cause of the fire was a faulty wire.

senses.def: probably
examples: She'll most likely be late again.

note: Pattern: "be likely to do": He is likely to win. As an adverb, usually with "most", "very" or "quite".

senses.def: in the same way
examples: She worked hard, and her children did likewise.
Prices rose sharply in March; likewise, rents went up.

senses.def: used in reply to show you feel the same
examples: "Nice to meet you." "Likewise."

note: Formal as a linking word; informal as a short reply.

senses.def: an arm or a leg, or a similar part of an animal such as a wing
examples: The soldier lost a limb in the explosion.
After the long flight, my limbs felt stiff.

senses.def: a large branch of a tree
examples: A heavy limb fell from the oak during the storm.

note: The b is silent: /lɪm/. "Go out on a limb" = say or do something risky that others may not support.

senses.def: the greatest or smallest amount allowed or possible
examples: The speed limit here is 25 miles per hour.
There's a limit to how much I can help you.

senses.def: to stop something from going beyond a certain amount or level
examples: Try to limit your screen time before bed.
The museum limits the number of visitors each day.

note: "Off limits" = not allowed to be entered or used.

senses.def: the act of controlling or limiting something, or a rule that does this
examples: The treaty called for the limitation of nuclear weapons.
There are strict limitations on how the money can be spent.

senses.def: a weakness or limit on what someone or something can do
examples: Every research method has its limitations.
It's important to know your own limitations.

senses.def: not very large in amount or degree
examples: Seating is limited, so book your tickets early.
We only have a limited amount of time.

note: "Limited edition" = only a small number made. In names, "Limited" (Ltd.) is British; Americans use "Inc."

senses.def: a long, thin mark on a surface
examples: Draw a straight line across the page.
The ball was just over the line.

senses.def: a row of people or things waiting one behind the other
examples: We waited in line for an hour to get tickets.
There's always a long line at the post office.

senses.def: a row of words on a page, words spoken by an actor, or a phone connection
examples: She forgot her lines in the middle of the play.
The line went dead before I could answer.

senses.def: to form rows along the side of something, or to cover the inside of something
examples: Thousands of fans lined the streets for the parade.
Line the baking tray with parchment paper.

note: Americans "wait in line"; British people "queue". "Draw the line" = set a limit you won't go beyond.

senses.def: the people or acts taking part in an event, or a team's selected players
examples: The festival announced an impressive line-up of bands this year.
The coach made three changes to the starting line-up.

senses.def: a row of people shown to a witness who must identify a criminal
examples: The witness picked the suspect out of a police line-up.

note: Often written "lineup" in American English. The verb is two words: line up.

senses.def: in lines, or progressing in a straight, step-by-step way from one stage to the next
examples: The movie doesn't follow a linear storyline.
Career paths are much less linear than they used to be.

senses.def: showing a relationship in which one value changes in direct proportion to another
examples: The graph shows a linear relationship between price and demand.

senses.def: to continue to exist for longer than expected
examples: The smell of smoke lingered in the house for days.
Doubts about his honesty still linger.

senses.def: to stay somewhere longer than necessary because you don't want to leave
examples: We lingered over coffee long after the meal was finished.

senses.def: a connection between two or more people, things or ideas
examples: Scientists have found a link between sugar and heart disease.
The two countries have strong trade links.

senses.def: a word or image on a web page that takes you to another page when you click it
examples: Click the link in the email to reset your password.

senses.def: to connect two or more things, physically, electronically or in your mind
examples: The study linked air pollution to asthma in children.
A new bridge will link the island to the mainland.

note: "The weakest link" = the weakest part of a system or team.

senses.def: a large, powerful wild cat with yellow-brown fur that lives in Africa and parts of Asia
examples: We watched a lion hunting zebras on the safari.
The male lion has a thick mane around its neck.

note: "The lion's share" = the largest part of something.

senses.def: either of the two soft edges around the opening of the mouth
examples: She put on red lipstick and pressed her lips together.
My lips get dry and cracked in winter.

senses.def: the edge of a cup, bowl or other container
examples: Coffee spilled over the lip of the mug.

note: "My lips are sealed" = I won't tell the secret. "Lip service" = support in words only.

senses.def: a substance that flows freely, like water or oil, and is not a solid or a gas
examples: You can't take liquids over 3.4 ounces through airport security.
Drink plenty of liquids when you have a fever.

senses.def: in the form of a liquid
examples: Use liquid soap instead of a bar.
The rocket runs on liquid oxygen.

senses.def: easily changed into cash
examples: The company has plenty of liquid assets to cover its debts.

senses.def: a series of names, items or numbers written one below the other
examples: I made a shopping list before going to the store.
Her name was on the list of winners.

senses.def: to write or say things in a particular order, or to include something on a list
examples: Please list your previous jobs on the form.
The hotel is listed as one of the best in the city.

senses.def: to pay attention to someone or something that you can hear
examples: I like to listen to podcasts on my way to work.
Are you even listening to me?

senses.def: to take notice of what someone says and do what they advise
examples: I told him not to buy that car, but he wouldn't listen.

note: Use "to" before the object: listen to music, not "listen music". The t is silent: /ˈlɪsn/.

senses.def: a person who listens, especially to the radio or a podcast
examples: The radio show has more than a million listeners.
She's a good listener, so people often share their problems with her.

senses.def: a published list, or one item in a list, such as a property or product for sale
examples: I found the apartment through an online listing.
Check the TV listings to see what's on tonight.

senses.def: the fact of a company's shares being traded on a stock exchange
examples: The startup is planning a listing on the New York Stock Exchange.

senses.def: a metric unit for measuring liquid, equal to about 2.1 American pints
examples: The car's fuel tank holds 50 liters.
Buy a two-liter bottle of soda for the party.

note: British spelling: litre. In everyday US life, gallons and ounces are more common than liters.

senses.def: the ability to read and write
examples: The program aims to improve literacy among adults.
The country's literacy rate has risen to 95 percent.

senses.def: knowledge and skill in a particular area
examples: Schools are starting to teach financial literacy and media literacy.

senses.def: in the exact, basic meaning of the word
examples: The name of the town literally means "red river".
Don't take everything he says literally.

senses.def: used to emphasize something, even when it is not really true (informal)
examples: I was literally dying of boredom in that meeting.

note: The emphasizing use is very common in speech but annoys some people; avoid it in formal writing.

senses.def: connected with literature or with writing books
examples: The novel won a major literary prize.
She works as a literary agent in New York.

senses.def: typical of the style of language used in literature rather than everyday speech
examples: The word "steed" sounds quite literary today.

note: Don't confuse literary (edebi), literal (gerçek anlamda) and literate (okuryazar).

senses.def: written works such as novels, plays and poems that are valued as art
examples: She majored in English literature in college.
The book is considered a classic of American literature.

senses.def: pieces of writing on a particular subject, or printed information about a product
examples: There is a large body of literature on childhood obesity.
Ask the salesperson for some literature about the car.

note: Uncountable. In academic English, "the literature" means published research on a topic (literature review).

senses.def: small pieces of trash such as paper, cans and bottles left lying in public places
examples: The park was covered in litter after the concert.
You can be fined for dropping litter.

senses.def: a group of baby animals born to one mother at the same time
examples: Our dog had a litter of six puppies.

senses.def: to leave trash somewhere, or to be spread untidily over a place
examples: Clothes littered the floor of his bedroom.

note: "Litter box" = the box of sand indoor cats use (kedi kumu kabı).

senses.def: small in size, or young
examples: They live in a little house near the beach.
My little brother just started kindergarten.

senses.tr: (a little) biraz; (little) çok az, pek az
senses.def: a small amount of; without "a", not much or almost no
examples: Add a little salt to the water.
There's little hope of finding survivors now.

senses.def: a small amount, or not much
examples: I understood very little of what he said.

senses.def: to a small degree, or hardly at all
examples: I'm a little tired after the trip.
Little did she know that her life was about to change.

note: "A little" is positive (some); "little" is negative (almost none). Comparative: less, least.

senses.def: to have your home in a particular place
examples: We live in a small apartment downtown.
Where do your parents live now?

senses.def: to be alive, or to have a particular kind of life
examples: My grandfather lived to the age of 98.
They live a quiet, simple life.

senses.def: alive, or happening or broadcast at the same time as it is seen or heard
examples: The restaurant serves live lobsters.
The band played live music all night.

senses.def: broadcast or performed while the event is actually happening
examples: The final will be shown live on TV.

note: Verb is /lɪv/; adjective and adverb are /laɪv/. "Live on" = use as your money or food: live on $1,000 a month.

senses.def: full of life and energy; active and enthusiastic
examples: The neighborhood has a lively nightlife with lots of bars.
She's a lively, outgoing child.

senses.def: involving a lot of strong opinions and interesting ideas
examples: The panel led to a lively debate about immigration.

note: It looks like an adverb but is an adjective. Pronounced /ˈlaɪvli/.

senses.def: a large organ in the body that cleans the blood, or the liver of an animal eaten as food
examples: Heavy drinking can cause serious liver damage.
She ordered fried liver with onions.

note: Turkish "ciğer" can mean lungs or liver; in English these are different: lung = akciğer, liver = karaciğer.

senses.def: money to buy the things you need, or the way you earn it
examples: What does she do for a living?
It's hard to make a living as an artist.

senses.def: a particular way or standard of life
examples: The cost of living in big cities keeps rising.

senses.def: alive now, or still used or existing
examples: She is one of the greatest living writers.
Bacteria are tiny living organisms.

note: "What do you do for a living?" is the natural way to ask about someone's job.

senses.def: something heavy that is carried, often in large amounts
examples: The truck was carrying a load of bricks.
I do three loads of laundry every weekend.

senses.tr: iş yükü, sorumluluk; (a load of) bir sürü
senses.def: an amount of work or responsibility, or (informal) a lot of something
examples: Teachers have a heavy work load this term.
We've got loads of food left over.

senses.def: to put a large amount of things into a vehicle or container, or to put data into a computer
examples: They loaded the car with camping gear.
The page takes forever to load.

note: "Loaded" (informal) can mean very rich. "A loaded question" contains a hidden trap.

senses.def: money that a bank or person lends and that must be paid back, usually with interest
examples: They took out a loan to buy a new car.
It took me ten years to pay off my student loans.

senses.def: the act of lending something
examples: The painting is on loan from a museum in Paris.

senses.def: to lend something, especially money
examples: My uncle loaned me the money for the down payment.

note: As a verb, "loan" is common in American English; British English prefers "lend".

senses.def: a large area inside the entrance of a hotel or public building
examples: I'll meet you in the hotel lobby at seven.
There's a small café in the lobby of the office building.

senses.def: a group of people who try to influence politicians on a particular issue
examples: The gun lobby is very powerful in Washington.

senses.def: to try to persuade politicians or officials to support or oppose a law
examples: Environmental groups are lobbying Congress to cut emissions.
Parents lobbied for a new playground.

senses.def: belonging to or connected with the area where you live or the place you are talking about
examples: We buy our vegetables at the local farmers' market.
The story was covered by the local news.

senses.def: affecting only one part of the body
examples: The dentist gave me a local anesthetic.

senses.def: a person who lives in a particular place
examples: Ask the locals where the best restaurants are.

note: Trap: "local" doesn't mean "lokal" (restaurant/club) as in Turkish. "The local" in British English = the nearby pub.

senses.def: to find the exact position of someone or something
examples: Rescuers managed to locate the missing hikers.
Police used phone data to locate the suspect.

senses.def: to put or build something in a particular place
examples: The company decided to locate its new factory near the port.

senses.def: existing or situated in a particular place
examples: The hotel is conveniently located near the airport.
Our office is located on the third floor.

note: Used after "be": The museum is located downtown (= Müze şehir merkezinde yer alıyor).

senses.def: a place where something happens or exists, or the position of something
examples: The restaurant is in a great location near the river.
Turn on your phone's location services to use the map.

senses.def: a place outside a studio where a film is made
examples: The movie was shot on location in Morocco.

senses.def: a device that keeps a door, box, etc. closed, usually opened with a key
examples: Someone broke the lock on the back door.
I heard the key turn in the lock.

senses.def: to close something with a lock, or to be able to be closed in this way
examples: Did you remember to lock the car?
The screen locks automatically after five minutes.

note: "Lock yourself out" = accidentally leave your keys inside and be unable to get in.

senses.def: a thick piece of wood cut from a tree or fallen from it
examples: Put another log on the fire.
We sat on a log by the river and ate our sandwiches.

senses.def: an official written record of events, especially on a ship or aircraft
examples: The captain kept a detailed log of the voyage.

senses.def: to officially record information or events
examples: All customer calls are logged for training purposes.
I log my workouts in an app.

note: "Log in/on" = enter a computer system with a password. "Sleep like a log" = sleep very deeply.

senses.def: a reasonable way of thinking about or explaining something
examples: I don't understand the logic behind the new rules.
There's no logic in spending money we don't have.

senses.def: the formal study of reasoning and argument
examples: She took a course in logic and philosophy.

senses.def: seeming natural, reasonable or sensible
examples: It's the logical choice, since she has the most experience.
The logical next step is to test the product with users.

senses.def: following the rules of logic
examples: He laid out his argument in a clear, logical way.

senses.def: a design or symbol that a company or organization uses to identify itself
examples: The company's logo is printed on every product.
They hired a designer to create a new logo.

senses.def: unhappy because you have no friends or nobody to talk to
examples: She felt lonely after moving to a new city.
Many elderly people are lonely and isolated.

senses.def: far from other places and with few people
examples: We drove for hours along a lonely desert road.

note: "Alone" = without others (neutral); "lonely" = sad because you are alone. You can be alone but not lonely.

senses.def: to tell someone about something officially or formally
examples: Passengers will be notified by text message if the flight is delayed.
You must notify the bank immediately if your card is stolen.

note: Pattern: notify someone OF something (not "notify something to someone" in everyday use). More formal than tell.

senses.def: an idea or belief about something, often one that is vague or not fully accepted
examples: She rejected the notion that women are less ambitious than men.
I had no notion of how expensive the repairs would be.

senses.tr: kötü şöhretli, adı çıkmış, dillere düşmüş
senses.def: famous for something bad
examples: The intersection is notorious for traffic accidents.
He was a notorious gang leader in the 1990s.

note: Always negative, unlike famous. Trap: Turkish "meşhur" can be neutral, but notorious is never a compliment.

senses.def: despite something; without being affected by it
examples: Notwithstanding the bad weather, the festival drew a huge crowd.
The project went ahead, budget problems notwithstanding.

senses.def: in spite of what has just been said
examples: The plan has some flaws; notwithstanding, we should give it a try.

note: Very formal, typical of legal and academic writing. It can come before or after the noun.

senses.def: a long written story about imaginary people and events, filling a whole book
examples: She spent three years writing her first novel.
I read a crime novel on the flight home.

senses.def: new and different from anything seen or done before
examples: Researchers have found a novel way to recycle plastic bottles.
The virus was a novel strain that doctors had never seen.

note: Trap: a novel is fiction. A non-fiction book is not a novel.

senses.def: a person who writes novels
examples: The novelist based the story on her childhood in Ohio.
He is best known as a novelist, but he also writes poetry.

senses.def: the eleventh month of the year, after October and before December
examples: Americans celebrate Thanksgiving in late November.
The election will be held on November 5.

note: Months always start with a capital letter in English. Use "in November" but "on November 5".

senses.def: at the present time
examples: I'm busy right now, can I call you back?
She now lives in Chicago with her husband.

senses.def: immediately
examples: If we leave now, we can still catch the train.

senses.def: because something has happened or is now true
examples: Now that the kids are in college, the house feels very quiet.

note: "Now that" means "because now". "For now" means "for the time being" (şimdilik).

senses.def: at the present time, compared with the past
examples: Nowadays most people pay with their phones instead of cash.
Kids nowadays spend hours a day on screens.

note: Used to contrast the present with the past. Do not use it for a single moment: say "now", not "nowadays I'm busy".

senses.def: not in any place or to any place
examples: The keys were nowhere to be found.
We had nowhere to stay, so we slept in the car.

senses.def: used to say that there is no progress or success
examples: The negotiations are going nowhere.

note: "Out of nowhere" = suddenly. "Nowhere near" = not at all, far from ("nowhere near enough").

senses.def: using or connected with the energy released when atoms are split or joined
examples: The country gets about a fifth of its electricity from nuclear power.
World leaders met to discuss reducing nuclear weapons.

senses.def: connected with the nucleus of a cell or an atom
examples: The study looked at changes in nuclear DNA.

note: "Nuclear family" = parents and their children only (çekirdek aile).

senses.def: a word or symbol that shows an amount, or a set of digits used to identify something
examples: Can I have your phone number?
Pick a number between one and ten.

senses.def: an amount or quantity of people or things
examples: A large number of students failed the test.
The number of cyclists in the city has doubled.

senses.def: to give each thing in a series a number
examples: Please number the pages before you print the report.

note: "A number of" takes a plural verb (A number of people are...), but "the number of" takes a singular verb (The number is...).

senses.def: existing in large numbers; many
examples: The senator has appeared on numerous TV shows.
We tried numerous times to contact the landlord.

note: More formal than many. Use it with plural countable nouns only.

senses.def: a person trained to care for sick or injured people, usually in a hospital
examples: The nurse checked my blood pressure before the doctor came in.
She has worked as a nurse in the emergency room for ten years.

senses.def: to care for someone who is sick or injured
examples: He nursed his wife through a long illness.

senses.def: a place where young children are looked after while their parents are at work
examples: She drops her son off at the nursery before work.
The company runs a nursery for employees' children.

senses.def: a place where young plants and trees are grown for sale
examples: We bought two apple trees at the local plant nursery.

senses.def: a room in a house where a baby sleeps
examples: They painted the nursery yellow before the baby arrived.

note: In American English, daycare or preschool is more common than nursery for childcare. "Nursery rhyme" = çocuk tekerlemesi.

senses.def: the job or skill of caring for sick or injured people
examples: She is studying nursing at a state university.
There is a shortage of nursing staff in rural hospitals.

note: "Nursing home" = a place where old people live and get care (huzurevi, bakımevi).

senses.def: a dry fruit with a hard shell that grows on some trees
examples: He snacks on nuts and fruit instead of chips.
This cake may contain nuts, so be careful if you're allergic.

senses.def: a small metal piece with a hole in it that screws onto a bolt
examples: Tighten the nuts on the wheel before you drive.

senses.def: a person who is very enthusiastic about something, or who is a little crazy
examples: My uncle is a real fitness nut who runs every morning.

note: Informal: "go nuts" = get very excited or angry; "the nuts and bolts" = the basic practical details.

senses.def: the process of getting the food needed for health and growth, or the study of this
examples: Good nutrition is essential for children's development.
Check the nutrition label for sugar and salt.

note: Nutritious food is healthy food; nutritional describes things related to nutrition (nutritional value).

senses.def: used after the numbers one to twelve to say an exact hour
examples: The meeting starts at ten o'clock sharp.
I woke up at six o'clock this morning.

note: Only for exact hours: say "three o'clock" but not "three thirty o'clock" or "15 o'clock".

senses.def: the condition of being so overweight that it is dangerous to health
examples: Childhood obesity has risen sharply over the past thirty years.
Obesity increases the risk of heart disease and diabetes.

senses.def: to do what a person, law or rule tells you to do
examples: Soldiers are trained to obey orders without question.
Drivers must obey the speed limit near schools.

note: Transitive: obey the law, not "obey to the law" (a common trap from Turkish "-e uymak").

senses.def: a thing that you can see and touch but that is not alive
examples: The museum displays everyday objects from ancient Rome.
Police found a sharp object in his bag.

senses.def: the purpose or aim of an activity
examples: The object of the game is to collect as many points as possible.

senses.def: to say that you disagree with or do not like something
examples: Many residents objected to the new parking rules.
I object to being treated like a child.

note: Stress shift: noun OBject /ˈɑːbdʒɪkt/, verb obJECT /əbˈdʒekt/. Verb pattern: object to + noun/-ing.

senses.def: a reason why you disagree with or oppose something, or a statement of this
examples: Does anyone have any objection to moving the meeting to Friday?
The plan went ahead despite strong objections from local residents.

senses.def: something you are trying to achieve
examples: Our main objective this year is to reduce costs.
The course has clear learning objectives.

senses.def: based on facts rather than personal feelings or opinions
examples: It's hard to be objective when your own child is involved.
We need objective evidence, not just opinions.

note: Opposite of the adjective: subjective.

senses.def: something you must do because of a law, a promise or a duty
examples: Employers have a legal obligation to provide a safe workplace.
You are under no obligation to buy anything.

note: "No obligation" in ads means you don't have to buy or commit ("a free, no-obligation quote").

senses.def: to force someone to do something because of a law, rule or duty
examples: The law obliges companies to publish their annual accounts.
I felt obliged to invite her, since she had invited me.

senses.def: to help someone by doing what they ask
examples: When the reporters asked for a photo, the singer happily obliged.

note: Usually passive: be/feel obliged to do something. "Much obliged" is an old-fashioned way to say thank you.

senses.def: the act of watching something carefully over time to learn about it
examples: The patient was kept in the hospital overnight for observation.
Her findings are based on years of careful observation.

senses.def: a comment based on something you have noticed
examples: He made an interesting observation about the way people use their phones.

senses.def: to see or notice something, or to watch it carefully
examples: Scientists observed the birds' behavior for six months.
Witnesses observed a man leaving the building at midnight.

senses.def: to obey a rule or law, or to follow a custom
examples: All visitors must observe the safety regulations.
Many families observe the holiday with a special meal.

senses.def: to make a remark about something you have noticed
examples: "It's getting late," she observed.

senses.def: a person who watches or notices something, or whose job is to watch an event and report on it
examples: International observers said the election was free and fair.
To a casual observer, the two paintings look identical.

senses.def: to fill someone's mind completely, or to think and worry about something all the time
examples: Stop obsessing about your weight; you look great.
She is obsessed with true crime podcasts.

note: Most common as "be obsessed with". Active use: obsess about/over something.

senses.def: a state in which one thing or person fills your mind all the time, in a way that is not normal
examples: His obsession with video games was hurting his grades.
Cleanliness has become an obsession for her.

senses.def: something that blocks your way or makes it hard to achieve something
examples: Lack of money is the biggest obstacle to starting a business.
The runners had to jump over several obstacles.

note: Pattern: an obstacle TO something (an obstacle to peace).

senses.def: to get something, especially through effort or an official process
examples: You need to obtain a visa before you travel.
The journalist obtained a copy of the secret report.

note: Formal. In everyday speech, people usually say get.

senses.def: easy to see, notice or understand
examples: It was obvious that she had been crying.
For obvious reasons, we can't discuss the case in public.

note: "State the obvious" = say something everyone already knows.

senses.def: used to say that something is easy to see or understand, or that people should already know it
examples: Obviously, we can't afford a new car right now.
He was obviously upset when he heard the news.

senses.def: a particular time when something happens
examples: I've met him on several occasions.
On one occasion, the train was three hours late.

senses.def: a special event or celebration
examples: She saves her best dress for special occasions.
The wedding was a joyful occasion for the whole family.

note: Spelling: two c's, one s. "Rise to the occasion" = deal successfully with a difficult situation.

senses.def: happening sometimes, but not often or regularly
examples: I don't smoke, apart from the occasional cigar at weddings.
The forecast is for sun with occasional showers.

senses.tr: ara sıra, arada bir, zaman zaman
senses.def: sometimes, but not often
examples: We occasionally eat out, but usually we cook at home.
Occasionally, the system crashes and we lose our work.

senses.def: a job or profession
examples: Please write your name, age and occupation on the form.
Nursing is one of the fastest-growing occupations.

senses.def: the act of an army taking control of a country or area
examples: The city was under military occupation for five years.

note: "Occupation" is formal and used on forms; in conversation, ask "What do you do?"

senses.def: to fill or use a space, area or period of time
examples: The bookshelves occupy an entire wall of the living room.
Is this seat occupied?

senses.def: to keep someone busy
examples: I brought some games to keep the kids occupied on the trip.

senses.def: to take control of a place by military force or as a protest
examples: Protesters occupied the university building for three days.

senses.def: to happen, especially without being planned
examples: The accident occurred on the highway just after midnight.
Most of these errors occur when users are tired.

senses.def: to come into your mind
examples: It never occurred to me that he might be lying.

senses.def: to exist or be found somewhere
examples: This mineral occurs naturally in volcanic rock.

note: Doubles the r: occurred, occurring, occurrence. "It occurred to me" = I suddenly thought of it.

senses.def: something that happens
examples: Power cuts are a common occurrence in this part of the city.
Car thefts are a rare occurrence in our neighborhood.

senses.def: the fact of something happening or existing, or how often it does
examples: Doctors are studying the occurrence of the disease in young adults.

note: Spelling: double c, double r: occurrence.

senses.def: the mass of salt water that covers most of the earth, or one of its large areas
examples: They rented a house with a view of the Pacific Ocean.
Plastic waste is a growing threat to ocean life.

note: Americans often say "the ocean" where British people say "the sea" (go swimming in the ocean).

senses.def: the tenth month of the year, after September and before November
examples: Halloween is celebrated on October 31.
The leaves start changing color in early October.

note: Months always start with a capital letter in English.

senses.def: strange or unusual
examples: It's odd that she hasn't called; she usually calls every day.
There was an odd smell coming from the fridge.

senses.def: (of a number) that cannot be divided exactly by two
examples: 1, 3, 5 and 7 are odd numbers.

senses.tr: ara sıra olan, çeşitli; teki kayıp
senses.def: happening sometimes but not regularly, or not part of a matching pair
examples: He does odd jobs around the neighborhood for extra money.
I have a drawer full of odd socks.

note: "The odd one out" = the one that is different from the rest. Opposite of odd number: even number.

senses.def: how likely it is that something will happen
examples: The odds of winning the lottery are about one in 300 million.
The odds are that prices will keep rising.

senses.def: difficulties that make success seem unlikely
examples: Against all odds, the small team won the championship.

note: Always plural. "Be at odds with" = disagree or not match (görüş ayrılığı içinde olmak).

senses.def: belonging to or connected with someone or something
examples: The roof of the house was damaged in the storm.
She is a friend of my sister.

senses.def: used to show an amount, a part or what something contains
examples: Could I have a glass of water, please?
Some of the students missed the bus.

senses.def: about or concerning
examples: Have you heard of this band?
I'm afraid of spiders.

note: In fast speech it often sounds like /ə/ ("kinda", "lotta"). Never write "could of"; the correct form is "could have".

senses.def: removed or separated, or no longer working or switched on
examples: Please turn off the lights when you leave.
Take your shoes off before you come in.

senses.def: away from a place, or not at work
examples: I'm off tomorrow, so let's meet for lunch.
She waved and drove off.

senses.def: down from or away from a surface or place
examples: The cat knocked the glass off the table.
Keep off the grass.

note: Trap: don't say "off of" in formal writing; "off the table" is enough. Also "20% off" = indirimli.

senses.def: to upset or insult someone by being rude or thoughtless
examples: I didn't mean to offend you; it was only a joke.
Many viewers were offended by the ad.

senses.def: to commit a crime
examples: Young people who offend are often victims themselves.

senses.def: a person who has committed a crime
examples: The program helps young offenders find jobs after prison.
First-time offenders usually receive a lighter sentence.

senses.def: a person or thing that does something wrong or causes a problem
examples: When it comes to air pollution, coal plants are the worst offenders.

senses.def: an illegal act; a crime
examples: Driving without a license is a serious offense.
He was arrested for a minor drug offense.

senses.def: the feeling of being upset or insulted by something someone says or does
examples: No offense, but I think your plan won't work.
She took offense at his comment about her accent.

senses.def: the players in a team whose job is to score points
examples: The team's offense scored 35 points in the first half.

note: American spelling is offense; British is offence. In US sports, offense (attack) is the opposite of defense, stressed on the first syllable.

senses.def: rude or insulting in a way that upsets people
examples: The comedian apologized for his offensive jokes.
Many people find that word deeply offensive.

senses.def: a large military attack, or a strong organized effort to achieve something
examples: The army launched a major offensive in the north.
The company began a marketing offensive to win back customers.

note: "Go on the offensive" = start attacking or criticizing instead of defending yourself.

senses.def: to say you are willing to give something to someone or to do something for them
examples: He offered me a ride to the airport.
The hotel offers free breakfast to all guests.

senses.def: a statement that you are willing to do or give something
examples: She accepted a job offer from a tech company in Austin.
Thanks for the offer, but I can manage.

senses.def: a reduced price for a product for a short time
examples: This special offer ends on Sunday.

note: Pattern: offer someone something / offer to do something. Not "offer someone to do something".

senses.def: something that is produced or made available for people to buy, use, watch or enjoy
examples: The band's latest offering is their best album yet.
The restaurant's vegetarian offerings are limited.

senses.def: something given as a gift, especially to God or a church
examples: Villagers left offerings of fruit and flowers at the temple.

note: In finance, an "initial public offering" (IPO) is when a company first sells shares to the public (halka arz).

senses.def: a room or building where people work, usually at desks
examples: I usually get to the office around 8:30.
The company is moving to a new office downtown.

senses.def: an important official position, especially in government
examples: The president has been in office for two years.
She plans to run for office next year.

note: In American English, a doctor's or dentist's place of work is an office (British: surgery).

senses.def: a person in a position of authority in the army, navy or air force
examples: Her father was an officer in the Navy.
The officers gave orders to the soldiers.

senses.def: a police officer
examples: Excuse me, officer, can you tell me where the station is?
Two officers arrived at the scene within minutes.

senses.def: a person with an important position in an organization
examples: She was promoted to chief financial officer last year.

senses.def: approved or done by people in authority, or connected with a position of authority
examples: The official results will be announced tomorrow.
English is the official language of the conference.

senses.def: a person with authority in a government or large organization
examples: Government officials refused to comment on the report.
A city official said the road would reopen on Monday.

note: Officials (yetkililer) are usually government or organization staff; officers are usually in the army or police.

senses.def: to balance the effect of something with something opposite, so that the situation stays the same
examples: Higher fuel prices were offset by lower food costs.
Many travelers pay to offset the carbon emissions from their flights.

senses.def: something that balances or cancels out the effect of something else
examples: The tax cut serves as an offset to rising living costs.

note: Irregular: offset – offset – offset. Often passive: be offset by something.

senses.def: a person's child or children, or an animal's young
examples: Some birds feed their offspring for weeks after they hatch.
Parents naturally want the best for their offspring.

note: Plural is also offspring. Formal or humorous when used about people.

senses.def: many times, or in many cases
examples: How often do you go to the gym?
Teenagers often sleep late on weekends.

note: The t is usually silent: /ˈɔːfn/. "Every so often" = sometimes, not frequently.

senses.def: used to react to something, especially news you did not know, or to show surprise, disappointment or pain
examples: "I got the job!" "Oh, that's wonderful!"
Oh no, I left my wallet at home.

senses.def: used before a short pause, or when adding a comment
examples: Oh, by the way, your mom called.

note: "Oh well" shows you accept a disappointing situation (neyse, napalım).

senses.def: a thick dark liquid found underground, used to make fuel and other products
examples: Oil prices rose sharply after the attack.
The country's economy depends heavily on oil exports.

senses.def: a smooth liquid from plants or animals, used in cooking or for other purposes
examples: Heat a little olive oil in a pan.
I need to change the oil in my car.

senses.def: used to agree to something or to say yes
examples: "Can you pick me up at six?" "OK, no problem."
OK, let's get started.

senses.tr: iyi, sağ salim; idare eder, fena değil
senses.def: safe and well, or acceptable but not especially good
examples: Are you OK? You look pale.
The food was OK, but nothing special.

senses.def: in a satisfactory way
examples: Is your new laptop working OK?

note: Informal. Also spelled okay. "Is it OK if...?" is a common way to ask for permission.

senses.def: having lived for a long time
examples: My grandfather is getting old, but he still walks every day.
She takes care of old people in her neighborhood.

senses.def: of a particular age
examples: How old is your daughter?
Our house is about a hundred years old.

senses.def: having existed or been used for a long time, or from an earlier time
examples: I ran into an old friend from high school.
We sold our old car and bought an electric one.

note: "An old friend" usually means a friend you have known a long time, not an elderly friend. Elder/eldest are used only for family members.

senses.def: not modern; typical of the past and no longer common or fashionable
examples: My parents still have an old-fashioned phone with a cord.
He has some old-fashioned ideas about women working.

senses.def: traditional, in a way that people like
examples: The bakery sells good, old-fashioned apple pie.

note: Opposite: modern, up to date. "Good old-fashioned" is positive.

senses.def: touching or supported by a surface
examples: Your keys are on the kitchen table.
There's a spider on the wall.

senses.def: used with days and dates, topics, and means of communication
examples: We're meeting on Friday.
She wrote a book on climate change.

senses.def: working or switched on, being worn, or continuing
examples: Is the oven on?
Put your coat on; it's cold outside.

note: Use on for days and dates (on Monday, on May 3), in for months and years, at for clock times.

senses.def: one time only
examples: I've only been to New York once.
We meet once a month to discuss the project.

senses.def: at some time in the past
examples: This building was once a factory.

senses.def: as soon as; after
examples: Once you've finished your homework, you can watch TV.
It's easy once you know how.

note: "At once" = immediately or at the same time. "Once and for all" = finally and completely (ilk ve son kez).

senses.def: the number 1
examples: I have one brother and two sisters.
Only one of the candidates passed the test.

senses.def: used to mean a particular person, thing or time that is not named
examples: One day I'd like to live by the ocean.

senses.def: used instead of repeating a noun that has already been mentioned
examples: I don't like the red shirt; I prefer the blue one.
Which one do you want?

note: "The blue one / the old ones": English needs one(s) here, while Turkish just says "maviyi".

senses.def: continuing to exist or develop; not finished
examples: Police say the investigation is ongoing.
Training is an ongoing process, not a one-time event.

note: Common in news and business English.

senses.def: a round vegetable with many layers and a strong smell and taste
examples: Chop the onion and fry it until it's golden.
Cutting onions always makes me cry.

note: In American English, green onions are what British people call spring onions (taze soğan).

senses.def: available on or done using the internet
examples: She runs an online store that sells handmade jewelry.
Online classes became common during the pandemic.

senses.def: using the internet, or onto the internet
examples: I bought my plane tickets online.
He spends hours online every evening.

note: Opposite: offline. "Come online" can also mean that a new system starts working.

senses.def: no one or nothing except; no more than
examples: The store only accepts cash.
It only takes ten minutes to get there by bike.

senses.def: used to say that there is no other person or thing of the same kind
examples: She was the only person who noticed the mistake.
I'm an only child, so I have no brothers or sisters.

senses.def: (informal) except that; but
examples: I'd love to come, only I have to work late.

note: Position matters: "Only I saw her" vs "I only saw her" vs "I saw only her" have different meanings. "If only" expresses a wish (keşke).

senses.def: used to show movement to a position on a surface
examples: The cat jumped onto the kitchen counter.
Pour the sauce onto the pasta.

senses.def: (informal) aware of what someone is doing, especially something wrong
examples: The police are onto him, so he'd better be careful.

note: Onto shows movement (jump onto the bed); on shows position (sit on the bed). "Be onto something" = have found something important.

senses.def: not closed, so that people or things can go through, or ready for business
examples: Someone left the window open all night.
Is the pharmacy open on Sundays?

senses.def: honest and willing to talk, or willing to consider new ideas
examples: She's very open about her struggles with anxiety.
I'm open to suggestions.

senses.def: to move something so it is no longer closed, or to start operating
examples: Can you open the door for me?
The new library opens next month.

senses.def: a space or hole that something can pass through
examples: The dog escaped through an opening in the fence.

senses.def: the beginning of something, or a ceremony to start a new building, business or event
examples: Hundreds of people came to the opening of the new museum.
The movie's opening was a little slow.

senses.def: a job that is available, or a good opportunity
examples: There are several openings for nurses at the clinic.

senses.def: without hiding your feelings, opinions or information
examples: He spoke openly about his divorce in the interview.
Few employees dared to openly criticize the boss.

senses.def: a drama in which most or all of the words are sung to music, or this kind of art
examples: We saw a wonderful opera at the Met last night.
She trained as an opera singer in Italy.

note: "Soap opera" = a TV drama series about the daily lives of characters (dizi, pembe dizi).

senses.def: to work or function in a particular way, or to do business
examples: The company operates in more than 40 countries.
Most smartphones operate on rechargeable batteries.

senses.def: to use and control a machine
examples: You need special training to operate a crane.

senses.def: to cut open someone's body in order to repair or remove a damaged part
examples: Surgeons operated on her knee last week.

note: For surgery, use operate ON someone.

senses.def: medical treatment in which a doctor cuts open the body to remove or repair a part
examples: He had an operation on his back last year.
The operation took four hours.

senses.def: an organized activity involving many people, especially soldiers or police
examples: The rescue operation continued through the night.

senses.def: the way something works, or the fact of being active
examples: The new factory will be in operation by next spring.

note: American speakers often say surgery rather than "an operation": "He had knee surgery."

senses.def: connected with the way a business, machine or system works
examples: The company is cutting operational costs to save money.
We faced several operational problems in the first year.

senses.def: working and ready to be used
examples: The new airport terminal will be fully operational by June.

senses.def: a person who works a machine or piece of equipment
examples: The crane operator lifted the steel beams into place.

senses.def: a company that runs a particular business or service
examples: The tour operator canceled our trip because of the storm.
Mobile phone operators are raising their prices.

senses.def: a person who works at a telephone exchange and connects calls
examples: I called the operator to ask for the number.

senses.def: what you think or feel about something, rather than a fact
examples: In my opinion, the movie was too long.
Public opinion has turned against the war.

note: Say "in my opinion", not "according to me". "A second opinion" is advice from another expert, especially a doctor.

senses.def: a person you play, compete or fight against
examples: She beat her opponent in straight sets.
The senator attacked his opponent's record on taxes.

senses.def: a person who disagrees with an idea or plan and tries to stop it
examples: Opponents of the new law say it will hurt small businesses.

senses.def: a time or situation in which it is possible to do something you want
examples: Studying abroad was a great opportunity to learn Spanish.
I'd like to take this opportunity to thank my team.

note: Pattern: an opportunity to do something / for something / of doing something.

senses.def: to disagree strongly with a plan, policy or idea and try to stop it
examples: Many parents oppose the plan to close the school.
The bill was opposed by both parties.

note: Transitive: oppose something (not "oppose to something"). Compare: be opposed to something.

senses.def: strongly disagreeing with something
examples: Most residents are opposed to the new highway.
I'm not opposed to the idea, but we need more details.

note: "Be opposed to" + noun/-ing. "As opposed to" = rather than, in contrast with ("-in aksine").

senses.def: completely different, or on the other side or in the other direction
examples: The two brothers have opposite personalities.
The bus was going in the opposite direction.

senses.def: a person or thing that is as different as possible from another
examples: "Hot" is the opposite of "cold."
I thought he'd be shy, but he was the exact opposite.

senses.def: on the other side of an area from someone or something, facing them
examples: The bank is opposite the post office.

senses.def: on the other side, facing
examples: She sat down opposite and smiled at me.

note: As a preposition, Americans often prefer "across from" (the bank is across from the post office).

senses.def: strong disagreement with something, usually with the aim of stopping it
examples: There was strong opposition to the new tax.
The plan met with fierce opposition from environmental groups.

senses.def: the main political parties not in government, or the people you are competing against
examples: The opposition accused the government of hiding the truth.

senses.def: to choose one thing or course of action instead of another
examples: Many students opt for online classes because they're cheaper.
She opted to take the train instead of flying.

note: "Opt out" = choose not to take part (e.g., opt out of emails); "opt in" = choose to take part.

senses.def: connected with sight or with light and how it is used to see
examples: The lines look curved, but it's just an optical illusion.
The lab makes optical instruments such as microscopes.

note: "Optical illusion" = göz yanılması.

senses.def: a feeling that good things will happen and things will be successful
examples: There is growing optimism that the economy will recover.
She faced her illness with remarkable optimism.

note: Opposite: pessimism.

senses.def: expecting good things to happen or something to be successful
examples: Doctors are optimistic that she will make a full recovery.
I'm optimistic about our chances in the final.

note: Opposite: pessimistic. Pattern: optimistic about something / optimistic that...

senses.def: something you can choose, or the freedom to choose
examples: We have two options: take the bus or walk.
Selling the house is not an option for us.

note: "Have no option but to" = be forced to (başka çaresi olmamak).

senses.def: used to connect possibilities or alternatives
examples: Would you like coffee or tea?
You can pay by card or in cash.

senses.def: used to say what will happen if something is not done
examples: Hurry up, or we'll miss the bus.

senses.def: used after a negative to mean "and not"
examples: He doesn't smoke or drink.

note: "Or so" = approximately (an hour or so). In negatives, English uses or, not nor: "I don't eat meat or fish."

senses.def: spoken rather than written
examples: We have an oral exam in French next week.
The story was passed down through oral tradition.

senses.def: connected with the mouth, or taken by mouth
examples: Good oral hygiene helps prevent gum disease.

note: Opposite of the first meaning: written.

senses.def: a round, juicy citrus fruit with a thick skin
examples: I squeeze fresh oranges for juice every morning.
She peeled an orange and shared it with her son.

senses.def: having a color between red and yellow
examples: The workers wore bright orange vests.

senses.def: the color between red and yellow
examples: The sky turned a deep orange at sunset.

note: One word, two Turkish translations: portakal (the fruit) and turuncu (the color).

senses.def: a large group of musicians who play different instruments together, led by a conductor
examples: She plays the violin in the city's symphony orchestra.
The orchestra performed a program of Mozart and Beethoven.

note: In US theaters, "the orchestra" also means the seats on the main floor (British: the stalls).

senses.def: the way things are arranged in relation to each other, or a state of being neat and organized
examples: The names are listed in alphabetical order.
The police were called to restore order.

senses.def: an instruction from someone in authority, or a request for goods or food
examples: The soldiers were given orders to retreat.
Your order will arrive within three days.

senses.def: to ask for food, drinks or goods to be brought or sent to you
examples: Are you ready to order, or do you need a few more minutes?

senses.def: to tell someone to do something, using your authority
examples: The judge ordered the company to pay damages.

note: "In order to" = so that you can (-mek için). "Out of order" = not working (bozuk).

senses.def: normal or usual; not special or different in any way
examples: It was just an ordinary Tuesday until the phone rang.
Ordinary people can't afford to live in this neighborhood.

note: "Out of the ordinary" = unusual (alışılmışın dışında).

senses.def: a part of the body or a plant that has a particular job, such as the heart or a leaf
examples: The skin is the largest organ of the human body.
Thousands of patients are waiting for an organ transplant.

senses.def: a large musical instrument with pipes and keys, often found in churches
examples: She played the organ at her sister's wedding.

senses.def: grown or produced without artificial chemicals
examples: Organic vegetables usually cost more at the supermarket.
They run a small organic farm in Vermont.

senses.def: produced by or coming from living things
examples: Compost is made from organic waste like food scraps and leaves.

senses.def: developing naturally and gradually
examples: The company's growth has been slow and organic.

senses.def: a group of people who work together for a particular purpose, such as a business or charity
examples: She works for a nonprofit organization that helps refugees.
The World Health Organization issued a new warning.

senses.def: the act of planning or arranging something, or the way it is arranged
examples: The organization of the conference took months.
His essay is full of good ideas but lacks organization.

note: American spelling with z; British also uses organisation. Trap: an event is not usually called "an organization" in English; say event.

senses.def: connected with an organization or the way it is run
examples: The company went through major organizational changes last year.
Organizational culture affects how happy employees are.

senses.def: connected with planning and arranging things
examples: She has excellent organizational skills.

senses.def: to plan and arrange an event or activity
examples: We're organizing a surprise party for Dad's birthday.
Students organized a protest against the tuition increase.

senses.def: to arrange things in a sensible order or system
examples: I spent Sunday organizing my closet.

senses.def: to form a group such as a labor union
examples: Workers at the warehouse are trying to organize.

senses.def: planned and carried out by a large group of people working together
examples: Police believe the thefts are the work of organized crime.
He isn't a fan of organized religion.

senses.def: able to plan your work and life well, or arranged in a clear way
examples: She's very organized and never misses a deadline.
The report is well organized and easy to follow.

note: Opposite: disorganized. "Get organized" = start planning things properly.

senses.def: a person who plans and arranges an event or activity
examples: The organizers expect 10,000 people at the festival.
She works as a community organizer in Detroit.

senses.def: a container or diary used to keep things in order
examples: I bought a desk organizer for my pens and cables.

senses.def: to aim something at a particular group or purpose
examples: The program is oriented toward first-generation college students.
We need to orient our marketing more to younger customers.

senses.def: to find your position or get used to a new situation
examples: It took me a few days to orient myself in the new city.
He used the mountains to orient himself.

note: Very common in compound adjectives: goal-oriented, family-oriented. British English often uses orientate.

senses.def: a person's basic beliefs, attitudes or interests
examples: It is illegal to discriminate based on sexual orientation.
The party has a strong left-wing orientation.

senses.def: training or information given to people who are new to a place or job
examples: All new employees attend a two-day orientation.
Freshman orientation starts the week before classes.

senses.def: the direction in which something faces
examples: The orientation of the house gives it lots of morning sun.

senses.def: the point where something begins, or the cause of something
examples: Scientists are still debating the origin of the virus.
Many English words have Latin origins.

senses.def: the country, race or social class that a person comes from
examples: She is of Mexican origin.
People of all origins live in this neighborhood.

senses.def: existing at the beginning, before any changes
examples: The original plan was to drive, but we flew instead.
The house still has its original windows.

senses.def: new and interesting, not copied from something else
examples: It's a highly original novel with a surprising ending.

senses.def: the first version of a document or work of art, from which copies are made
examples: Keep the original and send them a photocopy.
The painting in the hall is a copy; the original is in Paris.

senses.def: at the beginning, before something changed
examples: The building was originally a train station.
I'm originally from Ohio, but I live in Texas now.

senses.def: in a new and creative way
examples: The room was decorated very originally.

note: "Where are you originally from?" asks where someone was born or grew up.

senses.def: to start or come from a particular place, time or situation
examples: The tradition originated in Germany in the 16th century.
The fire originated in the kitchen.

senses.def: to create or start something new
examples: Who originated the idea of a four-day workweek?

senses.def: additional, different, or the remaining one(s) of a group
examples: Do you have this shirt in any other colors?
The other students had already left.

senses.def: the remaining or a different person or thing
examples: Some people like summer; others prefer winter.
One twin is shy, but the other is very outgoing.

note: "The other day" = a few days ago. "Every other day" = every second day (gün aşırı). "Other than" = except.

senses.def: used to say what will happen if something is not done or the situation is different
